chapters.title: Chapter 1851: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (1)
paragraphs: CRAAAASSSH! BOOM! BOOOOOOM!
Mountains collapsed, and trees were reduced to mere shrapnel. All around, devastation marred the ground and scarred the space around.
The air was filled with thick sword intent, the kind many swordsmen wish they could attain in their lifetime.
Just standing within this intent would make one feel their sword tingle, and everything they knew about swords would be tested.

This place is the infamous Amon’s Guillotine Cave, one of the seven Calamity Zones in the Infinity Universe. It is a place where only swordsmen could live since, aside from sword intent and sword aura, nothing else works there.
No matter how much spiritual qi or any other qi one possesses, once they get to Amon’s Guillotine Cave, only their sword intent would work.
It was one of the reasons why even Celestials dreaded coming here.
Right now, Inaya, Baldy, and Mak were surrounded on all sides by a pack of wolves, each standing approximately 20 meters tall, every last one boasting the strength of a Celestial.

Returning to Amon’s Guillotine Cave after several years had passed made Inaya a bit elated. However, now that she was surrounded on all sides, she couldn’t help but smile, recalling some of the dreadful battles she had fought in the past.
"This is a bit troublesome," she said, taking a deep breath. They had already killed close to a dozen wolves, but they still had over 30 to kill.
More importantly, the Alpha had yet to appear, so they had to be on high alert for its arrival as well.
"You know, I have been away from the world of battles for so long I forgot how enjoyable they can be," Mak said with a laugh, scanning the deadly wolves baring their fangs at them.
As one of the seven Eternal Sword Intents Lord Genesis had refined before he died, he possessed a completely different personality, just like how Baldy and Han also had their own ways of life.
Baldy liked to eat candy and sleep, while Han preferred living among mortals as a way to train his Eternal Karmic Sword Domain.

As for Mak, he was fond of women, so he spent most of his days in brothels. One would wonder why someone who was supposed to forge a sword path and master it to its peak would spend his days around women.
The answer is quite simple.
Just like how Han’s domain could influence the laws, rendering any space into a mortal plain, Mak could also do the same, but his domain was rather unique.
"Big Brother, why don’t you show me what your domain looks like?" Baldy said, summoning a sword that was three times taller than his body.
Mak smiled and nodded. "My lady, kindly step back and let me handle these bugs."
Inaya had no reason to doubt him. She had seen firsthand what Baldy and this pink-haired brother of his were capable of during their journey within Amon’s Guillotine Cave.
Mak took a deep breath and advanced forward.
The wolves lunged at him.
However, they could only get so far before they were all shrouded in a pink mist.
Their steps halted, and for a split second, the space around them became filled with lust.
Inaya and Baldy furrowed their brows at the sensation. However hard they looked at it, the moment the domain appeared, everyone felt their hearts skip a beat.
But the worst came when the advancing wolves suddenly started whimpering.
Then the first wolf did the impossible.

Instead of attacking Mak, it turned its claws on another wolf, landing a devastating attack on its hide. The attack was so brutal that one half of the wolf’s body was torn off, and it crashed into a mountain 2 km away, shattering it into chunks of stone.
The attacker didn’t let it rest. Instead, it moved at a terrifying speed, crashing into it again.
Inaya, who cultivated the Ten Emotions, sensed a wave of hatred emanating from the attacker, causing her to frown slightly as she wondered where the sudden aggression was coming from.
The rest also started attacking, each radiating intense hatred... well, some were radiating intense hatred and aggression, while others were radiating intense lust.
"Big Brother, what kind of domain is this?" Baldy asked, confused. Unlike how he was able to figure out Han’s domain, Mak’s was just too complex for his childish mind to comprehend...
Inaya, on the other hand, seemed to have grasped a bit of the nature of the domain. But she would have to hear from Mak before she could be certain about her deduction.

Mak smiled and brushed Baldy’s clean head. "You will know one day. For now, all you need to know is that they will kill each other, and no matter what anyone does, as long as I remain standing, none of them can break free."
Baldy nodded, not too bothered. Though it would be good to understand the insidious nature of the domain his big brother had cultivated since the Divine Era.
Inaya sighed but said nothing, despite wanting to know.
She sensed lust and hatred. Aside from that, she had also deduced that Mak walked the path of an incubus—well, he was an incubus, so it was only natural.
He cultivated the Dao of Desire.

But his Sword Domain concerned illusions and lust. If she had to guess, the wolves had been subjected to an illusion where some were experiencing lust while others were thrust into a state of extreme anger and hatred.

She had no idea how any of that was possible, but she knew for a fact that the ones attacking were mentally unstable at the moment, resulting in an intense battle with those who seemed happy with whatever they were seeing in the illusion.
"ROARRRRRR!"
Suddenly, a roar came from the distance, shaking the ground, trees, and the very air around them.
"It is here," Baldy said, flying into the air.
Far in the distance, a pair of red wolf eyes lit up, causing intense killing intent mixed with sword intent to spread across the space.
"It is strong," Inaya commented.
She could sense the Alpha wasn’t weak at all. But she wasn’t scared, not when Baldy had already volunteered to handle it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1852: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (2)
paragraphs: "Be careful, Baldy," Inaya said, watching as Baldy flew into the distance, choosing to take the fight to the Alpha Wolf.
Mak smirked, seeing that Baldy wanted to compete with him by choosing to bite off more than he could chew.𝕗𝗿𝕖𝐞𝐰𝗲𝕓𝐧𝕠𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝐨𝚖
It can aso be that he may be small, but he packs a much bigger punch. Baldy appeared to be the youngest among them, despite their being the same age.
But as if by design, he was also the weakest.
That said, it had been a very long time since he had seen him use his domain, so however this battle went, he would finally be able to place a ranking on Baldy’s power.
After flying for a few seconds, Baldy stopped and crossed his tiny arms over his chest. Behind him hovered two large swords.

In the distance, the Alpha Wolf took a step forward, causing the ground to shake and split open, spewing lava. It took a second step, and the lava rose, forming into a large wolf head. Its body exploded into flames, causing the very space around it to sizzle.
"Hey there, how about you just turn around and scram? I really don’t want to waste my time on you," Baldy said, not too bothered by the calamity walking toward him.
His words fell on deaf ears.
Seeing this, he sighed and unfurled his arms. Behind him, the two swords moved and dissolved into liquid metallic form. Then they transformed into two crescent-shaped blades.
"You know, it’s been several eras since I used my Sword Domain, so how about I test it on you?"
The two crescent-shaped blades spun, humming with intense sword intent.
Baldy spun his finger, causing the spinning blades to spin even faster.
"ROARRRR!"
The wolf roared again, a wave of terrifying aura surging out of its body. Then it lunged forward, sending flames exploding from its body and molten lava rising from the cracks in the ground.
The space sizzled, and terrible sword intent, born of the scorching heat of flame and lava, filled the surroundings.
Baldy smiled and took a swing with his right hand, causing the spinning crescent blades to surge forward.
"Longing Crescent Sword Domain."
Standing approximately 30 km away, Mak and Inaya furrowed their brows when Baldy’s Sword Domain surged forward. They had all expected to see something fancy, as in most domains.

Inaya cultivated the Ten Emotions Sword Dao, so her Ten Emotions Sword Domain allowed her to harness the power of all ten emotions. She rarely used it, but when she did, the space around her changed, taking on the manifestation of all ten emotions.
The same was true for Mak, whose Extreme Desire Sword Domain released pink mist that seemed to mess with the mind and heart.
Another example was Kent’s Genesis Sword Realm. Even as a Sword Realm, it affected space and, to some extent, bent the laws.
Baldy’s, however, was merely two crescent blades that formed a circular construct, gleaming with sword intent and profound understanding of the sword dao.
In most cases, many would scoff at his mediocre Sword Domain. But then it happened, and the two onlookers widened their eyes.

Just as the crescent blades closed in on the Alpha Wolf, Baldy grinned and snapped his fingers, causing them to expand. In the blink of an eye, an iron domain formed from two enormous crescent blades appeared around the Alpha Wolf, spinning rapidly around each other.
The Alpha Wolf was caught within this large domain of spinning swords, and if one looked at it, they would see a translucent dome form around the wolf, with the large swords acting as rings.
Inaya and Mak were in shock, but it was what Baldy said and did that made them nearly fall on their butts...
"You long to get out of my domain, but that is impossible. You see, the more you long to get out, the stronger it becomes. But if you choose not to leave, then well..."
He snapped his fingers, and crescent swords exploded outward, thousands of them, attacking the wolf, who couldn’t afford to ignore even a single one of them.
"...you have no choice but to long to get out."

Regardless of how one saw it, being attacked in such an enclosed space would make anyone want to get out of there. But by longing to get out, the domain grew stronger, intensifying the attacks, which in turn made the victim long even more desperately to escape.
"Damn, looks like Baldy has even surpassed me in terms of the offensive aspect of Sword Domains," Mak said with a smile, happy for his brother.
"It appears loneliness had helped him master his domain."
Inaya nodded to Mak’s words.

She had the privilege of learning more about Baldy and Mak, so she knew the little bald kid had lived alone since the Divine Era. Aside from the two times Mak came to visit him, he hadn’t spoken to anyone until recently, when Kent returned.

So he had been very lonely, and as someone with a child’s mindset, that might have been very painful. But then again, his domain required that, and looking at the Alpha Wolf, which was already at death’s door, it seemed everything had been worth it.
"No matter how I see it, Baldy’s domain has great potential," Inaya commented, also happy for Baldy.
The wolves trapped in Mak’s domain were down to the last two. Soon, the last wolf to survive the ordeal lost consciousness, never to wake up again.
Five minutes later, the Alpha Wolf also couldn’t endure the relentless attacks of Baldy’s domain, so it succumbed to death. Baldy deactivated his domain and returned to Mak and Inaya’s side.
"So, what do you think, Big Brother? Do you think Big Brother Kent will be happy with my domain?"
Mak smiled and brushed Baldy’s bald head. "Well, I think he is going to be more pleased with your domain than mine."
That was all Baldy needed to know. He retrieved three candies from his space ring that Gaia and her minions had given him before leaving for this mission and started eating.
Mak just smirked and turned to Inaya.
"Where do we go from here if we want to locate the person we came here for?"
Inaya looked due east and replied, "Let’s go see an old friend of mine."

chapters.title: Chapter 1853: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (3)
paragraphs: Amon’s Guillotine Cave clearly isn’t for everyone. Traveling for an hour without encountering danger is rare.
Inaya and her team always had to be on high alert, since a slight mistake could result in an attack so dangerous that all three of them wished they had never come to this dreadful place.
Luckily, Baldy seemed to be in a good mood, so he was always proactive, facing the dangers before they came.

His mood was high because Gaia and her minions went out of their way to fill his space ring with all kinds of candy. Gaia is the Cosmic Weaver, so by tapping into the cosmos, she can pull just about anything from anywhere she wants.
Since Baldy is the only male in their group, they treated him to the best delicacies that would last him for months, perhaps even years.

After traveling due east for two weeks, they came to a halt before a large river filled with clean, green water. The green mist covering the water’s surface reeked of poison, so dense that even from 2 km away, they could sense their bodies reacting to it.
"It is strange how everything here reeks of sword intent, yet mutated in a way," Baldy said, seated on Mak’s shoulder.

"That is the strange nature of this place, Baldy," Inaya said. "The last time I was here, I managed to cultivate my sword intent to a monstrous level simply by watching many beasts and beings fight using it.
If you stay here long enough, you will come to appreciate the great benefits you can reap. However, it is dangerous in every way, so staying on high alert is ideal. Regardless, we are here."
"We are?" Mak asked, his brow furrowed.
In his mind, this place doesn’t seem like a place a person should live.

"Yes. The person I came to see is the overlord of this domain." Inaya let out a deep sigh. Then, after a few hesitations, she said, "He is a badmouth, so kindly cut him some slack. Well, it would be good if you cut him all the slack you have because we are in his domain, and I don’t think we have what it takes to take him on, much less his minions."
Baldy and Mak, who knew how fearless Inaya was, furrowed their brows upon hearing her warning. It appeared she was wary of this person.
They, of course, became curious to meet the person who could make the fearless Inaya weary.
The next second, however, they tensed when someone spoke from behind them.
"Looks like you still hold me in high regard, Sleeping Beauty."

The person who spoke was a white-haired man in his late fifties. He looked fit and, by some standards, handsome. However, aside from his age and hair, he had green, leathery skin and a serpentine tail.
He had four arms and serpentine black eyes, the reeks of danger and mischief. He was clad in a human-like cloak.

If there is one thing Mak is good at, it is reading people. He excels in that regard; in fact, in most cases, whenever he faces someone in battle, he can tell exactly how dangerous they are and whether or not he can face them.
Today, his senses told him this person was a calamity, and, more importantly, he couldn’t even sense what made this person so dangerous.
He appeared ordinary, but Mak knew he was very dangerous.
Instinctively, he held Baldy’s arm, almost as if he didn’t want him to do anything funny.
Inaya, on the other hand, turned to the newly arrived, smirked, and asked, "Aren’t you too old to be sneaking up on people, Damba?"
"Oh, please. It wasn’t like you never expected it. Or are you telling me that after you returned to the Land of Bugs, you had become dull?"
Inaya chuckled upon hearing how Damba referred to the universe beyond Amon’s Guillotine Cave.
She turned to Mak and Baldy. "This is Damba, one of the many Overlords who live here. He cultivates Poison, and as you can see, he is very shameless in everything he does."
She smiled and introduced her teammates to Damba. "The pink-haired one is Mak, and the bald one is Baldy. They are my friends."

Damba studied the two for a few seconds before smiling. "Some friends you have, Inaya. Though I have to say, they aren’t ordinary at all, so why did you bring them?" He smiled and added, "Just so you know, I have stopped eating humans, but I wouldn’t mind a snack."
Baldy narrowed his eyes and was about to curse at the green-skinned man, but Mak covered his mouth. Seeing this, Inaya shook her head.
"Stop scaring the kid, Damba."
Damba didn’t seem to care.

Instead, he turned to Inaya and asked, "Why have you returned? And alone at that. You do know the Ash Maiden is still out to get you. She is even convinced you are still here somewhere, so she has her minions snooping around every now and then."

Inaya frowned a bit, but she didn’t panic. "I am not here for her, so you can rest assured that what happened the last time won’t happen again. But if she still comes after me, then guess what? She is in for a rude awakening."
"Oh, you seem rather confident. Did something happen that I am not aware of?" Damba asked with a curious look in his eyes.
He had intended to scare Inaya, but it appeared she wasn’t scared so easily this time around. When they first met, he had captured her and was planning on eating her.
However, Inaya had managed to convince him to free her.

In return, she would tell him stories from the world outside. The Calamity Zones are restricted in such a way that the beings inside can only leave by becoming companions to the natives of the Infinity Universe.
The problem, however, was that no beast or living being in this place would dare bow their head to anyone. So they were destined to remain trapped in this place forever.
Inaya managed to pique Damba’s interest, and so, for years, she revealed almost all she knew about the Infinity Universe to him. This was why he had come to realize Inaya’s bottleneck.
"Something did happen, as you can see, but that isn’t why I am here."
"Then why are you here?"
"Do you remember that race I told you about... you know, the Forsaken Race?"

The next second, however, they tensed when someone spoke from behind them.
"Looks like you still hold me in high regard, Sleeping Beauty."
The person who spoke was a white-haired man in his late fifties.
He looked fit and, by some standards, handsome.
However, aside from his age and hair, he had green, leathery skin and a serpentine tail.
He had four arms and serpentine black eyes, the reeks of danger and mischief.
He was clad in a human-like cloak.
If there is one thing Mak is good at, it is reading people.
He excels in that regard; in fact, in most cases, whenever he faces someone in battle, he can tell exactly how dangerous they are and whether or not he can face them.
Today, his senses told him this person was a calamity, and, more importantly, he couldn’t even sense what made this person so dangerous.
He appeared ordinary, but Mak knew he was very dangerous.
Instinctively, he held Baldy’s arm, almost as if he didn’t want him to do anything funny.
Inaya, on the other hand, turned to the newly arrived, smirked, and asked, "Aren’t you too old to be sneaking up on people, Damba?"
"Oh, please.
It wasn’t like you never expected it.
Or are you telling me that after you returned to the Land of Bugs, you had become dull?"
Inaya chuckled upon hearing how Damba referred to the universe beyond Amon’s Guillotine Cave.
She turned to Mak and Baldy.
"This is Damba, one of the many Overlords who live here.
He cultivates Poison, and as you can see, he is very shameless in everything he does."
She smiled and introduced her teammates to Damba.
"The pink-haired one is Mak, and the bald one is Baldy.
They are my friends."
Damba studied the two for a few seconds before smiling.
"Some friends you have, Inaya.
Though I have to say, they aren’t ordinary at all, so why did you bring them?" He smiled and added, "Just so you know, I have stopped eating humans, but I wouldn’t mind a snack."
Baldy narrowed his eyes and was about to curse at the green-skinned man, but Mak covered his mouth.
Seeing this, Inaya shook her head.
"Stop scaring the kid, Damba."
Damba didn’t seem to care.
Instead, he turned to Inaya and asked, "Why have you returned?
And alone at that.
You do know the Ash Maiden is still out to get you.
She is even convinced you are still here somewhere, so she has her minions snooping around every now and then."
Inaya frowned a bit, but she didn’t panic.
"I am not here for her, so you can rest assured that what happened the last time won’t happen again.
But if she still comes after me, then guess what?
She is in for a rude awakening."
"Oh, you seem rather confident.
Did something happen that I am not aware of?" Damba asked with a curious look in his eyes.
He had intended to scare Inaya, but it appeared she wasn’t scared so easily this time around.
When they first met, he had captured her and was planning on eating her.
However, Inaya had managed to convince him to free her.
In return, she would tell him stories from the world outside.
The Calamity Zones are restricted in such a way that the beings inside can only leave by becoming companions to the natives of the Infinity Universe.
The problem, however, was that no beast or living being in this place would dare bow their head to anyone.
So they were destined to remain trapped in this place forever.
Inaya managed to pique Damba’s interest, and so, for years, she revealed almost all she knew about the Infinity Universe to him.
This was why he had come to realize Inaya’s bottleneck.
"Something did happen, as you can see, but that isn’t why I am here."
"Then why are you here?"
"Do you remember that race I told you about... you know, the Forsaken Race?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1854: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (4)
paragraphs: "Aren’t they the race that betrayed the universe by accepting aid from some unknown source?" Damba asked for more context, since he could still remember the conversation he had with Inaya all those years back.

"Yes, that same race. Apparently, someone from that place has been kept trapped here for years. We have come to rescue her, so you wouldn’t happen to have heard of or come across anyone with the features of that race, would you?"
Damba’s information network is one of the most extensive and vast sources Inaya had ever encountered, so she knew that if anyone had heard of Safira, the Forsaken Seer, it would be him.
"You know, Inaya, there are many people with features similar to those of the Forsaken Race, so you may have to be a bit more specific."
Inaya nodded. Then, recalling the description Kent had given her, she replied,

"Like I already said, she is a Forsaken being, so naturally, she has pale white skin and deep black hair streaked with silver strands. But aside from that, she has a pair of purple horns and reddish eyes. She is very beautiful, and, well, she has big breasts."
As she said that, her mind wandered back to how vividly Kent had described Safira’s breasts.

Then again, during the Primordial Era, when they first met, one of the most striking features Chaos had noticed was her breasts. They were the biggest he had ever seen, and while he never meant to stare too much, he couldn’t ignore such majestic racks.
Luckily, the mention of her boobs seemed to have stirred a memory in Damba’s mind.𝘧𝓇ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝘣𝓃ℴ𝓋𝑒𝑙.𝑐𝘰𝑚
"It appears I have information on the person you are searching for. In fact, I know where she is. However, I am not sure you are ready to go there."
"Why is that?" Inaya asked with a slight frown.

"Because the same person looking for you is also looking for her. The chances of you crossing paths with her minions are very high, so this might just be the most dangerous mission yet. Or, if you are lucky, it might be the simplest."
"Just tell me where she is. I will figure out how to handle that bitch later."
If she could simply kill that person, then she would have done so already. However, when it came to the Ash Maiden, she was no match for her, not even with Mak and Baldy’s help.
However, she also couldn’t leave now, not when she had come for Safira. This meant that whoever was after her, or both of them, had better prepare well because she wasn’t leaving without her asset.
Damba smiled, seeing the determined look that had appeared on Inaya’s face. This told him she had no intention of leaving just because someone of his power level was after her.
In fact, he was thrilled that Inaya seemed so defiant right now.

"The one you are looking for lives in the Umbrella Forest. She resides in the Inner Zone, surrounded by all kinds of horrors. If you go there, there is a high chance you will encounter the Ash Maiden’s minions on top of the horrors living there."
Inaya nodded. Then her eyes narrowed.
"You are awfully talkative today, Damba. You wouldn’t happen to have a motive behind this, would you?" Her eyes narrowed further, and she took a step forward, causing Damba to take a step back.
"You always seem to have an angle in whatever you do, so tell me, what do you have planned this time? After all, I am in this mess because of your schemes."
Damba chuckled, brushing a hand through his hair. "No angle here, Inaya. I just want my favorite human bug to succeed."
"Liar. You want something, so spill it before I find another way to make sure your plans never come to pass. And trust me, I mastered that many years ago."
Damba and Inaya locked into an intense glare for a few minutes before Damba smirked and said,
"Let’s just say that, without my help, you cannot get to the person you came for. So, for a moment, let’s assume our interests align."

"The last time our interests aligned, I became the most wanted person to an Overlord. So tell me, please, what do you have planned this time around? And don’t bullshit me, or I will be very pissed, and you don’t want me angry right now."
"True, you do not want Big Sister angry right now," Baldy said while still seated on Mak’s shoulder.
Damba smiled, and for a few seconds, he contemplated his next move. In the end, he decided to come clean.
"The last time you had a falling out with the Ash Maiden, I went on a mission to retrieve the Nameless Map. I succeeded, but got ambushed on my way back.
I had to ditch the map somewhere in the Umbrella Forest. Several years ago, I received a report that it had fallen into one of the Variant Pools.
Unfortunately for me, the Ash Maiden had also heard the same report and had deployed her minions to investigate and find an opening, just as I had.
A couple of years ago, I managed to find an opening, but it required two things. First, we have to get closer, which can only be achieved by someone who isn’t a native of this place.

That is not something to worry about, since we both have human subordinates. However, not all of us have a human friend called Inaya, the Ten Emotions Sword Maiden," he laughed, causing Inaya to smirk.
"I want you to get closer to the entrance and place my Teleportation Rune there. This would allow me to teleport directly there, which I think would solve your problem.

The second part of the plan has to do with me fighting the Ash Maiden, whom I know will come there. With me fighting her, you will have the chance to find the person you are looking for and rescue her long before the battle comes to an end.
All you have to do is get within ten meters of the entrance to the Blood Variant Pool and place my rune there." He looked closely at Inaya and asked,
"Do you think you can handle it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1855: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (5)
paragraphs: The question isn’t whether Inaya can handle the mission Damba had given her. She can, and with ease at that, especially now that she has become a True Sword Supreme.
The right question should be: what is Damba not telling her?

Inaya had lived with this shameless bastard for years, and so she knew just how insidious he could be. He is secretive, and whatever plans he comes up with, there is always a hidden aspect he doesn’t reveal until it is too late.

Inaya never intended to sign her name in the Ash Maidens’ book, not by a long shot. However, Damba’s scheme had landed her in that hot mess. Now, he had come up with something else, and that alone didn’t sit right with her.
Inaya narrowed her eyes and walked closer to Damba, who couldn’t help taking a few steps back.
While he was way stronger than Inaya, considering he was a Primordial and she was only a Supreme, he had to admit that this human lady scared him.

"Tell me, Damba, what else do you have planned this time around? And before you laugh and tell me everything is normal, know that my man is someone you wouldn’t want to anger. Trust me, if you play a fast one on me this time, I will return with a legion of terrifying warriors led by a very angry dragon. So tell me the truth, is the mission as simple as you claim or not?"

Damba smiled and shook his head. "Trust me, it is that simple. All you have to do is get closer to the Blood Variant Pool and put my teleportation rune there. The only danger is how you will get past those blood monkeys living in that zone."
She looked at Baldy and Mak and said, "I believe you have it covered, especially with their help."
Inaya didn’t nod at his words. Instead, she studied Damba’s expression for a few minutes before a sigh escaped her lips.
She knew she had no choice but to take up the offer. Safira was somewhere in there, and by finally getting the Ash Maiden off her back, she would be able to look for her.
The last thing she wanted was to return to the tower without the person she came for.
"Fine. I will do it, but as I said, pray this isn’t a setup. Trust me when I repeat this, but my man and my sisters aren’t the kind you want to offend."
Of course, it was just a brag. While Pandora was a Primordial, she isn’t a swordsman, so she doesn’t have sword intent. Because of that, she will be powerless in this calamity zone.
And while Kent had become much stronger, his cultivation of the sword was still limited, so even if he came, he would be a bug before someone like Damba.
But nothing was preventing her from making a threat, especially if she knew her man had managed to find himself seven Blood Warriors, with two qualified to come and wreak havoc in this place.
Damba raised two of his four hands and said with a smile, "I swear there are no curves to this mission. Just make sure you prepare for a quick and decisive battle."
Inaya nodded and turned to Mak and Baldy. "Are you two up for it?"
"Yes, big sister, let’s go kick some ass," Baldy was as enthusiastic as ever, while Mak seemed okay with everything as well.
"I would like to meet big brother, so the earlier we get things done, the better."
She nodded and turned back to Damba. "Hand over the rune and send us closer to the Umbrella Forest. Just prepare for battle because the last thing I want is to fight that bitch."
"But of course."
Damba still looks suspicious, but Inaya had no plans to dwell on it. If she failed to get close, she would just teleport into the tower and try again later.
Initially, when they appeared inside this place, their connection to the tower was severed. However, it was restored a couple of days ago, allowing them to return to the tower whenever they wanted.
So she wasn’t worried about the success of this mission.

Inaya, of course, collected more details on where they would find Safira. She couldn’t handle this dangerous mission without first getting a heads-up on where they would have to go after completing the mission Damba had given them.
Damba formed a hand seal, and when he pointed forward, a green portal appeared, swirling with green water.
"When you are ready."
Inaya turned to her teammates, and without a word, they walked through the portal and vanished from sight.
Somewhere else, the portal opened atop a cliff, and the three walked out. Before them lay a vast and expansive forest teeming with all kinds of dangers.
Standing atop the cliff, they could see seven segments of the forest, each bearing a different color.

The closest to them was a blue-colored forest, and right beside that was a red one. They could directly head to the red one, but to get to the green one, where Safira lived, they would have to go through the red forest, which housed the Blood Variant Pool.
"Our destination is that place," Inaya said, pointing at the red forest.
"Isn’t that sweet? I can already sense dangers staring at us from all the way here." Baldy smiled and jumped down from Mak’s shoulder. "Somehow, I want to fight them."
"You are not the only one, Baldy. I also want to fight them," Mak said, causing Inaya, who had planned to come on this mission alone initially, to be grateful these two were with her.
"Then let’s not waste too much time, shall we? We have a Forsaken Seer to save, and knowing their kind, she probably knows we are coming, so we should be on high alert."
They nodded, then they were gone, speeding toward the Blood Variant Pool, where their mission would officially begin.
The mission was very simple: they had to get close to the Pool and place the rune there. The rest would handle itself, hopefully.

chapters.title: Chapter 1856: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (6)
paragraphs: [Somewhere in Amon’s Guillotine Cave]
Inside a cave hidden somewhere in the Green Field Variant Pool, one of the seven zones in the Umbrella Forest, a pale-skinned woman opened her eyes from what appeared to be a deep sleep.
The moment she opened them, she rose to her feet and rushed to the entrance of the cave, where a very strong formation protected outsiders from entering.

She walked out, and when she was finally outside, she looked to her left, her gaze piercing deep into the distance. After a few moments of staring, she sighed, walked back into the cave, and sat down.
Then she formed a hand seal and pointed it at her forehead. For a moment, she saw nothing. But then she saw everything, and her eyes widened.

She could see Inaya, Mak, and Baldy locked in battle with hundreds of Blood Monkeys, their fight shaking the very forest. However, what intrigued her the most and kept her looking despite the constant drain on her essence was the mark on Inaya’s body.
The mark was that of a dragon’s head with four deadly fangs crossing it.
This mark felt familiar, too familiar that she couldn’t help but wish to figure out what it all meant. For a couple of minutes, she couldn’t help but wonder where she had seen this mark before.
But then it all clicked, and her eyes widened.
"Chaos..."
It had been thirteen eras since she had been sent to this place. That was a very long time for someone like her to remember names from the distant past.
She had forgotten many names, including those of some close friends. However, she had never forgotten the name of the dragon who was the reason she had found herself in this mess.
She had helped Chaos after he was ambushed by the Forsaken Race. When they found out, they sealed her cultivation and imprisoned her here.
She had been here for eras already.
She pulled a small purple token from her storage pouch and brushed her hand across it, a sigh escaping her lips. For a moment, she contemplated what to do.
It had been many eras since she had last heard of Chaos, so sensing his seal on Inaya, she was tempted to go meet her.
However, she hesitated because, despite living here for billions of years, her cultivation, which had been sealed at the peak of the Universal God Stage, remained unchanged.
She couldn’t be reckless and head over to such a place, not when she had been hiding from the Ash Maiden and her minions.
But if she wanted to find out more about Chaos, then she had to go and learn what these people knew about him.
She soon made up her mind and left her cave dwelling, using her many years of experience to sneak through the dangerous forest as she closed in on the Blood Variant Pool.
Somewhere else, a lady with large twisted horns and ashy skin stood atop a large tower overlooking the red forest in the distance. Of course, the distance between them was several million kilometers.
However, she could see what was happening there, and judging by the amused expression on her face, she was happy to have found the one she had been looking for all these years.
But as she watched Inaya and her team head in a particular direction, realization flashed across her face, making her turn away from the forest and look into the distance.
There, Damba stood with an amused smile, looking back at her.
For a moment, she fumed with anger.
Damba smirked and said, "I believe this is what humans call checkmate."
His laughter spread across the vast forest around him, causing the already angered expression on the Ash Maiden’s face to darken even further.
"Don’t celebrate too early, you green-faced bastard. I haven’t lost just yet."

Just as she said that, a streak of red light flashed across the sky, entering the Blood Variant Pool. Within this red light, five people, each from the Infinity Universe, began attacking the Blood Monkeys as they headed toward the portal on the other side.

Already, Inaya and her team were two kilometers away from where they would place the rune. However, the speed at which these five were moving was so great that, in no time, they had closed the distance to three kilometers, and soon they would surpass even Inaya.
"Let’s see which team makes it there first," the Ash Maiden said with a smug expression.
However, instead of panicking, Damba just smiled and replied, "You’ve already lost, bitch. Now watch how I drag your face through the mud."

Considering how fast the Ash Maiden’s team was moving, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say she held the advantage. Yet despite that, she couldn’t shake the feeling that Damba had something else planned.
Damba’s reputation as a sneaky and crafty bastard wasn’t earned for no reason.
He was that crafty, and perhaps that was what kept the Ash Maiden from feeling at ease.

Still, she knew the outcome would be determined by who could overpower whom. As far as she remembered, Damba wasn’t on her level of power, so she kept her composure and continued to wait for the rune to be planted.
Inaya harnessed the power of the Hatred and Resentment Sword Dao, cleaving through the Blood Monkeys as though they were bugs.
At the side, Baldy was also unleashing terrifying crescent-shaped sword slashes at the Blood Monkeys while riding atop a rather large sword.

This sword had been given to him by his big brother, Han, before leaving for this mission. While they both possessed Eternal Sword Intent, Han, like the rest of his siblings, was overprotective of Baldy.
So, to make up for the years of neglect, he had given Baldy that sword, which contained seventy percent of his power. In dire moments, it would reveal its true might.
Mak, on the other hand, was like a mist, gliding across the battlefield from one side to the other, cutting down his enemies as though they were made of foam.
"I feel like something is terribly wrong," Baldy said, cutting off the tail of a Blood Monkey.
"You are not the only one feeling that, Baldy. I feel the same way too," Inaya replied, a frown appearing on her face.

sentences.text: [Somewhere in Amon’s Guillotine Cave]
Inside a cave hidden somewhere in the Green Field Variant Pool, one of the seven zones in the Umbrella Forest, a pale-skinned woman opened her eyes from what appeared to be a deep sleep.
The moment she opened them, she rose to her feet and rushed to the entrance of the cave, where a very strong formation protected outsiders from entering.
She walked out, and when she was finally outside, she looked to her left, her gaze piercing deep into the distance.
After a few moments of staring, she sighed, walked back into the cave, and sat down.
Then she formed a hand seal and pointed it at her forehead.
For a moment, she saw nothing.
But then she saw everything, and her eyes widened.
She could see Inaya, Mak, and Baldy locked in battle with hundreds of Blood Monkeys, their fight shaking the very forest.
However, what intrigued her the most and kept her looking despite the constant drain on her essence was the mark on Inaya’s body.
The mark was that of a dragon’s head with four deadly fangs crossing it.
This mark felt familiar, too familiar that she couldn’t help but wish to figure out what it all meant.
For a couple of minutes, she couldn’t help but wonder where she had seen this mark before.
But then it all clicked, and her eyes widened.
"Chaos..."
It had been thirteen eras since she had been sent to this place.
That was a very long time for someone like her to remember names from the distant past.
She had forgotten many names, including those of some close friends.
However, she had never forgotten the name of the dragon who was the reason she had found herself in this mess.
She had helped Chaos after he was ambushed by the Forsaken Race.
When they found out, they sealed her cultivation and imprisoned her here.
She had been here for eras already.
She pulled a small purple token from her storage pouch and brushed her hand across it, a sigh escaping her lips.
For a moment, she contemplated what to do.
It had been many eras since she had last heard of Chaos, so sensing his seal on Inaya, she was tempted to go meet her.
However, she hesitated because, despite living here for billions of years, her cultivation, which had been sealed at the peak of the Universal God Stage, remained unchanged.
She couldn’t be reckless and head over to such a place, not when she had been hiding from the Ash Maiden and her minions.
But if she wanted to find out more about Chaos, then she had to go and learn what these people knew about him.
She soon made up her mind and left her cave dwelling, using her many years of experience to sneak through the dangerous forest as she closed in on the Blood Variant Pool.
Somewhere else, a lady with large twisted horns and ashy skin stood atop a large tower overlooking the red forest in the distance.
Of course, the distance between them was several million kilometers.
However, she could see what was happening there, and judging by the amused expression on her face, she was happy to have found the one she had been looking for all these years.
But as she watched Inaya and her team head in a particular direction, realization flashed across her face, making her turn away from the forest and look into the distance.
There, Damba stood with an amused smile, looking back at her.
For a moment, she fumed with anger.
Damba smirked and said, "I believe this is what humans call checkmate."
His laughter spread across the vast forest around him, causing the already angered expression on the Ash Maiden’s face to darken even further.
"Don’t celebrate too early, you green-faced bastard.
I haven’t lost just yet."
Just as she said that, a streak of red light flashed across the sky, entering the Blood Variant Pool.
Within this red light, five people, each from the Infinity Universe, began attacking the Blood Monkeys as they headed toward the portal on the other side.
Already, Inaya and her team were two kilometers away from where they would place the rune.
However, the speed at which these five were moving was so great that, in no time, they had closed the distance to three kilometers, and soon they would surpass even Inaya.
"Let’s see which team makes it there first," the Ash Maiden said with a smug expression.
However, instead of panicking, Damba just smiled and replied, "You’ve already lost, bitch.
Now watch how I drag your face through the mud."
Considering how fast the Ash Maiden’s team was moving, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say she held the advantage.
Yet despite that, she couldn’t shake the feeling that Damba had something else planned.
Damba’s reputation as a sneaky and crafty bastard wasn’t earned for no reason.
He was that crafty, and perhaps that was what kept the Ash Maiden from feeling at ease.
Still, she knew the outcome would be determined by who could overpower whom.
As far as she remembered, Damba wasn’t on her level of power, so she kept her composure and continued to wait for the rune to be planted.
Inaya harnessed the power of the Hatred and Resentment Sword Dao, cleaving through the Blood Monkeys as though they were bugs.
At the side, Baldy was also unleashing terrifying crescent-shaped sword slashes at the Blood Monkeys while riding atop a rather large sword.
This sword had been given to him by his big brother, Han, before leaving for this mission.
While they both possessed Eternal Sword Intent, Han, like the rest of his siblings, was overprotective of Baldy.
So, to make up for the years of neglect, he had given Baldy that sword, which contained seventy percent of his power.
In dire moments, it would reveal its true might.
Mak, on the other hand, was like a mist, gliding across the battlefield from one side to the other, cutting down his enemies as though they were made of foam.
"I feel like something is terribly wrong," Baldy said, cutting off the tail of a Blood Monkey.
"You are not the only one feeling that, Baldy.
I feel the same way too," Inaya replied, a frown appearing on her face.

chapters.title: Chapter 1857: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (7)
paragraphs: "We are almost there," Inaya said, deflecting an attack from a Blood Monkey with the blade of her sword. The monkey didnt falter and quickly moved, and its tail, which is many times longer than its body, whipped from behind it, coming in for yet another attack.

But before it could arrive, Inaya had already moved away, circling around the monkey. Just as its tail struck nothing, a red light mixed with black flames, filled with so much sword intent, flashed out, landing on the monkey’s side.
A deep wound was cut into its body, and the impact sent it flying several kilometers away.
Inaya dissolved into the chaos, choosing not to go after it, not when she had already injured it severely.
She appeared in the distance, her sword carving arcs in the air.
Looking deeper into the Blood Variant Pool, she could see a team of four coming toward them, each a powerful warrior. Of course, she had no idea this team was initially five, but one had been killed.
Well, even if she did, the mere fact that they were coming toward them told Inaya one of two things...
First, they were either on the same mission as them or they were here to kill them. The ashy tattoos on their foreheads told her they were from the Ash Maiden.

So maybe they were here for them, or worse, for both reasons. But she couldn’t afford to think of that just yet... the Blood Monkeys weren’t going anywhere, and the closer they got to where they would plant the Teleportation Rune, the fiercer the attacks became.
Looking to the side and seeing Baldy and Han fighting the monkeys, she smiled. ’Good thing they came with me, else I would have had it hard this time around.’
She had lived here for a few eras, but most of that time was spent sleeping. She hadn’t really discovered much of the danger here.
But today, she was seeing and experiencing it firsthand, which, from her expression, showed she had to hurry before they found themselves besieged by beings they couldn’t afford to handle.
They kept pushing forward, using every ounce of their power.
But then something happened, and Inaya’s biggest fear came true.
Just as they were 200 meters away from the location, a red portal flared, and a lone figure holding a blood-dripping broadsword stepped out, causing the very ground beneath them to turn into blood.
At once, Inaya and her team felt their bodies tense, their muscles tighten, and every ounce of strength in them drain.
On the other side, the four teammates kept pushing forward, breaching the 100-meter mark from where they would also plant the rune.
Inaya gritted her teeth and looked up, meeting the gaze of the person who had stopped them. The person had long red hair, flawless red skin, and eyes like red gems.
She was beautiful, with well-defined bone structure and breasts barely contained within her sexy armor. What was even more alluring about her was the red fox tail billowing behind her.
This clearly showed she was a foxkin, and a Blood-type foxkin at that.
For a moment, she appeared more seductive than dangerous. However, Mak, who liked the company of women, wasn’t turned on even by her looks.
That was because he had met Damba, and the same danger he felt from him, this lady also gave off. But what was even more chilling was that she didn’t have the same cultivation base as Damba.
This lady was a Pseudo-Primordial, yet her danger level was at Damba’s level or perhaps even higher.
For a moment, the air hung heavy. Then the lady spoke, and Inaya’s eyes widened.
"I am Ruby. It’s a pleasure to finally meet the Ten Emotions Sword Supreme," she said with a gentle bow. Then the pressure around them vanished, and all three of them could finally breathe.
"You know who I am?" Inaya asked after catching her breath.

"I do. I have read about you so much that I know every little thing about you ever recorded," she smiled and took one step forward, causing the blood on the ground to part and allowing her slender legs to step onto the bare earth.
Inaya and her two teammates narrowed their eyes, not underestimating this lady at all.

She simply smiled and said, "I came from the Infinity Universe, same as you. However, back when I lived there, I was a member of the Hell Devastators, a team formed and led by the legendary Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith."
Inaya’s eyes widened, causing Ruby to realize that she knew who that person was.
"So you know about the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith," she asked, and Inaya nodded.
"Who doesn’t know about such a legendary warrior? His legends are simply out of this world, so you can say I am a huge fan."
Of course, she wasn’t lying. Kent was her husband, and since he had been the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, she could boldly say she knew him better than anyone.
But she would also be lying to some extent because, while both she and her sisters were aware that Kent was once the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, they didn’t really know much about that life.
She knew more about his second incarnation as Lord Genesis, but not much about his life as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith or any of his other incarnations.
Still, Ruby was pleased to hear someone remember her leader and master, the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.
"It is good to see that someone still remembers my leader. That said, why are you here, and why did you choose to join forces with those two to kill me?"𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝔀𝓮𝒃𝙣𝓸𝒗𝒆𝒍.𝙘𝒐𝒎
Inaya, Mak, and Baldy widened their eyes, realization finally dawning on them. Before Inaya could reply, the rune she had been given flew out of her space ring and exploded, forming a green portal.

Two hundred meters away, the others carrying the Ash Maiden’s rune also stopped just as the rune exploded into an ashen portal. From within, the Ash Maiden flew out, bringing with her a terrifying pressure.
Inaya looked up at Damba and furiously asked, "Damba, you bastard, what is the meaning of this?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1858: Amon’s Guillotine Cave (8)
paragraphs: Damba grinned, his expression turning twisted. "No hard feelings, Inaya, but as you can see, she is a threat to the two of us, and as such, she has to die. I never meant for you to get entangled in all of this, but your presence is what we needed most to flush her out."

He turned and looked at Ruby, who stood there calmly, her expression still soft and relaxed, almost as if, despite being a Pseudo-Primordial, she wasn’t bothered that two Primordials had surrounded her.
"You already know that this domain cannot have a third Primordial. It is simply impossible. We are already short on resources, so having you here will hurt business.
This is why you must die, since you refuse to submit to either of us."

Damba’s words were followed by the Ash Maiden, whose voice was as ashen as her appearance. "The green-faced bastard is right. The other six who refused have already been put down. You, however, had to prove your stubbornness by still refusing to bend the knee.

Now that we have finally managed to flush you out, you can say we will finally be rid of you. Then we can go back to fighting each other," she laughed, her voice spreading throughout the Blood Variant Pool.
Ruby looked at the two Primordials and smirked. "So that’s how it is, huh? Three eras ago, you two tried to kill me but failed, so what makes you think you can succeed now?"

Damba smirked. "Three eras ago, she wasn’t here. And from what you revealed back then, it is clear that you are obsessed with her. So tell me, now that she is in danger, are you going to run or fight? If you run, she dies. If you fight, you die."
"Both of you die," the Ash Maiden corrected Damba, making the latter smirk before nodding.
Inaya gripped her sword tightly, regret washing over her face. Her expression was filled with deep hatred and anger, so intense that one could almost see it manifest around her.𝕗𝕣𝐞𝐞𝘄𝐞𝚋𝚗𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗹.𝚌𝕠𝚖
"So all this while, the bitch hasn’t been hunting me because I offended her. She has been hunting me because I was the only person who could flush Ruby out of hiding."
"Bingo," Damba said, snapping his fingers.
Inaya narrowed her eyes and pointed her sword forward. "I already warned you, Damba. Crossing me will result in your death. Clearly, you didn’t take my threat seriously."

Damba laughed in reply, spreading all four arms wide. "Look around you, Inaya. This is Amon’s Guillotine Cave, and right now you are inside my domain. No matter what kind of trump card you possess, as long as I am here, nobody can touch me."
Inaya smiled and turned to Baldy and Mak. "Get behind me and make sure you maintain physical contact."
They obeyed immediately. Baldy jumped onto Mak’s shoulder while Mak placed his hand on Inaya’s shoulder.
Inaya then turned toward Ruby and asked, "Are you really a subordinate of the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith?"
Ruby nodded. "I sure am. I fought side by side with him during the Flame Wars."
"Very well. Then do the same as them, and whatever happens, don’t let go."
Ruby didn’t object to her command. She teleported behind Inaya and placed her hand on Inaya’s other shoulder.
Turning back toward Damba, Inaya spoke, her tone colder than ice.
"I am grateful for your care back when I had nowhere else to go, Damba. You took me in and gave me some peace of mind. But by helping you get here today, you can consider that debt repaid.
Now, as for whether you survive what is about to happen or die, you have no one to blame but yourself."
Inaya let go of her sword, then clapped her hands together and invoked the words Kent had taught her.
"Standing on the authority granted by my beloved, I, Inaya, the Ten Emotions Sword Supreme, invoke the wrath of the Primordial Chaos Dragon... Kill my foe and wash away my shame."
RUMBLE!
The sky split open, and terror descended, shaking the entire Amon’s Guillotine Cave. Suddenly, all light was drained from the sky, and darkness engulfed everything.
Inaya stood tall, her figure bathed in absolute power.

Mak, Baldy, and Ruby, still holding onto her, felt their bodies tense. However, compared to Damba and the Ash Maiden, who were now on the ground, barely having the strength to stand, they were in a much better state.
But the worst was yet to come.
From the crack in the sky, a massive crimson dragon eye snapped open, causing the already terrifying pressure to intensify.

Thirty kilometers away, Safira looked at the crimson eye, and a cold sweat instantly broke out across her back. However, before she could gather the courage to run, a rune lit up on her forehead, and at once, her body was pulled forward.
In an instant, she appeared in the air above Damba and the Ash Maiden.
Then, from the eye in the sky, a crimson rune descended and merged with the rune on her forehead.
BOOOOM!

A terrifying pressure exploded from her body, causing the space beneath her to cave in. Then, as if she had been possessed, she extended her hand, and the sword lying beside Inaya flew into her firm grip.
Turning toward the Ash Maiden, her fury erupted.
"DIE!"

She lunged forward, and in an instant, her sword pierced the Ash Maiden’s shoulder. She didn’t stop there. Instead, she severed both of her arms, then both of her legs, before moving to her face and slicing off her ears, nose, and lips.
Then she unleashed countless more slashes across her body. Within ten seconds, the Ash Maiden was barely clinging to life.
But instead of killing her, Safira shifted her attention to Damba.
He had four arms, and Safira took her time severing every one of them before moving on to his legs and the rest of his body.
It took only thirty seconds, but by the time she was done, even a god could have killed the two Primordial, now reduced to bugs.
She didn’t kill them, though. Instead, she landed silently on the ground.
Then the eye in the sky slowly closed, and Safira lost consciousness.
Before she could hit the ground, however, Inaya rushed forward and caught her. Then she turned to Baldy, Mak, and Ruby and said,
"Time to leave."

chapters.title: Chapter 1859: Friends or Enemies
paragraphs: A portal opened inside the Legion Tower, and five people fell out, three landing on the ground while two—one seated on the other’s shoulder and the other passed out in the other’s arms.
Inaya, Baldy, Mak, Ruby, and Safira had appeared inside the tower, leaving the dying Primordials to be attacked by the beast that had been watching their battle.
Inaya never intended to kill them that easily, anyway.
If they survive, then it is their good fortune. If not, then they have themselves to blame for crossing the wife if the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
Her plan had been to use Kent’s authority as the Primordial Chaos Dragon to suppress them long enough so they could escape and go look for Safira.

But in a twist of fate, Safira rather came to them, and for reasons she couldn’t explain, she became possessed by Kent’s power, allowing her not only to buy time but also to leave the two Primordials completely beaten.
She won before the battle even began.
Safira also never expected this to happen.

When she sensed Inaya’s presence because of Kent’s mark on her, she came to investigate. For a moment, she watched them battle the Blood Monkeys. However, things changed when Inaya invoked Chaos’s name.
Under normal circumstances, she would have verified that Inaya was somehow related to Chaos. But she never expected herself to also be pulled into the chaos of the moment.
Now, they had returned to the tower with Safira, the Forsaken Seer they had gone to Amon’s Guillotine Cave for in the first place.
The moment they appeared, the legions, including their sisters who were training in the various arenas, rushed to their side...

"Inaya, what happened?" Ainna asked, staring at the injuries on her best friend’s skin. She had yet to taste the forbidden fruit, but she had been living with Kent’s wives the entire time, even going on missions with them.
Seeing that her friend had sustained injuries and was now holding an unconscious lady in her arms, she panicked.
Luckily, they were just flesh wounds. "I am fine, Ainna. However, she needs more attention." She let go of Safira’s body, allowing her to lie on the lush ground.
Elaine rushed forward, activating her healing abilities instantly. Part of it went to Inaya, while the majority entered Safira’s body.

"Is this the Forsaken Seer Kent sent you to go get?" Neomi asked, looking at Safira’s pale face, which was now even paler due to the strain she had endured in those 30 seconds of being possessed by Chaos’s authority.
"Yes."𝓯𝙧𝙚𝒆𝙬𝙚𝒃𝙣𝙤𝒗𝓮𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
"Damn, she is gorgeous," Selene, of course, had to say the obvious. But she wasn’t wrong. Compared to how ugly some of the Forsaken beings were, Safira was akin to an angel.
She has the looks and the body.
But her words were drowned out when, suddenly, heat and the smell of blood came from one side.

Everyone turned only to see Meiko and Ruby staring at each other, their auras clashing. For a moment, the air hung tense. However, Pandora waved her hand, and the two of them lost their ability to harness their power...
"Who are you?" Pandora asked, staring at Ruby, who appeared stunned, having lost her ability. Looking into Pandora’s dark eyes, she panicked.

However, Meiko arrogantly answered on her behalf, "Her name is Ruby, one of the minions who used to follow the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith back then." She smirked and added, showing her hatred for the lady,
"She is a demon fox and someone I want to kill very much."
Pandora didn’t take Meiko’s words for it. She had been living with her for a while now, so she knew this feisty sister of hers would say just about anything to get into a fight.
So she turned to Ruby and asked again, "Who are you?"
"My name is Ruby, but during the Flame Era, I was known as the Blood Fox Demoness, one of the people who fought under the banner of the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith."
"So you are one of the Hell Devastators," Zaila asked, taking a step forward.
"I was and still am." Ruby then narrowed her eyes and pointed her large crimson sword at Meiko. "I would like to know why you are protecting this bitch. She is my enemy, and I wish to kill her now."
"I am afraid I cannot do that," Pandora said, walking to Meiko’s side. "Hate or love her, she is my sister, so if you want her dead, you have to go through me."
Even though Ruby’s power was suppressed, the killing intent in her eyes said otherwise...
"She is your sister? Are you saying this vixen who caused many to lose their minds is your sister?" A pained laugh came from Ruby’s mouth, causing her killing intent to start leaking...

"This bitch killed my friend simply because she liked the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith. Then she went ahead and attacked me simply because I was her friend, so tell me, do you think you can stop me from killing her today?"

"Oh please, you should be grateful I killed that bitch. In case you are not aware, she colluded with one of the Flame Monarchs, and she was going to betray you. Had it not been because you were related to Fjorge, I wouldn’t have minded. So instead of spouting nonsense, be grateful, for I did you a great favor."
"You bitch, you killed her because you were jealous of our friendship and her liking for Fjorge. Or you think just because we used to be friends, you had the right to kill my other friends?"

Meiko giggled. "As a matter of fact, yes. And in case you are wondering, I was also the one who killed your stepsister and your stepmother. Those losers tried to betray you too, and despite hating you with all my guts, we used to be friends, so be grateful again."
"You crazy bitch."
For a tense couple of minutes, the air hung heavy, everyone wondering just what was happening. However, the next second left them all asking what the fuck was going on.
After staring at each other like mortal enemies, the two moved, and in what could be considered the biggest shock ever, they hugged each other.
Lilian narrowed her eyes and asked, "Are they friends or enemies?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1860: Frenemies
paragraphs: Be it the warriors of the Chaos Dragon Legion or the ladies who had come to attend to their sister, they were all left stunned, unsure of how to explain what had just happened.
Ruby and Meiko clearly hated each other from what they had seen. Something had happened between them, and Meiko had even admitted to killing Ruby’s friend, stepsister, and stepmother.
That alone, if nothing else, warranted Ruby tearing out her throat. However, from the look of things, that wouldn’t happen, for the two ladies were now hugging, and that was just too shocking.
The sheer amount of mental stress the ladies were feeling right now, as they tried to understand what had happened, was just too much.
Eventually, Unity asked, "What in the actual fuck is going on right now?"
Was she sad that the ladies weren’t at each other’s throats? No.

But was she confused about them hugging each other? The answer was yes, and that was plain as day, judging by the looks on everyone’s faces. Pandora, who had stopped them from gutting each other, now stood there with a lost expression.
She had sensed it and knew, deep within, that Ruby wanted to kill Meiko and that the latter also wanted to fight.
Maybe Meiko was unhinged, so that could be considered normal.
The difference between her and Kaizo was that she knew how to pick her opponents, unlike Kaizo, who just wanted to fight regardless of the strength of his opponent.
But Ruby wanted her dead.
Now, however, Pandora didn’t know what to think.
Soon, however, they were able to ask the questions that mattered when the two ladies broke the hug and stared daggers at each other.
"So are you two friends or enemies?" Vexthra asked, walking toward the two ladies...
Ruby smirked and answered, "Who wants to be friends with this vixen?"𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦
"As if I had any plans to be friends with a demoness." Meiko fired back, leaving Vexthra unsure of what to ask next. She, however, managed to think of something else.
"So, do you ladies want to kill each other then?"

This time, too, Ruby was the first to answer. "I would love nothing more than that. However, considering the person she was with back then, killing her would put me in trouble, so she can keep her bitchy life for now."
"Oh please, as if you have what it takes to kill me." Meiko smirked and pointed her slender finger at Ruby. "Let’s go a few rounds and see if you can maintain your arrogance."
"Actually, Meiko, she can kill you in less than five seconds," Pandora said, causing Meiko to falter, her brow knitting as she turned to face Pandora.
"Big sister, what do you mean by she can kill me in less than five seconds? We are both Pseudo-Primordials."

Pandora smiled and brushed a few strands of crimson hair from Meiko’s face before saying, "Inasmuch as I would love to tell you that being a Pseudo-Primordial would save you, the lady standing there is very deadly.

You cannot see it because you aren’t paying close attention, but from what I can see, she has an incredibly solid foundation—so solid that killing you would be as simple as a single swing of her sword."
"This..." Meiko was left speechless, her expression faltering as she glared at Ruby, who wore a smug expression on her face...
"You... How come you are stronger than me now?" Meiko asked.

Ruby knew her chance to brag had come, and she took it. "Unlike you, who couldn’t handle a few bugs and died like a lizard, I fought to the end, killing as many Flame Demons as I could. After we managed to close the Flame Gate, I left for Amon’s Guillotine Cave, and for the last couple of eras, I have been tempering my swordsmanship there.
So while you’ve been dead, I have been training, waiting for the day I could get my hands on you again. Who knew you would turn out to be such a disappointment?"
Meiko gritted her teeth, not liking the fact that her frenemy had become more powerful than she was. Even more annoying, she now had to train and try to catch up to her.
"Damn it."
Ruby laughed, causing Meiko to glare hatefully at her...

"Relax, Meiko. Once Kent awakens your true name, you will gain the power to contend with her." Vexthra consoled her sister, who nodded but still hated the fact that Ruby, her rival back when they both served under the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, was now stronger than her.
"I have to ask, though, how are you still alive? The last I heard, you died like a bug, so how are you standing before me now?" Ruby asked.
"How else, if not because of Fjorge?" Meiko replied, losing the enthusiasm and vigour she had displayed a few minutes ago.
Ruby, however, widened her eyes when she heard her reply. "Are you saying the Leader is still alive?"
"Yes. He is alive, just not available at the moment."
Ruby’s eyelids trembled for a few seconds, then tears started rolling down her face. "Leader is alive... He is alive."
"Yes, he is alive, bitch, and all of us are his wives." Meiko smirked. "Welcome to the tower."
She teleported away and appeared in one of the training halls. Now that she knew she was much weaker than Ruby, Meiko wanted to train and keep training until she caught up to her.
Ruby, however, was surrounded by some of Kent’s wives, knowing she needed attention right now. On the other hand, some of the ladies teleported to the Harem Tower with Safira’s still-passed-out body.
They bathed her and allowed her to rest for now. When she woke up, they would explain everything to her.
Kent still hadn’t woken up from the event that happened when he read the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual.
But he was closer to waking up.

Five days later, he woke up feeling as though his soul had been shredded and stitched back together again. It was the same feeling he had experienced when he read the name of the person whose very existence threatened existence itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 1861: Fated
paragraphs: "What happened?" Kent asked the moment he opened his eyes.
Lady Kenzie turned to Fiannarel, who had been with her when he woke up. While she stayed because she is literally Kent’s life spirit, Fiannarel came because she wanted to be with her brother.
Fiannarel nodded to Lady Kenzie, who then told Kent what had happened.
By the time she was done, Kent had managed to piece together his memories of the events that had transpired when he read the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual.
"So that was what happened, huh?" He took a deep breath, summoned the manual again, and flipped it open only to see an almost empty page.
The only writings available were of some runes that, when he examined them, pointed to a technique linked to cultivating killing intent.
The word he had said that led to him going unconscious was no more, and the other pages were locked, so he had no way of knowing what or whose name it had been in the first place.
"I’d better be careful next time, or I might just die inheriting my own legacy," he sighed and turned to Lady Kenzie.
"Thank you for taking care of me, my dear. You have done an amazing job."
She smiled and nodded. "If you need something else, let me know immediately."
"I sure will."

She vanished back into his soul sea, leaving only Kent and Fiannarel in the room. He stood up from the healing pod and walked into the bathroom. A few minutes later, he came out looking more refreshed.
"You scared me, little brother," Fiannarel said, hugging Kent.
Aside from her, Lady Kenzie, Tower, and Hades, none of his wives knew he had come this close to death. This decision was reached because Tower saw no reason to scare them.
They were having so much fun, so she allowed them to be.

So instead of revealing the truth, she merely told them Kent was tired from training and had decided to sleep for a while. Of course, the ladies knew there was more to it, but since nothing alarming had happened to the tower, they accepted her excuse.
As for Fiannarel, she came to check on Kent every now and then, this time waiting for him to wake up.𝘧𝓇ℯ𝑒𝓌𝑒𝑏𝓃𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘭.𝒸ℴ𝓂

"I am fine, big sister. It was just that I tried to bite off more than I could chew." He smiled, and holding Fiannarel’s hand, they walked out of the healing chamber and onto the vast world inside the Soul Tower, where cultivating the soul was less stressful.
"Don’t scare me like that again, or else I will kill you myself."
Kent laughed and nodded, allowing Fiannarel to rest her head on his shoulder as they stood on a cliff overlooking the vastness below them.
"I have some business on the outside that will take a couple of months, perhaps a year. Once it’s handled, we can go look for Mother and the others."
"Really?" Fiannarel asked, turning to look at Kent.

"Yes. I wasn’t really up for that family reunion before, but my wives seem to like the idea of meeting my past-life families, so since I want them to be happy, I wouldn’t mind exploring the Celestial Realm with you."
"That would be great, little brother. It would be like a field trip... the one we never got to go on back then."
Kent nodded. "Exactly. I can finally make it up to you."
Fiannarel had no reason to say no to that, so she rested her head back on his shoulder and hugged his arm. They stood in that posture for a couple of hours, talking about other things.
Eventually, they were forced to part when Tower arrived with a report.
"Big Brother, Lady Inaya has returned from Amon’s Guillotine Cave with the package."
"Tower, her name is Safira... and what do you mean by package?" Kent couldn’t hold back his laughter.
Tower, however, smiled and nodded, taking note.
"You know what? You can say whatever you want as long as it makes you happy."
Kent turned to Fiannarel and said, "Big sister, I am leaving now. Don’t miss me too much."
"I am coming with you," Fiannarel stated, not attempting to mask her desire.
"This is a private reunion between old acquaintance... so I think you are not welcome."

"Who said I am coming with you to meet the Forsaken Seer? In case you are not aware, your wives are like sisters to me, so I couldn’t care less about your business. I am coming with you to meet them."
Kent smirked. "Well, that was before. Now, the Harem Tower is off-limits to you... Isn’t that right, Tower?"
"Well, Big Brother, your wives gave me a strict warning never to block Big Sister Fiannarel from coming here, so maybe don’t drag me into your siblings’ squabbles."
The tower was gone before Kent could pull on her tiny elven ear.
Seeing this, Fiannarel laughed.
Kent chuckled. "Better stay away from Selene before she pollutes your mind. I have no plans on spreading your legs."
Fiannarel smirked and whispered into his ear, "That’s the thing, little brother. She is my favorite among your wives. And one more thing—we have different parents now, so technically, we are not..."
Kent was gone before she could finish her sentence.
Fiannarel laughed and also vanished from the Soul Temple.
Kent arrived before the Love House, where Safira was still asleep.
He walked in and, seeing the familiar pale-white beauty who had saved him back then and nurtured him back to life, the hatred he felt for most Forsaken beings surprisingly vanished from his heart.
This caused him to halt, his eyelids trembling slightly. He tried to summon that hatred, but for reasons he couldn’t explain, he couldn’t.
It had completely vanished from his heart, mind and soul.
Instead, watching her sleep with a much thinner body than he remembered, he felt his heart break.
’She might have suffered so much because of me.’
Without even knowing how, tears started falling down his face. Seeing this, Vexthra and Elaine, who were with Safira, teleported away to give him some space.

Kent walked to the bed and sat down. Then, lifting Safira’s head, he placed it on his lap and hugged her, his tears falling onto her chest, which was only covered by a thin cloth shielding her nipples.
He had no idea why he was crying.
But amid the tears and embraces, Safira opened her eyes and began to tear up, too.
Seated somewhere far away, Fate smiled, watching the reunion that had been in the works since the dawn of the universe.
