"I’d better be careful next time, or I might just die inheriting my own legacy," he sighed and turned to Lady Kenzie.
"Thank you for taking care of me, my dear.
You have done an amazing job."
She smiled and nodded.
"If you need something else, let me know immediately."
"I sure will."
She vanished back into his soul sea, leaving only Kent and Fiannarel in the room.
He stood up from the healing pod and walked into the bathroom.
A few minutes later, he came out looking more refreshed.
"You scared me, little brother," Fiannarel said, hugging Kent.
Aside from her, Lady Kenzie, Tower, and Hades, none of his wives knew he had come this close to death.
This decision was reached because Tower saw no reason to scare them.
They were having so much fun, so she allowed them to be.
So instead of revealing the truth, she merely told them Kent was tired from training and had decided to sleep for a while.
Of course, the ladies knew there was more to it, but since nothing alarming had happened to the tower, they accepted her excuse.
As for Fiannarel, she came to check on Kent every now and then, this time waiting for him to wake up.𝘧𝓇ℯ𝑒𝓌𝑒𝑏𝓃𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘭.𝒸ℴ𝓂
"I am fine, big sister.

It was just that I tried to bite off more than I could chew." He smiled, and holding Fiannarel’s hand, they walked out of the healing chamber and onto the vast world inside the Soul Tower, where cultivating the soul was less stressful.
"Don’t scare me like that again, or else I will kill you myself."
Kent laughed and nodded, allowing Fiannarel to rest her head on his shoulder as they stood on a cliff overlooking the vastness below them.
"I have some business on the outside that will take a couple of months, perhaps a year.
Once it’s handled, we can go look for Mother and the others."
"Really?" Fiannarel asked, turning to look at Kent.
"Yes.

I wasn’t really up for that family reunion before, but my wives seem to like the idea of meeting my past-life families, so since I want them to be happy, I wouldn’t mind exploring the Celestial Realm with you."
"That would be great, little brother.
It would be like a field trip... the one we never got to go on back then."
Kent nodded.
"Exactly.
I can finally make it up to you."
Fiannarel had no reason to say no to that, so she rested her head back on his shoulder and hugged his arm.
They stood in that posture for a couple of hours, talking about other things.
Eventually, they were forced to part when Tower arrived with a report.
"Big Brother, Lady Inaya has returned from Amon’s Guillotine Cave with the package."
"Tower, her name is Safira... and what do you mean by package?" Kent couldn’t hold back his laughter.
Tower, however, smiled and nodded, taking note.
"You know what?
You can say whatever you want as long as it makes you happy."
Kent turned to Fiannarel and said, "Big sister, I am leaving now.
Don’t miss me too much."
"I am coming with you," Fiannarel stated, not attempting to mask her desire.
"This is a private reunion between old acquaintance... so I think you are not welcome."
"Who said I am coming with you to meet the Forsaken Seer?
In case you are not aware, your wives are like sisters to me, so I couldn’t care less about your business.
I am coming with you to meet them."
Kent smirked.
"Well, that was before.
Now, the Harem Tower is off-limits to you...
Isn’t that right, Tower?"
"Well, Big Brother, your wives gave me a strict warning never to block Big Sister Fiannarel from coming here, so maybe don’t drag me into your siblings’ squabbles."
The tower was gone before Kent could pull on her tiny elven ear.
Seeing this, Fiannarel laughed.
Kent chuckled.
"Better stay away from Selene before she pollutes your mind.
I have no plans on spreading your legs."
Fiannarel smirked and whispered into his ear, "That’s the thing, little brother.
She is my favorite among your wives.
And one more thing—we have different parents now, so technically, we are not..."
Kent was gone before she could finish her sentence.
Fiannarel laughed and also vanished from the Soul Temple.
Kent arrived before the Love House, where Safira was still asleep.
He walked in and, seeing the familiar pale-white beauty who had saved him back then and nurtured him back to life, the hatred he felt for most Forsaken beings surprisingly vanished from his heart.
This caused him to halt, his eyelids trembling slightly.
He tried to summon that hatred, but for reasons he couldn’t explain, he couldn’t.
It had completely vanished from his heart, mind and soul.
Instead, watching her sleep with a much thinner body than he remembered, he felt his heart break.
’She might have suffered so much because of me.’
Without even knowing how, tears started falling down his face.
Seeing this, Vexthra and Elaine, who were with Safira, teleported away to give him some space.
Kent walked to the bed and sat down.
Then, lifting Safira’s head, he placed it on his lap and hugged her, his tears falling onto her chest, which was only covered by a thin cloth shielding her nipples.
He had no idea why he was crying.
But amid the tears and embraces, Safira opened her eyes and began to tear up, too.
Seated somewhere far away, Fate smiled, watching the reunion that had been in the works since the dawn of the universe.

chapters.title: Chapter 1862: How Are You
paragraphs: There are some events in history that aren’t meant to happen, not even with Fate’s intervention.
One such event was the Primordial Chaos Dragon meeting a Forsaken being and, instead of killing each other, one sacrificing everything to save the other.

The funny part was that even after everything that had happened, which ultimately landed her in the most dreadful place anyone could ever dream of going, she never once blamed or regretted saving Chaos.
Over the years, she had lived on the edge, not knowing when death would come for her. Safira asked herself many times whether or not she would do what she did again if she were sent back in time.
Every time, her answer was yes.
She wouldn’t hesitate.
This meant she had no regrets.
On the other side, while he could put everything down to repaying a debt, Chaos also never once thought that ne day he would spare the life of a forsaken being.
His hatred for the Forsaken race at that moment was so great that he wouldn’t spare even a single soul from that race.
But not killing Safira hadn’t pained him, not even for a moment.
He could have said he spared her only because she had saved him. But that thought never crossed his mind, which, now that he thought about it, was unusual for him.
However, while neither of them knew it at the time, they had done something even Fate was not prepared for.
They defied Fate, which, now that things had become clear, pointed to a contingency that had saved Kent from the Primordial Era to this very moment.
By Safira saving Kent and him not killing her, they broke Fate, changing the trajectory of both their lives for thirteen whole eras.
In Kent’s case, he survived his heart demon simply because his fate wasn’t complete. As for Safira, she had spent the last thirteen eras surviving one harrowing danger after another.
Maybe seeing how lean she had become, Kent couldn’t hold back his tears. And Safira, seeing the person who was the sole reason she had lived and never given up all these years, also teared up.
On the outside, Kent’s wives, unable to contain their curiosity, asked Tower to project what was happening inside so they could all see. Before long, every one of them had tears in their eyes.

They had learned from Ruby that Safira hadn’t had it easy inside Amon’s Guillotine Cave. Ruby had lived inside the Blood Variant Pool for eras, and while she had no business entering the Green Variant Pool, she had seen Safira before.
Back then, Safira had been doing her best to escape from three Supremes, her body covered in grave wounds.
The second time Ruby saw her, she was barely clinging to life as she fled from her pursuers.
Learning all this and seeing how malnourished and unkempt she had become when Inaya brought her back, they wished with every fibre of their being that Kent would be good to her.
Even if he hated Forsaken beings, Safira shouldn’t be one of them.
So, seeing him break down and emotionally reveal what he truly felt deep within, none of them could hold back their tears.
Elina, whose death had sparked the slaughter campaign Chaos embarked upon, stood with trembling eyes as she watched what could be considered the beginning of something beautiful.
Maybe, and this is a big maybe, Kent could finally make peace with her death and do away with his bitterness, one that had already caused enough damage to both himself and the people around him.
Tower stopped the projection when she deemed it was enough for now.
Meanwhile, inside the Love House, Kent held Safira in his arms for a couple of minutes before he reached forward and wiped her tears away.
Then, leaning down, he planted a kiss on her forehead.
Safira opened her beautiful green eyes, meeting Kent’s. So much was said in that single moment of eye contact.
Safira raised her trembling hand and gently brushed her fingers across his cheek. Deep within her eyes, Kent saw that she wanted to say something, but the words never reached her lips.
He kissed her forehead again and asked in a calm tone, "How are you, Safira?"
Hearing Kent call her name, her body trembled. In her heart, she felt happy that Kent could still remember her name.
"I am fine... now."
"That is good." Kent smiled faintly and wiped the tears from her eyes.

"I can say a lot of emotional things and make all kinds of generous gestures just to tell you how sorry I am. However, we both know that what you have been through can’t be undone with a mere apology.
"But we can start somewhere and work our way toward making sure the next eternity is the best you will ever experience."
Safira’s eyelids trembled slightly, and she nodded before burying her face in Kent’s lap.

Kent brushed her hair while taking a deep breath. He clearly wasn’t looking forward to this emotional reunion. He had only expected to meet Safira and have whatever she had unintentionally taken from him returned to him.
He had no idea today would turn out to be the day he would hold a Forsaken being in his arms and weep because of how much she had suffered.
When Kent had described Safira to Inaya, he hadn’t exaggerated by saying she had a body to die for. She truly was curvy, and that alone spoke volumes about her beauty.
But she had lost so much weight that, as he looked at her now, even despite possessing the cultivation of a Universal God, she looked malnourished.
That was how much she had suffered.
And that was what broke Kent.
She was banished because of him, so he feels guilty for what happened to her.
He didn’t know what he had to do to get his fate back.

But he didn’t even think about it, because right now, he was simply happy that she had returned to the universe in one piece. And she would forever remain by his side, even if the entire universe rejected her.
Kent continued to hold Safira when, suddenly, a message appeared before his eyes, causing him to smirk.
[A part of your fate is linked to Safira. To get it back, you must get to know her and build a strong bond with her. Only then can you restore your fate to 100%.]
[Current Bond: 15%]

chapters.title: Chapter 1863: Forsaken Race History
paragraphs: Creating a solid, unbreakable bond is something Kent is rather good at. He understands people more than one would wish they could fathom.
Maybe it had to do with his many lives and experiences. But when it comes to understanding people, he is very good at it, especially when he draws on his life as Kevin Sage.
That life had been one deep mind game where he had the choice to trust or kill. He had never once made a bad call, for he had a good read on people.
Safira is a Forsaken being, a natural enemy of the Primordial Chaos Dragon. However, looking at her right now, Kent could tell with certainty that she isn’t someone he can bring himself to hate.
Maybe his feelings are being influenced by the fact that he had a past with Safira, one where she helped him and, in turn, suffered for it.
Maybe he feels sorry for her, and so he feels like he could trust her.
But even if both reasons were valid, the point is that Kent feels like he could trust Safira. Due to that feeling, he also knew that creating a bond with her wouldn’t be too hard.
The question, however, is whether Kent is willing to completely trust a being from the Forsaken race, someone who is a natural enemy of the universe and, by extension, Kent’s mortal enemy.
The answer is yes.
He really wanted to because even if getting his fate back isn’t his main priority, making his wives happy is reason enough.

They hadn’t said anything, but he could tell they weren’t all in favour of how he hated the Forsaken race. Maybe they knew something he didn’t, and if that was the case, then he could at least compromise and allow them to justify why they didn’t want him to continue his slaughter campaign against the Forsaken race.
One could even argue and say Kent had already done enough damage to the Forsaken race, and that statement would be valid.
During the Primordial Era, when he was hunting them down, it got to a point where the Forsaken race started pleading with him to spare their lives.

Initially, they thought they could overpower him, but that proved futile soon after. They lacked the confidence to continue to fight him, so they started to run, some pleading for a chance to live on.
But Chaos never batted an eye, killing all he encountered and hunting them down until his wake-up call when he met Dia and developed a heart demon.
So maybe he had already gotten his revenge.

But Chaos would be a bastard if he believed, even for once, that the Forsaken race was an innocent bunch. They were far from it, and that is why getting to know Safira would finally clear the air for him.
Kent shifted his body and placed one leg on the bed. Then, pulling Safira closer, he let her rest on his chest. Kent placed both hands on her shoulders and hugged her.

"Thank you for saving my life back then, Safira. Had it not been for you, I would have died, and the universe would have perished with me. So thank you for saving me and, by extension, saving the universe too."
She smiled and nodded.

"That said, I would like to know why you saved me. Don’t get me wrong, I appreciate you saving me. It’s just that back then, I was the number one most hated being in your race, so why did you go against your hatred for me and save my life instead?"
Safira sighed. Then she turned her head slightly and looked at Kent.
"That was because I never hated you to begin with. I don’t know how you see Forsaken beings, but not all of us are bad."
Kent knew better than to say anything since Safira was about to open up.
"To the rest of the universe’s races, all Forsaken beings are evil. However, that shouldn’t be the case, not when there are three different tribes that make up the Forsaken race.

We have the Forsaken Blood Tribe, ruled by the Sinister Blood Elder. Then there is the Forsaken Bone Tribe, ruled by the White Skull Elder, and the Forsaken Snow Tribe, ruled by the Snow Maiden Elder.
All three of us are Forsaken beings, but the Forsaken Snow Tribe is a peaceful tribe, mainly because our leader has no interest in attacking your kind.

We never sought animosity with your kind, nor did we ever try to take over your planets. We love peace above all else. However, the same cannot be said for the Forsaken Blood Tribe and the Forsaken Bone Tribe.
They are violent, and they were the main enemy you should have attacked. The ones who offended you were the Forsaken Blood Tribe. However, you didn’t know that, and so you attacked all of us.
Many in my tribe really wanted you dead, but against all odds, my leader prevented us from doing that. In the end, thousands died by your hands.
When I found you barely conscious in the snow back then, I had every reason to kill you, but I didn’t. Not because I was weak, but because I couldn’t bring myself to kill you.
And yes, I paid dearly for it. But at least because of that decision, I can now beg you that, in case you wish to attack the Forsaken race again, spare my Forsaken Snow Tribe.
We didn’t choose to be Forsaken beings, but we chose to seek peace above all else simply because we wished to live in harmony with your kind.
Maybe I am just delusional for thinking the universe can ever align with the Forsaken race. But even if there is a small chance that it can happen, then please, consider my people and spare them."
Kent could only stare back at Safira, regret written all over his face.
As they say, grief really fucks with the head.
He had killed millions of Forsaken beings, believing they were all the same. Thinking about it now, he could tell there was a clear difference between them.
After all, some fought back, while others surrendered, pleading for their lives and those of their loved ones.
But he never listened.

chapters.title: Chapter 1864: Regret
paragraphs: A wise man once said, "Everyone believes they are in the right until they hear the other side of the story."
They had killed his best friend and someone he loved, and so Chaos saw all Forsaken beings as evil. So he attacked, and he killed, and kept killing until he had to stop and handle other matters.
Afterwards, while he had no memories of his life as Chaos during his subsequent incarnations, that hatred was still there, and so whenever he met a Forsaken being, they died.
He believed he was right to kill all Forsaken beings.
But the narrative had changed now, and Kent, while he could still choose to believe he was justified in killing the Forsaken beings, knew he had made a blunder.
Forsaken beings, in truth, are considered evil because they chose to side with corruption, becoming existences that defy the order of the universe. So, in a sense, they are all bad.
But from the way Safira spoke, not all of them had succumbed to corruption. The Forsaken Snow Tribe hadn’t succumbed, but he didn’t know that, and so he killed without holding back.
Now, he knew he had fucked up, and that realization alone seemed to eat away at his sanity.
"It is not your fault, Chaos. You merely wanted revenge, and to be honest, there were many like you who came before you but died. You surviving is already a miracle."
That was indeed true.
Kent might not know it yet, but the Forsaken race wasn’t weak at all.

Whoever corrupted them had granted them a power capable of threatening the universe. The only reason they never succeeded was that the universe itself was fighting back, holding back the greatest dangers that could have threatened everyone.

Chaos was merely a weapon that the Forsaken race never saw coming. Their main enemy—the universe—had prevented them from dealing with him. But by becoming someone who had killed a great number of them, he had become their enemy.
What they never expected was what came next.
Chaos might have been brave enough to take on an entire race. However, in the background, thousands more wanted a piece of the Forsaken race.
One of them was Arien’s incarnation.
She was someone who had harnessed the chaos unleashed by the Primordial Chaos Dragon to trap the Forsaken race for good. She didn’t have the power to kill them, but she managed to imprison them.
So while Chaos killed, she sealed them, protecting all life from the corruption and infestation of the Forsaken race.

When Chaos stopped his assaults, she finally revealed her hand and did what should have been done many years before. She stopped the Forsaken race from invading any more worlds, and that was how the Forsaken race was finally defeated.
But were they really defeated...
The answer can only be given by the one person who knew the secrets of the forsaken race...Safira
"Tell me more about your Forsaken Snow Tribe."
"We are just like all other forsaken beings, but you can differentiate us by the color of our hair and horns. We have two distinct colors - blue and green.
The dominant color is blue. However, those with a much stronger bloodline possess green. We or all forsaken beings had existence since the time of the Six True Primordials..."

Kent furrowed his brow, hearing the mention of the six true primordials. He is the seventh True Primordial, but he wasn’t born with the other six. Hearing about them is a bit unexpected but also interesting.

"Even before you rose to fame, the forsaken race had the power to take over the entire universe. The only hindrance was the fact that the universe held us back. But aside from that, my leader also stood in the way of the other two tribes.

Dia’s awakening began...

chapters.title: Chapter 1865: Power of a Heart Demon
paragraphs: Kent had already been made aware that the day his fate was complete, the heart demon that had plagued him his entire life would finally be purged.
That heart demon had been Dia all along.
She first revealed herself during the Primordial Era, and she had followed him throughout his 13 lives. So he knew that with Safira back, it was only a matter of time before things happened.
What he never expected, however, was the sudden awakening that took form in Dia the moment the Bond Meter struck 100% and his fate was restored.
The moment Kent’s fate was restored, the power that had been planted inside her, turning her into a heart demon for Kent, awakened, and she had to fight to defeat it or be defeated by it.

Dia may have already suspected something like this would happen, so she had been preparing diligently, waiting for the insidious power that took her free will from her, turning her into a weapon that nearly claimed the life of the saviour of the universe.
At the moment, inside the Harem Tower, a large cocoon reeking of soul energy so dark and corrupted that when Kent and Safira arrived, they were both taken aback by it.
Safira was left rather shocked because she recognised the energy emanating from the cocoon.𝕗𝗿𝕖𝐞𝐰𝗲𝕓𝐧𝕠𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝐨𝚖
"This energy is similar to the Founders," she muttered, holding Kent’s hand.
"The Founders? You are talking about the beings who turned your kind into a forsaken race? Those who went into contract with the unknown beings?"
"Yes."
Safira, over the two months she spent with Kent, had revealed chilling details about her race that made Kent question many things he knew about the universe.
Apparently, the forsaken race had three ancestors known as the Founders. They were still alive, but from what she had been told, they were not within this universe.
Kent was already aware of the Primordial Chaos, so he knew they were there, just like many ancient powerhouses that this universe couldn’t contain anymore.
He had met a few during his 13 reincarnations.

However, from what Safira said, if they were indeed the Founders of the forsaken race, then in the near future, they would return, and when they did, he would have to fight them, at least two of them.
Hearing that the power they commanded was now coming from Dia’s cocoon told Kent two things.
First, either they had a hand in turning Dia into a heart demon to infect him, or they did not.
They had every reason to harm him, after all. He was hunting down their people, slaughtering them, so killing him was the most logical path they could take.

So they may have infected Dia since they couldn’t kill him personally, and she, in turn, infected Chaos. What they never accounted for was that Chaos had an incomplete fate, and so their plans failed.
But for some reason, Kent doubted they were responsible.
He reached this conclusion because when they first learned that Dia had no fate or destiny, since it had been stolen from her, Gaia stopped them from finding out who was responsible.
She warned them that discovering the truth would end in their deaths.
He had learned about the Founders’ existence, yet he didn’t even feel a thing, not even a death threat.

This meant the second possibility was that the same people who corrupted the forsaken race were responsible for Dia becoming a heart demon. That meant they were aware of Kent’s existence and that they knew he was the Chaos Ascension King.
This told Kent he was dealing with beings far more dreadful than any horror he had faced so far.
If they were indeed the ones responsible, then he knew Dia was in for a rough time; perhaps she might not survive this.

Not that he had any plan to watch her die. Kent had also been preparing for this very moment, for he knew that if he wanted answers about why he had been targeted, he had to make sure Dia survived this.
"Give me a minute, Safira."
Kent walked toward the cocoon, surrounded by his wives, who were all rooting for Dia to come out as the winner.
"Relax, ladies. She will be fine."
Maybe if this had been before he started inheriting the legacy of the Chaos Ascension King, he wouldn’t have sounded so calm. But things were different now.
"But you all might want to step back a couple of meters, perhaps a kilometer if you don’t want to pass out and miss out on all the fun."
Some of them blinked, wondering if Kent possessed the power to force them to pass out. The answer was yes, so they didn’t argue, each flying back.
"Hmmmm."
Kent took a deep breath, and then he closed his eyes. When he snapped them open, thousands of eyes snapped open behind him, each exuding intense killing intent.

At once, the color in the air was drained, and the bone-chilling killing intent filling the space around Kent started to congregate at one point. It took a few seconds, but then all the killing intent in the air formed into a ball of colorless energy.
Kent gestured forward, and it transformed into a small bracelet. Then, harnessing the power of evil qi, he thrust his hand into the cocoon and placed the bracelet on Dia’s arm.
He teleported away immediately, and the next second, a bone-chilling corrupted qi mixed with soul qi exploded out of the cocoon. The entire Harem Tower trembled under the weight of what was coming.
"Oh, this will be fun," Kent smiled, watching as the cocoon started to struggle against something. He, of course, knew what that thing was, but he allowed himself to experience it all over again.

Suddenly, a large strand of pale white hair shot out of the cocoon, taking the form of a sword. The moment the first strand burst out, more followed, piercing the cocoon, each filled with intense killing intent.
The cocoon, almost as if it were a sentient being, struggled against the overwhelming attacks of the Hair Domain Dia had cultivated during the Divine Era.
Perhaps it had been given to her by the beings who turned her into a heart demon. They gave her that much power to alter the life of the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
However, today she was reclaiming that power, finally accepting her nature as a heart demon...

chapters.title: Chapter 1866: Dia’s Rebirth
paragraphs: Someone without fate or destiny isn’t meant to wield the power of an Overlord.

The Fateless are beings lost in the dust of power and struggle. They are meant to be controlled by someone or something. The moment they try to claim their own destiny, they are considered to have defied the natural order of things.
Dia is both Fateless and Destinyless, meaning that even if she wishes to reclaim her fate, she has no fate to rely on, leaving her a lost soul.
That is, if she even has a soul to begin with.
Her entire existence depended on someone, and that person was Kent. She lived because of Kent. She was his heart demon, and that alone was more than one could fathom.
One’s entire existence relies on a single soul...
But she wasn’t anymore, and that meant she was destined to die. One without fate and destiny, having lost their master (Kent), cannot live anymore...
But the one who transformed her into a heart demon forgot one major thing... they took away her destiny, leaving her with nothing.
In a sense, she was someone lost to everything and nothing.
She couldn’t die, not even if she wanted to. Unless, of course, she allowed the person who had made her into the heart demon to take over her mind, soul, and body.
That also revealed the second problem.

Dia had something worth living for. She had her sisters, and she had Kent, so to hell with allowing her soul to be taken over. She would fight, and thus she fought, pouring everything into the battle.
Before Kent’s intervention, she had been suppressed inside her soul sea by a version of herself that had succumbed to the corruption, becoming a corrupted heart demon.
However, things were reversed now. She stood there, looking at the mangled body of her corrupted self, a part of her saddened that she had been corrupted against her free will.
However, she wasn’t about to show sympathy and release this version of her.𝒻𝑟ℯℯ𝑤𝑒𝑏𝑛𝘰𝓋𝑒𝓁.𝒸𝑜𝘮
The problem, however, was that she couldn’t kill her either. She had tried but failed, leaving her with limited options... perhaps no options at all.
Suddenly, however, she narrowed her eyes as a portal formed, and a young white-haired man walked out, holding a white apple.
"Oh my, what do we have here... a Fateless, huh?" The white-haired man smiled and stopped beside the mangled and bound body of the corrupted heart demon.
Dia narrowed her eyes at the white-haired man and asked, "Who are you, and how did you get inside my soul sea?"
She knew that for someone to do something like that, they had to be unimaginably powerful. Not even Kent had the means to do so, which was why he could only aid her from the outside.
But this white-haired young man had just walked into her soul sea as though it were the most natural thing in the world...
"Oh, pardon my rudeness. I find it normal to go anywhere I want, so I forgot about privacy." He smiled and introduced himself. "You can call me the Paragon of the Nine Stars. Pleasure meeting you."

Dia narrowed her eyes even further, trying to remember if she had encountered someone with that name during the 13 lives she had lived. She came up empty, though she seemed to recall Kent mentioning the name before.
Thus, she asked, "You wouldn’t happen to know the Primordial Chaos Dragon, would you?"
"Oh, him? We go way back, you see. He is the third most handsome person in all of the multiverse, after all, so we know each other pretty well."
Dia frowned, clearly not expecting to hear such a response.
She had only wanted to find out whether Kent knew the Paragon, but the latter had to make sure she knew that her man ranked third on the list of the most handsome men in the multiverse.
Out of curiosity, Dia asked, "Who are the second and first most handsome, then?"

Paragon laughed. "Inasmuch as I would love to take the crown, I rank second. The first position goes to a friend of ours. He’s one rude motherfucker, but good-looking. Many don’t even hate him because of his good looks...ah, I hate redhead men the most."
Dia could only sigh, knowing there were clearly levels of shamelessness, and this bastard had long since graduated...
"Then why are you here?"

"Why else, if not to save your life?" Paragon gestured forward as the apple flew from his hand and landed in Dia’s palm. "A very long time ago, the Primordial Chaos Dragon asked me for a favor, and today I’m delivering what he wanted you to have.
Eat it, and you will know what to do. Until then, see you, and say hi to Kent for me."
Paragon was gone just as suddenly as he had come. Dia was left stunned, staring at the apple in her palm.
She was both stunned and shaken that Kent had already made plans for today. Maybe she had been worried for nothing after all.
Then again, she had no reason to doubt someone who seemed to know her man and even seemed like the type who would mess with the natural order of things for his own amusement.
So she bit into the apple, then took a second bite. Before she knew it, she had consumed the entire apple, and that was when clarity set in.
She formed a series of hand seals and pointed at the mangled body of the corrupted heart demon. A small black hole formed at her fingertips, and then it started devouring the corrupted heart demon.
On the outside, the cocoon that had been riddled with thousands of hair-like stabs started to crack and dissolve. In no time, everyone could tell that the moment for Dia to emerge had come.
Within five minutes, the cocoon was gone, and what remained was a cocoon of hair radiating a power that made Kent furrow his brow.
"She will be coming out as a completely different person."
Three days later, she did.
The hair cocoon exploded open, and a woman with long, wavy silver hair appeared, walking barefoot, her body covered in a crimson tunic fashioned from hair-like material.

Every step she took left a crimson lotus on the ground. Of course, the only thing everyone was focused on was her exceptionally long, wavy hair, cascading down her back, sweeping the floor with several strands falling over her shoulders.
Kent smiled, and as he lifted his head, he met Dia’s gaze.
That was when he finally came face-to-face with the person he had wished to have a conversation with.

So she bit into the apple, then took a second bite.
Before she knew it, she had consumed the entire apple, and that was when clarity set in.
She formed a series of hand seals and pointed at the mangled body of the corrupted heart demon.
A small black hole formed at her fingertips, and then it started devouring the corrupted heart demon.
On the outside, the cocoon that had been riddled with thousands of hair-like stabs started to crack and dissolve.
In no time, everyone could tell that the moment for Dia to emerge had come.
Within five minutes, the cocoon was gone, and what remained was a cocoon of hair radiating a power that made Kent furrow his brow.
"She will be coming out as a completely different person."
Three days later, she did.
The hair cocoon exploded open, and a woman with long, wavy silver hair appeared, walking barefoot, her body covered in a crimson tunic fashioned from hair-like material.
Every step she took left a crimson lotus on the ground.
Of course, the only thing everyone was focused on was her exceptionally long, wavy hair, cascading down her back, sweeping the floor with several strands falling over her shoulders.
Kent smiled, and as he lifted his head, he met Dia’s gaze.
That was when he finally came face-to-face with the person he had wished to have a conversation with.

chapters.title: Chapter 1867: Face of Corruption
paragraphs: Kent knew with absolute certainty that if Dia finally managed to break free from the hold the unknown beings had on her, their final play would be to threaten him.
He had seen this play out many times, so he knew they would act.

He was prepared for them, though, for he had no plans to let them go without telling them a piece of his mind. They had messed with Dia’s life and, by extension, his. So they had to understand that when it came to him, nobody was beyond reproach.
Looking into Dia’s eyes solved the issue, though.
They came for him, and so while the others were all staring at her, he seemed to see beyond that.
His body froze on the outside, and his soul vanished from his body and entered a very dark realm, appearing in an eerie space.
He immediately felt his bones tingle the moment he appeared there.
"They always choose the dark and twisted places for their meetings," Kent smirked. "How expected of beings said to be ancient horrors."
The mockery in his tone filled the place, echoing as he spoke.

Suddenly, a pair of green eyes lit up in the darkness, sending waves of bone-chilling feeling through the space. Kent felt his soul tremble; however, he stood his ground, for his soul was far more solid and potent than it used to be.

"You once used to be the most dreadful dragon in all of the Primordial Chaos. Now, look at you. I can kill you with a mere flick of my finger," a rushed and mangled voice spoke, causing the space to tremble.

Kent felt that if this voice had been heard up close, he would have died. Though horrible, he could sense a rather terrible corrupted Dao filled within it. This told him he was dealing with beings far beyond his current level of power.
But he wasn’t weak, nor was he afraid of them.
"Big talk, yet here we are, me standing and you hiding behind darkness." Kent grinned, and as if to test something, he added, "I dare you to show your face and reveal your body."

Of course, his taunt fell on deaf ears, for Kent had already suspected that the person behind the voice couldn’t come face to face with him without triggering something dangerous, even if they wouldn’t dare offend.
But by confirming his suspicion, Kent grew bolder, and so he began to threaten them for real...
"Now, before I tell you how ugly you are, allow me to say this... I am highly disappointed in you bunch. Honestly, beings who created the Forsaken Race could have done better.
In fact, I look down on you. I spit on your graves. I am disappointed in your mother for wasting her time giving birth to useless things such as yourselves.
To kill me, a mere dragon, you had to use a proxy. I mean, what kind of loser even came up with such an idea? Horrors such as yourself could have done better.
I, the Primordial Chaos Dragon, had the power of an entire universe, and you thought a heart demon would be enough to kill me. Honestly, you are all useless at this point.
But I commend you for finally making me see what is beyond my reach. I honestly wouldn’t have gotten to where I am if not for you motivating me to strive and reach higher.
So thank you, losers. Next time, instead of using useless tricks to face me, come against me, and let’s do it face-to-face. I for sure would love to see the face of corruption and spit on it."
A chuckle ended the sentence, leaving the dark space eerily quiet, with a sudden sense of corruption blanketing the place.
They were furious, and they had every right to be.
Kent had gone overboard, and that alone pointed to one thing in particular: they weren’t happy, but they were also powerless.
One could say the reason Kent was so loose with his words was that he knew they could not touch him. As they said, it is harmless to stick your fingers into a fangless tiger.
"I see you feel bold now. Good. One day, when we meet, we shall see who has the last laugh."

Kent laughed, holding his stomach. "Are you sure you are even the masters of corruption? You sound more like an underground artist. If I didn’t know better, I would say you are merely small fries in a very powerful and dreadful game.
Perhaps your master will be a pleasant chat, since the threat you give is just empty."
Kent took a step forward, approaching the green eyes. Of course, he maintained a certain distance so he wouldn’t accidentally wound his soul.

"Allow me to show you how it is done." The smile on his face vanished, and his tone turned cold. "Growing up, there was a certain tribe that drew its power from ashes and smoke. They grew stronger whenever there was fire and thick smoke.

Great guys with a peculiar take on power. However, they were also the worst kind of evil I have ever met. They believed that as long as there was fire, they would never run out, so they didn’t really pay attention to how they killed.
I witnessed them burn an entire city to the ground just because they wanted to have a taste of the smoke they produced. I mean, who does that?"
"Is there a point to this?" the corruption asked, and Kent grinned.
"Oh, but there is. You see, I recently recovered a part of my legacy that allows me to devour, like devour everything and anything. Now, I keep wondering, how would it taste to devour corruption?

Would it taste sour, bitter, or sweet? I do hope it is sweet because, guess what, I will devour every last one of you, and using your power, I will go further and devour everything, including your Forsaken Race.

But fear not. I know you guys are terrified of the Chaos Ascension King. Luckily for you, I am the Primordial Chaos Dragon, the real deal. So when the time comes, and we meet, we will have a proper discussion..." Kent laughed and turned away from the green eyes.
He then turned sideways and said, "On second thought, you should fear me the most."

chapters.title: Chapter 1868: Heart Demon Dao
paragraphs: Kent was back in his body, almost as if he hadn’t just had a conversation with corruption itself. Corruption came in different forms, so he wouldn’t treat it as a single entity.
But he had a nice chat with them, and from what had been said, they would surely come for him one day.
The good part is that Kent was prepared for them.

In fact, he wanted them to come so he could finally put an end to their infestation. He wanted them gone, and since he had finally confirmed they existed, planning how to get rid of them was his next step.
He wasn’t too bothered, though...

For now, he had plans to handle a few things before returning to his training. After reading the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual, he had gained insight into cultivating Killing Intent.

His next objective was to focus on that, since the legacy demanded dedication, and right now, he needed to dedicate his time to making sure he had more pages to read and more of his strength to recover, so he wasn’t about to slack off.
Turning to the side, his gaze landed on Dia, now surrounded by her sisters, every last one of them playing with her hair. That was the most visible part of her, so they all wanted to touch it.

Of course, they were happy for her. After all, she had finally become someone whole. She still had no fate or destiny, but at least her life didn’t depend on Kent, and her power no longer came from corruption.
Kent could tell she had become someone even the universe could not control. She wasn’t in the web of fate, and so her actions could only be dictated by herself.

Such an existence was akin to the Paragon. She had no home, so she could only choose a place to call home. Luckily for her, she had more than enough sisters to keep her sane for now. Luckily, she also seemed happy with her newfound powers.
She may have been corrupted, but now she was herself, and that was what she wanted.
"Congratulations, Dia. I am happy for you," Kent said, approaching her with a warm smile.
Dia turned from her sisters, looked at him, and smiled. "Thank you, dear. I am very happy right now."
Well, she wasn’t wrong about that. She was indeed delighted that she had finally become herself, free from corruption and manipulation by anyone.
"It is good that you are happy. After all, we all deserve happiness one way or the other."

Her sisters allowed her to approach Kent, so Dia did, and when she was close to him, she jumped into his arms, locking lips with his. Kent, of course, had no plans to shy away, so he grabbed her by the butt and started kissing her back.

A couple of minutes later, they separated, and Kent looked her in the eye, still holding her. "You would have to protect your sisters, Dia. You are now someone even I have to be wary of if you were my enemy, so stick by them and make sure they are protected."
Hearing what he said, some of his wives furrowed their brows, wondering why he would say something like this. Sure, Dia was now a Universal God with the power of corruption.
However, there were Supremes, Celestials, Pseudo-Primordials, and a Primordial in the harem. The idea that Kent would be telling Dia to protect them baffled them.
But they soon understood why he said that.
Dia smiled and said, "You are saying this because of him, right? The Paragon."
Kent nodded. "Yes. I can smell that bastard on you. Clearly, he visited you, didn’t he?"
"He did. Although your Killing Intent helped me suppress the corrupted version of me, he was the one who helped me finally get rid of it."
"That is classic him, always taking advantage of every small opening to do something mind-bending." Kent smirked, almost as if he knew the Paragon all too well.

He sure did. After all, he had read how they met in the past and how much the Paragon had helped him. That alone told him what kind of person the Paragon was and what a menace he could be when he wanted to spite the heavens.

"I don’t know how he did it, but he somehow captured a part of corruption, or specifically, Heart Demon Power, and made it into a Dao that only you, in all of existence, can harness. In other words, you now have your own Dao, and since you are Fateless, you can literally do just about anything you want.
Rules and restrictions don’t apply to you anymore, which, from where I stand, makes you the strongest. If you don’t believe me, let’s experiment and see something."
Kent turned toward his sister Fiannarel and said, "Big Sister, you wouldn’t mind if we experimented on you, would you?"
Fiannarel just smirked. "Now you need my help when you tried to block me from coming here."
Kent smiled guiltily. "Don’t be like that, Big Sister."
"Tch, fine, you can experiment on me. But you’ll owe me one."
"I sure will be sure to pay that favor later. For now, lower all defenses around your soul, at least to the level of a Pseudo-Primordial."
Fiannarel said nothing and did as she was told.
Kent turned to Dia and made the most shocking revelation. "Dia, plant a heart demon inside Big Sister Fiannarel’s soul."
"Huh?" Even Fiannarel herself was taken aback by Kent’s request to Dia.
"You know, access your Dao and target her soul. Then plant the heart demon there... And don’t worry, since you have a Dao, you can remove it whenever you want."
Dia took a deep breath, unsure if she could really do what she was being asked without hurting Fiannarel. Luckily for her, Fiannarel was okay with it.
"Go ahead, Dia. I can handle it."
A few minutes later, Fiannarel had become pale, her body shivering. Inside her Soul Sea, an eldritch horror stood facing her, an eerie smile on its face.
On the outside, everyone had gone silent, staring at the strongest among them, now shaking and trembling...
The shocking part was that the one responsible was Dia, a mere Universal God.

chapters.title: Chapter 1869: Forge Master (1)
paragraphs: Every last one of Kent’s wives was shaken to the core as they watched Dia display her abilities for the first time after breaking free from the unknown beings.
They had held supreme authority over her for a very long time.
Finally, she had broken free, and she could use the power that Paragon had helped her obtain, even against a Pseudo-Primordial.𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎

Fiannarel is an Eternal, but Kent made her lower her soul defenses to that of a Pseudo-Primordial, allowing Dia, who had her own Dao, to plant a heart demon inside her soul. This ability isn’t something to be taken lightly.
To be able to infect a Pseudo-Primordial that easily surely had to be considered a very dangerous thing.
Luckily, Dia had a good hold on her abilities, so after making sure Fiannarel experienced just a few minutes of what it feels like to have a heart demon, she removed it.
Fiannarel gasped for breath, dropping to one knee when the heart demon was taken away.
Kent’s wives rushed to her side, making sure she was alright, while some of them stared back at Kent, expecting him to explain some things.
What they had just seen defied common sense, and so they needed an explanation.

"Long story short, Dia had awakened a Dao, and that Dao allows her to harness heart demons on a whim. Now, before you say a Pseudo-Primordial’s soul shouldn’t be easily suppressed by her, you are indeed right; however, you are also wrong since Dia isn’t the same as before.

It is true that a Pseudo-Primordial’s soul is strong, but when affected by a Dao, the soul now has to fight against complex Dao concepts, which those of you who have interacted with Daos before can attest are incredibly powerful."
They nodded, some of them even coming to the realization that they may have been looking at Dia the wrong way...

"Now, consider a situation where someone has their own Dao, meaning they are free to dictate their Dao concepts and make the rules. If such a Dao is used to suppress a soul, do you think the opponent would have an easy time defending against it?

And Dia is not an ordinary person when it comes to harnessing the power of Heart Demons. She had been a Heart Demon for 13 eras. If anything, her accumulated experience is enough for her to even defeat a Primordial.
So rest assured, Dia isn’t the same person you all know. She has become someone whose cultivation base is merely a number used to describe her. Her true power is far more dreadful than that."
They nodded, each finally coming to terms with what they had seen.
It would take some getting used to and a better understanding of how Dao worked before they could finally conclude that Dia may have become the most dangerous among them.
Kent could only smile and watch as his sister returned to her feet.

Though she was still shaken by the heart demon she had faced a few minutes ago, she was an Eternal, so she wasn’t too beaten down. In fact, she seemed remarkably well to have gone through something this dangerous and be back on her feet in the next few seconds.
Kent also knew his wives would spend the next couple of days talking and getting used to Dia’s abilities before they would have time for him.
Vexthra always tries to understand her sisters’ abilities so they can fully integrate them into their combat styles, allowing them to work in synchrony during battles.
So he left them for now. Once they were done, he and Dia would spend some time together to celebrate her victory against the unknown beings.
In the meantime, he left the Harem Tower and returned to the Mountain Garden to meet with Lady Khronisia, who had already been waiting for him for months.
The last time she saw him was when they were on their way to the Blacksmith Association, and they were attacked by the Blood Ancestor.
She had been living inside the tower, and since time runs much faster there, months had already passed.
Of course, years had passed since then, but she spent most of her time in the Tower Cities, where time runs the same as in the outside world.

Those months had only accumulated because she spent most of her time cultivating inside either the cultivation havens within the Tower Cities, where the tower’s time difference applied, or inside the Legion Tower.
Today, however, Tower had informed her to come here since Kent planned to take her back to the outside world and continue their journey.
She needed his help to forge a weapon, and Kent needed her help to finally summon back his unruly hammer, which he had missed a lot...
"It appears a lot of time has passed since we last saw each other," Kent said, smiling at Lady Khronisia, who stood inside the Mountain Garden playing with some birds.
"It appears so," she turned and faced him. "But I had a great time here, which was all thanks to your quick thinking and decisive action back then."
They had indeed come close to death when the Blood Ancestor attacked all of a sudden, so Kent’s saving her was indeed appreciated.
"No need to thank me so much. I nearly got you killed, so accept my apologies, and as I had already promised, I will help you forge one of the deadliest spears the Immortal Realm has ever seen."
Lady Khronisia nodded, allowing a small smile to form on her face.
They left the tower a few minutes later, and after another week of travel, they finally arrived on Planet Flame Haven. It is a planet literally on fire, every part of it lit by red flames.
However, there was no visible heat to worry about.
Kent already knew where the heat was being channeled, but he was still fascinated by the unique nature of this world.
He had recovered his memories as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, and so he knew he had a private world made specifically for forging weapons.
He had unique flame pools and lava seas in that world, but nothing beat an entire planet on fire.
They arrived at the Blacksmith Association and immediately went to work.

Now, before you say a Pseudo-Primordial’s soul shouldn’t be easily suppressed by her, you are indeed right; however, you are also wrong since Dia isn’t the same as before.

It is true that a Pseudo-Primordial’s soul is strong, but when affected by a Dao, the soul now has to fight against complex Dao concepts, which those of you who have interacted with Daos before can attest are incredibly powerful."
They nodded, some of them even coming to the realization that they may have been looking at Dia the wrong way...
"Now, consider a situation where someone has their own Dao, meaning they are free to dictate their Dao concepts and make the rules.
If such a Dao is used to suppress a soul, do you think the opponent would have an easy time defending against it?
And Dia is not an ordinary person when it comes to harnessing the power of Heart Demons.
She had been a Heart Demon for 13 eras.
If anything, her accumulated experience is enough for her to even defeat a Primordial.
So rest assured, Dia isn’t the same person you all know.
She has become someone whose cultivation base is merely a number used to describe her.
Her true power is far more dreadful than that."
They nodded, each finally coming to terms with what they had seen.
It would take some getting used to and a better understanding of how Dao worked before they could finally conclude that Dia may have become the most dangerous among them.
Kent could only smile and watch as his sister returned to her feet.
Though she was still shaken by the heart demon she had faced a few minutes ago, she was an Eternal, so she wasn’t too beaten down.
In fact, she seemed remarkably well to have gone through something this dangerous and be back on her feet in the next few seconds.
Kent also knew his wives would spend the next couple of days talking and getting used to Dia’s abilities before they would have time for him.
Vexthra always tries to understand her sisters’ abilities so they can fully integrate them into their combat styles, allowing them to work in synchrony during battles.
So he left them for now.
Once they were done, he and Dia would spend some time together to celebrate her victory against the unknown beings.
In the meantime, he left the Harem Tower and returned to the Mountain Garden to meet with Lady Khronisia, who had already been waiting for him for months.
The last time she saw him was when they were on their way to the Blacksmith Association, and they were attacked by the Blood Ancestor.
She had been living inside the tower, and since time runs much faster there, months had already passed.
Of course, years had passed since then, but she spent most of her time in the Tower Cities, where time runs the same as in the outside world.

Those months had only accumulated because she spent most of her time cultivating inside either the cultivation havens within the Tower Cities, where the tower’s time difference applied, or inside the Legion Tower.
Today, however, Tower had informed her to come here since Kent planned to take her back to the outside world and continue their journey.
She needed his help to forge a weapon, and Kent needed her help to finally summon back his unruly hammer, which he had missed a lot...
"It appears a lot of time has passed since we last saw each other," Kent said, smiling at Lady Khronisia, who stood inside the Mountain Garden playing with some birds.
"It appears so," she turned and faced him.
"But I had a great time here, which was all thanks to your quick thinking and decisive action back then."
They had indeed come close to death when the Blood Ancestor attacked all of a sudden, so Kent’s saving her was indeed appreciated.
"No need to thank me so much.
I nearly got you killed, so accept my apologies, and as I had already promised, I will help you forge one of the deadliest spears the Immortal Realm has ever seen."
Lady Khronisia nodded, allowing a small smile to form on her face.
They left the tower a few minutes later, and after another week of travel, they finally arrived on Planet Flame Haven.
It is a planet literally on fire, every part of it lit by red flames.
However, there was no visible heat to worry about.
Kent already knew where the heat was being channeled, but he was still fascinated by the unique nature of this world.
He had recovered his memories as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, and so he knew he had a private world made specifically for forging weapons.
He had unique flame pools and lava seas in that world, but nothing beat an entire planet on fire.
They arrived at the Blacksmith Association and immediately went to work.

chapters.title: Chapter 1870: Forge Master (2)
paragraphs: Kent came to assist Lady Khronisia, who had already invited top blacksmiths to witness her final forge as an Immortal Blacksmith.
She would soon ascend to become a God Blacksmith. So she wished to leave her mark in the Immortal Realm, allowing her name to live on for years to come.

Because of this, by the time Lady Khronisia was ready to begin, the forging arena she had selected had already become crowded with all kinds of blacksmiths and powerful figures from the Eastern Region of the Immortal Realm.
Many blacksmiths hoped for a day like this to experience forging at its finest level. So when word spread, they came.
Some came to witness what Lady Khronisia had planned to forge, while others came to observe and learn from her.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦
Of course, the majority came when word spread that Kent Madson was the forge master Lady Khronisia had chosen to assist her.
It was known that Lady Khronisia had been searching for someone who possessed Absolute Named Ice. Many had Absolute Ice, but they didn’t know its true name.

Kent was different. His ice had a true name, and so he was the perfect person she wanted. In the past, when Kent’s name appeared on the Ice Elemental Dao Tablet, many tried to look for him but failed.
They recognized the potential his ice element could bring. So, learning that he would be serving as Lady Khronisia’s assistant left many looking forward to what they could achieve together.
"It has been a while since an event like this was organized. I wonder if this will be the last one for at least a while," some of the spectators started to converse, wondering about many things.
Most had been in the world of blacksmithing for years, so they knew just how events like this usually played out.
"There is no need to get emotional about this. If Lady Khronisia manages to leave her mark as she intends, then I am sure many will follow in her footsteps."
"That would be great. We allowed the world of alchemy to overshadow us for too long. So this is the best time to rise and reclaim the fame we once had during the Flame Era."
Upon hearing the declaration, many straightened up and waited for the event to start.
An hour later, Lady Khronisia walked onto the stage, with Kent following behind her. As they arrived, the noise died down, everyone focusing on what was about to be said before the main event began.
"Thank you all for coming on such short notice," Lady Khronisia said, looking across the gathered crowd.

"I wouldn’t want to waste anyone’s time by saying all kinds of things. I believe my forge today will do more of the talking. However, if what I have in mind today comes to pass, then for the first time in millions of years, the Immortal Realm will finally witness the birth of a Soul-type Immortal Grade Spear, forged using Sacred Flame and True Ice."
Everyone gasped upon hearing what Lady Khronisia had said.
Normally, the flames every blacksmith used were either Soul Flames produced by their own souls or Primordial Flames absorbed after being tamed.
Sacred Flames were a myth to most since they had never seen one.
They knew they existed, but they had never seen one before. To learn that she would be using one today surely came as a shock.
However, everyone soon turned to look at Kent, and suddenly it all made sense.
Still, some questioned her.

"I am not one to be jealous of your gains, Lady Khronisia, but isn’t using Sacred Flame a bit too reckless for such an event? After all, you have never used some before, so what makes you think you can handle it?"
The question was valid, and Lady Khronisia would have worried about it had it not been for what had happened between her and Kent a couple of days ago.

After they arrived at the Blacksmith Association, Kent taught her a flame-control technique and temporarily granted her control over his Nine Nirvana Flames. Since she would be using them, she might as well learn how to control them.
Of course, that alone wasn’t enough, since it takes time and a lot of soul cultivation to harness Sacred Flames to a level where forging with them would be within her reach.
Then again, she had stayed inside the tower for months, allowing Gaia and her minions to prepare her for this very moment.
Her soul was now robust, perhaps already at the level of a Supreme Blacksmith, so she was able to learn the technique and harness the power of the Nine Nirvana Flames in merely two days of practice.
She was smart, and that alone was all there was to know about her.
So, hearing the question, she smiled and answered, "I am sure I can handle it. I wouldn’t be here if I couldn’t handle a Sacred Flame."
Many sighed, some taking her decision as a reckless move driven by a hunger for greatness. But then again, she sounded confident, so they could only wait to see what she had planned.
Because of the revelation that she would be using Sacred Flames, many seemed not to have picked up on the soul-type aspect of the weapon she intended to forge.
Regardless, she was ready to start...
"Today, Kent Madson will be assisting me as my forge master. He has already accepted my proposal, so allow him the respect every forge master deserves."
They all clapped their hands, something they did for all forge masters. They would never be recognized as having helped forge the weapon, since their fame ended with its forging.
Regardless, they were respected by many for their role in history.
Not many blacksmiths needed forge masters, though...
"Since all has been said, then allow me to begin the process." She extended her hand and lit a green flame, instantly covering the space around her.
Turning toward Kent, she nodded.

Kent smiled and snapped his fingers, summoning a sleek golden anvil that caused many to gasp. Kent and Lady Khronisia didn’t seem bothered, as Kent retrieved the materials and the forging process soon began...

chapters.title: Chapter 1871: Eternal Ice Genesis Spear
paragraphs: Before the forging began, Lady Khronisia had selected ten materials to use, one of which was the mineral she had obtained at the auction where she and Kent met.
However, since she would be using the sacred flame for the forging, Kent added two more that he believed would amplify the effects of the other ten materials.
The best part was that Lady Khronisia had thought of the two items and even researched them, but she couldn’t get her hands on them since they are rather rare.
As for how Kent managed to get his hands on them, she didn’t know. But she was happy to have them included in her list of materials to be used.
Kent retrieved the twelve items, each filled with so much energy.
The moment the items were brought out, everyone fell quiet, their focus fixed on what was about to happen. Lady Khronisia summoned the sacred flame and started heating the materials.
Just like in alchemy, she had to work on the materials individually before combining them to achieve what she wanted.

Strangely, compared to the mundane way blacksmiths on Earth forged, cultivation worlds used different methods. Their techniques would be considered impossible, or even godlike, if Earth’s blacksmiths witnessed them.
Regardless, as the materials were heated and then melted if needed, Kent remained at the side, his focus fixed on what was happening before him.
’I miss this,’ he said inwardly, watching as the blacksmith paid close attention to the forging process. In the past, he had competed in many forging duels and won them all.
He had met thousands of blacksmiths and witnessed many amazing techniques.
Watching Lady Khronisia work, he smiled, his mind going back to the person whose bloodline Lady Khronisia came from.

He was one of the most intelligent blacksmiths Kent had ever met. They had competed a few times and even fought on occasion before finally becoming friends, and both ultimately died during the Flame Wars.
Seeing his friend’s descendant forging using techniques he had helped refine left him feeling a little happy. He missed his friend, but he was glad to see his legacy continue.
Time soon passed, and before long, every last material had been melted and poured into the mould. Kent stood back, watching as she worked. Soon, she started hammering the spear into shape.
The technique she was using was one of the best in the Immortal Realm—the Nine-Fold Demon Hammer. It had nine forms, and so far, Lady Khronisia had mastered three of them.
However, with just those three forms, she was proving to everyone that she was worthy of wielding the Nine-Fold Demon Hammer.
One thing that surprised many was the fact that she was able to use the sacred flame as though she had been wielding it for years.
That was the real shocker, and even Kent, who knew this was her first time ever using it, was shaken by how skillfully she handled it during the melting process.
’She will make a good apprentice,’ he said to himself and continued to watch.
Hours passed, and before long, an entire day had gone by, but she was only halfway done.

By now, the spear had taken shape, and she proceeded to the artistry of designing and inscribing runes on it. Basically, she was doing what Kent had offered to do, only this time, she was doing it herself.
Many had their mouths hanging open as they watched her inscribe all kinds of soul runes onto the spear.

"I know it is not my place to question the talent and techniques of an elder from the Pill Association, but fuck it, when did Lady Khronisia learn to inscribe soul runes that fast and effortlessly? I mean, it is one thing to have the talent to draw them, and another to possess a soul strong enough to draw them that fast and flawlessly.
Just what the fuck is going on?"
Many thought the same thing. Some even wondered if this was indeed the Lady Khronisia they knew.

"First was how flawlessly she handled the sacred flame. And now, she is drawing runes as if they are mere words. Even more shocking, she is drawing soul runes, something even God Blacksmiths struggle to do."
"Do you guys think this has something to do with Kent Madson? I mean, his arrival caused all this, so this can be attributed to him."
Focus shifted to Kent briefly, but they all quickly wiped the idea from their minds.
Kent might be monstrous, but even he didn’t possess the ability to possess someone else’s body and draw runes for them. That was just ridiculous.
But since he wasn’t the cause, then there was the issue of where Lady Khronisia had learned to draw runes so easily.

"I think we are all forgetting something... If the rumours are to be trusted, then she comes from a bloodline of legacy blacksmiths. Maybe what she showed us before and what she is showing us now proves that she isn’t simple."
Even Kent couldn’t help but nod at the assumption made by one of the spectators.
Gaia and her minions had helped Lady Khronisia train her soul during her stay in the tower, so that explained her robust soul strength.

However, in terms of talent, everything came from her. Naturally, that told Kent she wasn’t simple at all. Clearly, the legacy within their bloodline had either been inherited by her or was in the process of awakening.
Maybe she had already inherited part of it.

But Kent wasn’t one to pry into other people’s business. All he knew was that, from what Lady Khronisia had shown, she would soon become a sensation that would sweep across the entire Immortal Realm and even the God Realm.
’I only hope she can one day rise to the level of that monster and awaken her true bloodline.’
More time passed, and before long, it had been two days since the forging process began.
Kent had remained on the sidelines for the past two days since his turn hadn’t come yet.
However, on this day, after inscribing thousands of runes onto the spear, Lady Khronisia turned and looked at Kent.
"It is time for you to play your part, Kent Madson."

chapters.title: Chapter 1872: Eternal Ice Genesis Spear (2)
paragraphs: Kent’s only task was to imbue his ice essence into the spear.

Lady Khronisia had already created a core that would act as the heart of the spear. Inside this core, the weapon spirit she had already captured, thanks to the many dungeons inside the Dungeon Tower, would reside.
But before that could be done, she first had to awaken the core. Kent was in charge of that process.
Of course, she could have gone ahead and created an ice core right away. But that would have been unsuitable for a weapon spirit to reside in.

So Kent would have to handle that part since only an Ice Elemental bearing a True Name could create something of that sort. Initially, she had only wanted a spear that could harness the power of the ice element.
But now that she was forging a Soul-type weapon, things had become more complex and better defined. This time, she had to depend on Kent to handle his part well.
"Can I borrow your hammer?" Kent requested, and she handed it over without even bothering to ask why he needed a hammer for such a simple task.
Under normal circumstances, all he had to do was channel his ice essence into the spear, allowing the core to be stimulated and finally accept the coldness.
However, Kent requested a hammer, and that was unexpected.
Still, many wished to know what he had planned.

"You might want to distance yourself for the next part," Kent said before walking two meters away. Lady Khronisia, who had witnessed his battle prowess, moved back, putting another six meters between them.
Once they were both far enough apart, Kent stomped heavily on the ground, and three pillars of ice shot out from the earth, rising into the air. All three remained suspended before him.
He stood there for a few minutes before a smile formed at the corner of his lips.
’Let’s see how long you will remain hidden,’ he smirked.
Then, as the hammer was raised, a thick layer of ice coated it. With a powerful swing, the hammer came crashing down onto one of the ice pillars.

The blow caused a crack to appear in it. The next second, another strike shattered a portion of it. Then, in what could only be described as a flawless display of hammering mastery, Kent unleashed one blow after another.
The audience was left stunned, every last one of them wondering whether what they were witnessing was real.
There was no way they could be seeing an illusion, right?
That was impossible...
"Am I seeing things, or is Kent Madson using the Nine-Fold Demon Hammer technique?"
"He is using it, and flawlessly at that."

Many were left in shock, most wondering if what they were seeing was even real. The fact that Kent was using a technique that many could spend their entire lives without mastering even a single form was simply unbelievable.
Even Lady Khronisia was left stunned.
It had taken her thousands of years to master the first three forms.
However, it had taken Kent just a day or two of watching her to master them.
Naturally, that was impossible.

But then again, this was Kent, someone with talent that couldn’t be put into words. However, while he possessed talent that far surpassed mortal comprehension, his knowledge of this particular technique came from his past life.
The Nine-Fold Demon Hammer was a technique he had helped refine back when he was known as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.

The Lunar Saint Blacksmith was its creator, but back then, the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith was already renowned for possessing one of the greatest collections of hammer techniques, with his most prominent one being the Sixty-Six Hammer Art.
Because of his expertise with the hammer, many sought his assistance in refining their techniques.
The Nine-Fold Demon Hammer was one of the many techniques he had helped create, so using it was as simple as swinging his hammer.
He could use all nine forms flawlessly. But Kent only stuck to the first three forms. Then again, he could have used any other hammer technique he had personally created.

However, for what he had in mind today, he chose to use the Nine-Fold Demon Hammer. Naturally, as the hammer struck the ice pillar, a very deep and complex runic sorcery was taking place, one that nobody present could perceive.𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶
However, somewhere far away in the void, a being with white hair and crimson eyes sat on a throne-like chair, his expression narrowing toward the distance.

His gaze was fixed deep into the void, staring at Kent as he hammered the ice pillars into shape. Perhaps he recognized the technique Kent was using, or perhaps he recognized what Kent was doing, and he didn’t like it.
Regardless, as he continued to watch, the aura around him started to change, taking on a subtle annoyance that could only be discerned from his expression.
Then, just as the three ice pillars were hammered into the shapes of a square, a triangle, and a rectangle, Kent suddenly changed techniques, causing the hammer in his hand to hum.
When that happened, the white-haired man frowned. Then he stood up and, with a single step, vanished from where he had been seated.
Kent looked at the three ice pillars, which had now taken the forms of a square, a triangle, and a rectangle. He smiled, and just before he could strike them one last time, he paused and looked up.
Above him, storm clouds began to gather.
He smiled and turned to Lady Khronisia.
"I am done here. The rest can be handled by you."
He lowered the hammer and then, with a gentle pinch, the three shapes unraveled. They shattered, each transforming into a rune bearing the same shape as they were.
"You can come over when you’re done with everything." Kent said one last time to Lady Khronisia before turning his attention back to the storm cloud.
Looking up, he smiled before shooting forward like a missile and entering the storm that was brewing.
The moment he disappeared into it, the storm vanished. Lady Khronisia looked up for a few moments before sighing and imbuing the runes into the spear.
The storm returned, only this time, it carried the power of heavenly tribulation.

sentences.text: Kent’s only task was to imbue his ice essence into the spear.
Lady Khronisia had already created a core that would act as the heart of the spear.
Inside this core, the weapon spirit she had already captured, thanks to the many dungeons inside the Dungeon Tower, would reside.
But before that could be done, she first had to awaken the core.
Kent was in charge of that process.
Of course, she could have gone ahead and created an ice core right away.
But that would have been unsuitable for a weapon spirit to reside in.
So Kent would have to handle that part since only an Ice Elemental bearing a True Name could create something of that sort.
Initially, she had only wanted a spear that could harness the power of the ice element.
But now that she was forging a Soul-type weapon, things had become more complex and better defined.
This time, she had to depend on Kent to handle his part well.
"Can I borrow your hammer?" Kent requested, and she handed it over without even bothering to ask why he needed a hammer for such a simple task.
Under normal circumstances, all he had to do was channel his ice essence into the spear, allowing the core to be stimulated and finally accept the coldness.
However, Kent requested a hammer, and that was unexpected.
Still, many wished to know what he had planned.
"You might want to distance yourself for the next part," Kent said before walking two meters away.
Lady Khronisia, who had witnessed his battle prowess, moved back, putting another six meters between them.
Once they were both far enough apart, Kent stomped heavily on the ground, and three pillars of ice shot out from the earth, rising into the air.
All three remained suspended before him.
He stood there for a few minutes before a smile formed at the corner of his lips.
’Let’s see how long you will remain hidden,’ he smirked.
Then, as the hammer was raised, a thick layer of ice coated it.
With a powerful swing, the hammer came crashing down onto one of the ice pillars.
The blow caused a crack to appear in it.
The next second, another strike shattered a portion of it.
Then, in what could only be described as a flawless display of hammering mastery, Kent unleashed one blow after another.
The audience was left stunned, every last one of them wondering whether what they were witnessing was real.
There was no way they could be seeing an illusion, right?
That was impossible...
"Am I seeing things, or is Kent Madson using the Nine-Fold Demon Hammer technique?"
"He is using it, and flawlessly at that."
Many were left in shock, most wondering if what they were seeing was even real.
The fact that Kent was using a technique that many could spend their entire lives without mastering even a single form was simply unbelievable.
Even Lady Khronisia was left stunned.
It had taken her thousands of years to master the first three forms.
However, it had taken Kent just a day or two of watching her to master them.
Naturally, that was impossible.

However, while he possessed talent that far surpassed mortal comprehension, his knowledge of this particular technique came from his past life.
The Nine-Fold Demon Hammer was a technique he had helped refine back when he was known as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.
