chapters.title: Chapter 1873: Mjolnir
paragraphs: Blacksmithing is similar to alchemy.

When something grand or extraordinary has happened, the heavens acknowledge it. So, just like Pill Judgement, where the Pill Dao judges the pill created, in blacksmithing, the Blacksmith Dao also has to judge and acknowledge the item forged.
However, unlike alchemy, where there is a certain tier of pills that can be judged, in blacksmithing, there are no tiers.

The judgement only comes when something extraordinary has been forged. So whenever tribulation clouds form during a blacksmithing process, everyone becomes elated, for they know something remarkable has been born.
Lady Khronisia smiled, watching as the Eternal Ice Genesis Spear slowly rose into the air.
Just when it was high enough, she formed a hand seal, and a humanoid soul radiating intense ice essence appeared and entered the spear.
RUMBLE
The heavens shook, and then red, blue, and green-colored clouds appeared. Seeing this, the smile on her face widened even more.
’Wherever you are, thank you, Kent Madson,’ she said inwardly, her focus turning back to the tribulation...
Meanwhile, after entering the storm cloud, Kent found himself in a world filled with Natural Qi. It was as if everything about this place was made from Natural Qi.

From the trees to the birds, the mountains, the rocks, and everything else, it all reeked of Natural Qi. Naturally, that shouldn’t be possible unless, of course, there were thousands of natural artefacts in this world.

Natural artefacts are materials, such as weapons, that were forged but never used, allowing them to live on their own and grow. They do this by harnessing Natural Qi, and if such artefacts are allowed to exist long enough, they naturally release it, giving rise to the Dao of Nature in the space where they have been kept.
It isn’t common, but it has been said to have happened before, many times in the distant past.

Finding himself in such a place, one would expect Kent to feel overwhelmed. However, he was rather calm, his expression relaxed, and he even seemed to be enjoying the natural energy flowing into his body.

Perhaps it was because he had cultivated the World Root Chaos Scripture, so, sensing Natural Qi, he felt at ease. Lady Kenzie was certainly happy at the moment, since she could channel as much Natural Qi as she wanted to aid Kent in any way she deemed appropriate.
However, while the Natural Qi kept him calm and relaxed, he was truly relaxed because he recognised the place he had found himself in.

"You never could stay away, could you, Mjolnir?" Kent said, turning his head to the left, where a middle-aged man with a handsome appearance stood, his arms crossed over his chest, gazing back at Kent with an angry expression.
At first glance, one would think he was a person. However, while he looked human, he was actually a living weapon.
Specifically, he was the hammer that had accompanied the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith throughout his adventurous days in Hell and his journey as a blacksmith.
They had been through thick and thin together, fighting and forging every step of the way.

During the Flame Wars, when the danger reached a level that could not be handled, Fjorge made the ultimate sacrifice by detonating his body and using his soul. He finally gave his hammer a name, thus awakening its weapon spirit.
That awakening turned the weapon from a simple hammer into one that slew two Primordials and five Pseudo-Primordials.
After the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith died, Mjolnir vanished, and that was the last time anyone ever saw or heard from him.
A couple of months back, when Kent recovered his memories of the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, he sensed Mjolnir’s gaze from a very far distance.
However, for whatever reason, he didn’t know, Mjolnir didn’t come to him as he had expected.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦

The second time he sensed him was during the Dark War when he unleashed the Sixty-Six Hammer Art. That was the moment Kent realised he had to use a method that would make his unruly hammer become jealous.
So, taking advantage of the forging process, he used a technique he knew Mjolnir would hate. After all, the person that technique belonged to was an enemy of the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith...

Using it was perhaps the most unruly thing Kent had done, and thanks to that, he was now face to face with his living hammer, whose cultivation was so deep that even Kent couldn’t completely comprehend it.
"You have become weak," Mjolnir said, a smirk escaping his mouth...
Kent chuckled and replied, "And you have become talkative and a bit of a drama queen. Since when did you start throwing tantrums?"
"I don’t throw tantrums, and you know it." Mjolnir smirked again and added, "I am just disgusted by the fact that my master is so weak. Wielding me will certainly result in your own death."
Kent narrowed his eyes at Mjolnir and laughed. "You think I am weak, huh?"
The smile on his face slowly turned evil. Then he rose to his feet and took one step forward.
BOOOM
A terrifying killing intent exploded from his body, spreading all over the space. Mjolnir remained standing, the look of disdain plastered across his face. Kent didn’t seem to be bothered by that.
He took a second step, and the killing intent in the air doubled. Still, Mjolnir remained relaxed, not even a shift in his expression.
But everything changed when Kent took the third step.
BOOM BOOM BOOM
Three powerful explosions of energy erupted from his body, and behind him, three deadly Eyes of Chaos appeared. At that instant, Mjolnir frowned, then uncrossed his arms and adjusted his stance...
But Kent merely smiled and said inwardly, ’Oh, you think I am done, buddy.’
He took the fourth step, and that was when everything changed. The space behind him shattered, revealing a void.
From within the darkness, crimson dragon eyes, born of killing intent, began to open, each oozing the insidious power of blood and carnage.
Mjolnir finally flinched, his expression turning slightly pale.
He took a step back, then exhaled before tapping into his own power...
"Not impressed?" Kent ask, the smile on his face turning twisted.

chapters.title: Chapter 1874: True Killing Intent
paragraphs: BOOM BOOM BOOM
Mjolnir was pushed back, his expression finally cracking. He looked at the thousands of crimson eyes behind Kent, each oozing overwhelming killing intent and sigh.
All he could do was stare dumbfoundedly at Kent.
There was no way someone who hadn’t even reached the realm of Godhood could possess that much control over killing intent.
In fact, from what Mjolnir had seen in the last few eras he had wandered the universe, not even Celestials had that much control over their killing intent.
They didn’t even have enough kills under their belts to possess that much killing intent.
However, Kent did, and that was just too shocking.
"H-How?" he asked, his voice breaking, perhaps due to the strain on his body.
Kent had only taken six steps, but the pressure in the air was just on another level.
Each step came with so much pressure that Mjolnir, who lacked that much killing intent, struggled to hold his stance.

One funny thing about killing intent, however, is the fact that blocking it is nearly impossible. The only way it can be blocked is for the person being attacked to possess enough killing intent to rival that of the one suppressing them.

Mjolnir was a Primordial-grade weapon with powers so deep that even Kent could not fathom them. However, he lacked the level of killing intent Kent possessed, which, at the moment, left him shaken to the core.

The first step unleashed the killing intent, while the second doubled it. The third tripled it, and it continued from there, with every step raising the terrifying level of killing intent in the air to an all-time high.
Kent smiled and snapped his fingers, causing the killing intent in the air to vanish...

He then turned and looked at Mjolnir, who seemed to have finally found his footing again. "If you wish to know why a mere Demigod such as myself possesses this level of killing intent, then the answer is simple: I inherited it."
Mjolnir furrowed his brow upon hearing his answer. "You inherited it? That doesn’t make sense to me. Who inherits killing intent?"

Kent smiled. "Oh, trust me, it is a normal thing if you know what I know. However, while killing intent can be inherited, the quality of it depends on who you are inheriting it from, your soul strength and how much control they had over it when they sealed it away.
In my case, I have 100% control, so everything I showed you now all came from me. In other words, I have inherited the killing intent of my past incarnations."
Mjolnir was still confused, but that was normal considering what Kent was saying simply didn’t make sense.

He had lived thirteen lives, and so far, he had recalled nine of them. Each life came with its own unique story, yet they all shared something in common. They were all legendary warriors with millions of kills under their belts.
This means that in all 9 lives, he had accumulated a rather dense killing intent.
At first, he never really had that much control over the killing intent of his past lives. However, that all changed when he read the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual.
He had witnessed how the Chaos Ascension King cultivated his killing intent. But even that didn’t do much for his own killing intent.
It was after he had finished reading the book that the main gain came.
The runes left on the page were something linked directly to killing intent. He had learned them all, and the moment he did, he comprehended an aspect of killing intent called True Killing Intent.
This True Killing Intent opened access to his soul, connecting it to all nine lives he had recalled so far. This connection, however, allowed him to harness the killing intent of all those lives.
Of course, there was a limit to how much he could harness. But with how robust his soul was, he was able to channel at least 10% of the killing intent from each of his nine lives.
That, coupled with the fact that he was cultivating Blood, Evil, and Abyssal Qi, made the already terrifying killing intent reach a whole different level of madness.
"Allow me to burst your bubble, Mjolnir," Kent said. Then he proceeded to reveal his identities to Mjolnir, who, after hearing all he had said, could only stare back at Kent in awe.
"As you have heard, I have lived so many lives, with every last one ending with a bang. You knew me as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.
However, long before that life, I was Lord Genesis. I was also the Primordial Chaos Dragon, and I was even the dreadful bastard widely known as the Ruthless Bandit.
So yes, I may be a Demigod, but I have the killing intent of beings who once ruled the universe and walked with their shoulders held high."
Sigh
Mjolnir took a deep breath and exhaled. "Then answer me, who are you really?"
"I’ve lived several lives and experienced a variety of things. However, I identify as one person, and that is the Primordial Chaos Dragon. But you can just call me Kent."
Mjolnir nodded, making sense of the kind of person his master was, or had become.

The past him was merely a fragment of a much larger self. Luckily, he had been privileged to have been a part of it. Now, however, he would have the chance to walk the path of ascension with him again.
"So tell me, Mjolnir, do you still want to play hard to get, or are you ready to return to my side, where you belong?"

"Only if you promise to use me only in battles against Celestials and above, or to forge Supreme-grade weapons and above. I am not a simple weapon now, and I would rather rot in Hell than be lowered to the level where I will be used against Gods."
Kent laughed, hearing the concern of his fourth Living Weapon.
Already, he had Gaap, who was one of the most dreadful swords he had ever had in his arsenal. Then there was Ryoa, his evil spear, which he had wielded back in the day as the Ruthless Bandit.
The third was the corrupted spear, which, with Lady Kenzie’s help, had been transformed into the Grim Corrupted Dagger, becoming his third Living Weapon.
Now, he had reunited with his fourth Living Weapon...Mjolnir, the Devastating Hell Hammer.

chapters.title: Chapter 1875: Reunion
paragraphs: "So, where have you been, and what have you been up to while I was gone?" Kent asked, walking to a nearby cliff.
Mjolnir followed him and stood beside him, his arms crossed over his chest.

"When you gave me your soul, allowing me to awaken, I became the temporary owner of your personal world. So I returned here after the war, for a few thousand years, to cultivate and better understand my powers and nature.

Afterward, I started travelling the universe, learning the way of life wherever I found myself. Luckily for me, after travelling for a while, I managed to become a Primordial. I never expected it, but I knew one day I would become one.

So when I did, I ventured into the Universe Ocean to explore some more and gather resources for when you returned. I returned a hundred thousand years ago, and ever since then, I have been looking for signs of your return.
It took some time, but I did when you released a bit of the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith Flame Qi a couple of months back. Now, here I am and, well, glad to see you again."
Kent nodded and smiled.
"Looks like you hadn’t lived a boring life at all." Venturing into Primordial Chaos sure showed he had seen his fair share of things and experienced various events.
He is a Primordial, but with a much stronger foundation. On his own, he is a menace, and in Kent’s hands, who knows what kind of carnage they would cause?
Maybe Kent would even have an easy time navigating the Primordial Chaos one day.
"So what are your plans now?" Kent asked again.
Considering Mjolnir is a Primordial and also a living weapon, his strongest living weapon thus far, telling him to become his go-to weapon would be akin to looking down on him.
He can be used against Celestials, but he would have to suppress his own power to the Celestial stage since using Primordial Qi against Celestials would invoke the wrath of the heavens.
Basically, using him would violate so many rules...
Maybe some of those rules would not invoke the wrath of the heavens, but they would certainly go against Kent’s own pride as a cultivator and a warrior.
Regardless, Mjolnir is a weapon, and he must be wielded as such...
But as to how she wished to be handled, Kent wanted to find out from him instead.

Mjolnir turned to look at Kent and said, "I know the kind of person you are, so I know you will never wield me in a battle against Celestials and below. This is why I will not expect you to ask me to follow you now.

However, I also cannot just leave and wander on my own, so why don’t we go back to how things used to be, when you would forge weapons that defied common sense, and I will ride there in your grip, shaping them?" He smiled slyly.
"I can sense the aura of the Nine Dragon Whip on you, which means you have already reunited with them. The last time we forged them, we used primitive materials.
Luckily for you, I brought back thousands of minerals from my time in Primordial Chaos so we can work on turning the Nine Dragon Whip into a living weapon.
At least, that will be a challenge, right? You have never forged a living weapon outright, so take this as your first trial. Hopefully, you will either excel or fail.
Regardless, I can be your forging hammer for now until you are ready to venture into battles that require a more dreadful weapon."
"That works for me. I indeed have so many weapons to forge, and in case you are not aware, there are dangers everywhere, so I might be needing you as my war hammer sooner than you think."
Mjolnir nodded, feeling relieved.
He may have tried to play stubborn, but he really missed Kent. Not that he would admit it. But as the simple bone, crudely shaped into a hammer by a seven-year-old, showed, their bond runs deep.
Kent turned slightly and looked at Mjolnir, who was staring ahead, his expression calm.
"In your travels, did you happen to go to Hell?"
"I did. It was where I went first right after I left this world."
"Then what happened to the Hell Devastators after I died?" Kent clearly had no idea that one of the Hell Devastators was currently inside the Tower...
Since he hadn’t been to the Legion Tower since he woke up, considering most of the time he had spent with Safira was in the Tower City, he had yet to meet Ruby.
"Out of the ninety-six Hell Devastators, thirty-six perished during the Flame War. The remaining sixty, half of them returned to Hell and had been exploring the Hell Calamity Zones.
The other thirty, from what I could find out, had also ventured into all kinds of calamity zones this universe had to offer. Some even ventured into the Abyssal Chaos and the Forsaken Seas.
Honestly, they seem to have a thing for dangerous zones, so I wouldn’t be surprised if the next time you see them, they are monsters or perhaps dead."
Kent smirked and looked down the cliff, staring deep into the scorching sea of lava.

He laughed. "I picked them as my legion for a reason, Mjolnir. Every last one of them is crazy in their own way. So rest assured, even if they were to meet the most dreadful enemy, I wouldn’t be too worried about their safety, for they will survive somehow."
Kent sounded confident, which showed he indeed had that much confidence in the Hell Devastators. But then he turned around and spread his arms.
"Enough about the Hell Devastators. How about we go see our old friend we had chained down there? I am sure she will be happy to see us again... or not."
He fell backward, plunging headfirst into the lava below.
Mjolnir watched Kent falling into the lava, and a sigh escaped his lips.
"Sometimes I forget he has been alot more crazy than anyone I’ve ever met since he was seven years old."
He chuckled, then jumped down as well, following closely behind Kent.
After a few seconds of falling, they plunged into the lava pool and vanished. The ripples they left behind lasted only a moment before calm returned to the surface.
Meanwhile, in the scorching depths of the lava pool, a woman of flawless beauty and long gray hair slowly opened her eyes. Chains rattled as she turned her head to look up.

chapters.title: Chapter 1876: Second Flame Matriarch
paragraphs: [First Wave of the Flame War - Flame Era]
Fjorge, or as many called him, the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, stood on a scorched battlefield, his expression grim as he watched the advance of a sea of warriors, each radiating intense heat.
Some had twisted horns, many appeared as demon-beast hybrids, and some looked human—perhaps too perfect to be human, even.

Leading them was a woman whose beauty could easily bring about the fall of a galaxy. She radiated the intense flame aura of a Pseudo-Primordial, and in her hand was a spear shaped like the fang of a tiger.
"So she is the infamous Second Flame Matriarch?" Fjorge asked, turning to a lady clad in crimson armor and wielding a broadsword.

"Yes, my lord. She was the one the message said we should look out for and never underestimate," Ruby answered, her gaze burning with lethal battle intent. Behind her, forty others stood, each ready for battle.
"Have you heard from the others?" Fjorge asked, and Ruby nodded.
"They are in position, each waiting for your signal."
Fjorge smiled and pointed forward. "In that case, it was nice knowing you all, since I might die this time."
He laughed, jumped down from the cliff, and landed on the scorched ground, sending a large, powerful shockwave through the surroundings.
Up ahead, the Second Flame Matriarch grinned and flew into the air.
She had already heard about the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith and had wanted to fight him. So, seeing him advance, she did the same, hoping to battle him to the death.

"So you are who the Flame Empress was concerned about, huh? The infamous champion of the Damnation Arena, the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith," the Second Flame Matriarch remarked, a smirk forming at the corner of her lips.
"Oh, so you have heard of me, huh?" Fjorge laughed. "Do tell, aren’t you afraid of me, then?"
"Afraid of you?" the Second Flame Matriarch laughed out loud, her mocking tone echoing through the air. "If there is something I should be afraid of, then it should be what I am going to do to you."

"Is that so? Well, don’t say I didn’t warn you." Fjorge raised his hammer and rested the handle on his shoulder. "Now, allow me to teach you why your Empress had even heard of me all the way in the Flame Demon Realm."
Fjorge moved, and the flames moved with him.
The battle was what many would consider legendary. Every clash of their weapons left deadly marks in the air, the void shattering and healing with every passing second.

Around them, every flame was supercharged with flame runes and intense flame laws. Fjorge used his understanding of the flames to attack and defend, and the Second Flame Matriarch seemed to be doing the same.
It was just that they were moving so fast that nobody could see what kind of attacks either of them was using.
Five hours later, however, they saw the result, and it sent shockwaves throughout the ranks of the flame demons that had come with the Second Flame Matriarch.

Fjorge held the Second Flame Matriarch by the neck, every bone in her body broken and deformed. As much as she wanted to heal, her healing speed had been greatly suppressed while Fjorge held her by the neck.
Of course, Fjorge didn’t come out of the fight unscathed. However, he was in a far better position compared to the Second Flame Matriarch.
"Killing you would be mercy, and to be honest, very difficult. So I will not kill you, but you are going to wish I did." He slammed her body into the ground, and she passed out instantly.
[Several Years Later]
The Second Flame Matriarch looked up at the empty sky, her eyes radiating intense hatred. She sensed the presence of someone she had been meaning to kill for a very long time.
A few seconds later, the sky split open, and Kent appeared, with Mjolnir following behind a second later. The moment they appeared, the sky healed, and the heat that accompanied them vanished.
Their gazes met instantly, and an untamed killing intent erupted from the Second Flame Matriarch’s eyes.
"Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith..." she muttered, her tone flat and cold.
"Did you miss me?" Kent said with mocking laughter, a sound and expression that left the Second Flame Matriarch fuming.

They say obsession is not healthy. However, in her case, her obsession with killing the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith had kept her sane throughout the last couple of eras she had spent chained down here.

All she wanted was the chance to kill the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith and wash away the humiliation she had suffered at his hands. She had come with high expectations, hoping to kill Kent and make a name for herself.
However, things had ended rather badly for her instead.
"No need to look so angry, Second Flame Matriarch. For what it’s worth, we defeated the flame races, sending the rest packing, so you didn’t humiliate yourself that much."
Kent’s words only seemed to fuel her spirit of vengeance.
"Remove these chains now, and let’s see who would lose."
Kent laughed.

"Very funny, Second Flame Matriarch. We both know the only way you’re going to get out of those chains is by accepting my offer. To tell you the truth, your era has long passed, and there is no such thing as gaining your freedom ever again.

So, what do you think? Are you willing to swear the Oath of the Flame and fight for me, or will you keep being stubborn, hoping for a day when you can break free? News flash, that day will never come."
A grin formed on Kent’s face. Then he tapped into his newfound power, unleashing his killing intent and bringing an overwhelming pressure and dread down upon the Second Flame Matriarch.
Her expression suddenly paled. At that very moment, part of her wished she hadn’t tried to threaten Kent.
However, Kent hadn’t come this time to sweet-talk her.
No, he had come to recruit her, for he had found a way back to the Flame Realm, and he needed an obedient guide for when he was ready to head over.
If he wished to defeat the flame race, he first had to understand their power structure and battle formations.
Who better to help him with that than the second strongest Flame General of the Flame Era?

chapters.title: Chapter 1877: Ranking
paragraphs: Kent always thinks long-term.

It is perhaps one of the traits he shared with all 13 incarnations. Long before the Flame War ended, he knew they would never win, so the best-case scenario was for them to seal the flame demons away and try again later.
That was a solid plan, and long before it had been implemented, many other incarnations of his had done the same.
Chaos sealed away the Chaos Beasts.
Lord Genesis sealed away the Foreign Race.
Even the Ruthless Bandit sealed away the Dark Creatures.
So, sealing away the flame demons was the most ideal move he had come up with back then and implemented.
However, there was something else he wanted to do, and that was to prevent the flame demons from ever invading the Infinity Universe.
But to do that, he had to venture into the Flame Realm personally and bring the fight to them.
However, to accomplish that, he was going to need a guide, and he picked the Second Flame Matriarch for that role.
She had come to kill the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, but he had been prepared to capture and imprison her.
He succeeded, and now he wished to implement his plans.
"You see, while you had been rotting away here, I had been busy, working around the clock for the day I would find my way back to your realm.
Recently, I did, and it will be not only to destroy your kind, but also to ensure that, after all is said and done, your kind will become an army I will command to subjugate all other realms.

Rest assured, there is a chance I might die, which would then be your freedom. But there is also a chance I might not die, regardless of what your people throw at me. So consider this possibility and think about what you have to do.
Though you must know that regardless of your answer, I will invade your race and bring them to their knees. Whether you join or not, it will happen.
The question here is, are you willing to remain imprisoned for all eternity—because that is what will happen once I leave today—or join me and gain some form of freedom?"
One could tell the expression on the Second Flame Matriarch’s face had changed.
Indeed, she had been rotting away here for billions of years. If she got the chance to see her race again, then she had to take it.
The only issue was the oath she was being asked to swear. If she went ahead and swore it, it would be akin to selling out her kind, which, from what she knew, was frowned upon.
Basically, she had a lot to think about, and Kent, who knew the kind of plans he had for her, could only smile and watch her think about what she wished to do with her life.
Meanwhile, back inside the tower, Kent’s wives had all gathered inside the Harem Tower for the long-awaited reveal of who ranked at the top during the Dark War.
They had all bet that every kill would be translated into points that would be accumulated and used to rank them after the battle.
The point system was as follows.
Immortals would give points ranging from one to five, depending on the rank of the immortal.
Demigods would give points from six to ten. Gods would give 11-15, and Supremes would give 16-25. As for Celestials, their points started from 26 and ended at 50, depending on their ranking.
This point system was put in place so that those who were locked in battle against powerful Supremes and Celestials would not fall behind when it came to points gained from their kills.
So they gathered around for the reveal, and while some of them weren’t around during the Dark War, they came to see who among them had the highest kill count in terms of points.
Inaya, who was away on a mission, stood calmly beside her best friend Ainna, who still hadn’t joined the harem but was always with Kent’s wives.

"Don’t worry, Inaya. I did my best for you, so I am sure that while you won’t rank in the top ten, you certainly won’t be last in the rankings." She had, of course, done what any best friend would do and fought in Inaya’s stead, earning points for her.
Inaya smiled and nodded. "No need to worry about me, Ainna. I have already secured my slot by bringing back Safira."
Safira, who was nearby, turned and looked at Inaya with a smile. "Thanks for bringing me back then. At least my life counts for something good."
She smirked, causing Inaya to chuckle.
Safira was learning to adapt to their way of life, so instead of treating her like an outsider, they chose to treat her like one of them.
She had been having so much fun with them, so much so that she sometimes forgot she was even a Forsaken Being.
On the other side, the heavy hitters who knew they ranked in the top ten stood together, each wearing a smug expression.
Tower, clad in her brown leader’s suit, stood before a large stone tablet, her expression showing happiness.
Scanning the faces of the gathered ladies, she said, "Before we begin, I would like to point out that Big Sister Ainna donated her points to Big Sister Inaya.
Aside from her, Big Sisters Indie, Nyx, and Miryssa forfeited their points since they aren’t around to claim their rewards."

"That is fine. The fewer, the better," Unity said, knowing that while she had some kills under her belt, she could never compete with the likes of Indie, who had literally brought Grim Reapers from the Underworld to fight for her.
Her sisters laughed, and even Tower joined them.
Once the laughter died down, she pointed her tiny finger at the stone tablet, and a subtle light washed over it.

Then names started appearing on it. Tower deliberately made the names appear in a disordered manner to keep the suspense high. After all the names had appeared, she snapped her fingers, and they started rearranging themselves.

They all held their breath, especially those who had fought with such large teams. They knew the chances of them ranking near the top were very high, so they stared at the stone tablet in anticipation.
In no time, the rankings were finalized, leaving everyone dumbfounded.

If she went ahead and swore it, it would be akin to selling out her kind, which, from what she knew, was frowned upon.
Basically, she had a lot to think about, and Kent, who knew the kind of plans he had for her, could only smile and watch her think about what she wished to do with her life.
Meanwhile, back inside the tower, Kent’s wives had all gathered inside the Harem Tower for the long-awaited reveal of who ranked at the top during the Dark War.
They had all bet that every kill would be translated into points that would be accumulated and used to rank them after the battle.
The point system was as follows.
Immortals would give points ranging from one to five, depending on the rank of the immortal.
Demigods would give points from six to ten.
Gods would give 11-15, and Supremes would give 16-25.
As for Celestials, their points started from 26 and ended at 50, depending on their ranking.
This point system was put in place so that those who were locked in battle against powerful Supremes and Celestials would not fall behind when it came to points gained from their kills.
So they gathered around for the reveal, and while some of them weren’t around during the Dark War, they came to see who among them had the highest kill count in terms of points.
Inaya, who was away on a mission, stood calmly beside her best friend Ainna, who still hadn’t joined the harem but was always with Kent’s wives.
"Don’t worry, Inaya.

I did my best for you, so I am sure that while you won’t rank in the top ten, you certainly won’t be last in the rankings." She had, of course, done what any best friend would do and fought in Inaya’s stead, earning points for her.
Inaya smiled and nodded.
"No need to worry about me, Ainna.
I have already secured my slot by bringing back Safira."
Safira, who was nearby, turned and looked at Inaya with a smile.
"Thanks for bringing me back then.
At least my life counts for something good."
She smirked, causing Inaya to chuckle.
Safira was learning to adapt to their way of life, so instead of treating her like an outsider, they chose to treat her like one of them.
She had been having so much fun with them, so much so that she sometimes forgot she was even a Forsaken Being.
On the other side, the heavy hitters who knew they ranked in the top ten stood together, each wearing a smug expression.
Tower, clad in her brown leader’s suit, stood before a large stone tablet, her expression showing happiness.
Scanning the faces of the gathered ladies, she said, "Before we begin, I would like to point out that Big Sister Ainna donated her points to Big Sister Inaya.
Aside from her, Big Sisters Indie, Nyx, and Miryssa forfeited their points since they aren’t around to claim their rewards."
"That is fine.

The fewer, the better," Unity said, knowing that while she had some kills under her belt, she could never compete with the likes of Indie, who had literally brought Grim Reapers from the Underworld to fight for her.
Her sisters laughed, and even Tower joined them.
Once the laughter died down, she pointed her tiny finger at the stone tablet, and a subtle light washed over it.
Then names started appearing on it.
Tower deliberately made the names appear in a disordered manner to keep the suspense high.
After all the names had appeared, she snapped her fingers, and they started rearranging themselves.
They all held their breath, especially those who had fought with such large teams.
They knew the chances of them ranking near the top were very high, so they stared at the stone tablet in anticipation.
In no time, the rankings were finalized, leaving everyone dumbfounded.

chapters.title: Chapter 1878: Top Ranker
paragraphs: "No fucking way," Unity muttered, her expression dazed as she stared at the name sitting at the top of the ranking. One could tell they had never expected this person to rank first.
However, here they all were, staring at what they knew was the accurate ranking, for Tower wasn’t one to make mistakes about stuff like this.

"Still, how did Dia manage to become the top ranker? We all experienced the battle, and while I hate to admit it, I expected either Adina, Zaila, or Elsa to rank first. How did Dia make it to the top?" Vexthra asked, clearly stunned.
Even Dia herself seemed stunned, staring at her name at the top of the rankings.

During the Dark War, Adina used her abilities to mesmerize hundreds of Dark Creatures, permanently making them her army. They listened only to her, and per the rules, their kills were hers to claim.𝒻𝘳ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝒷𝘯ℴ𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝑐ℴ𝑚

They had killed quite a lot of dark fiends, and their points were added to Adina’s. However, it now appeared that even with this aid, she hadn’t reached Dia’s level. Still, she managed to rank second, which was something.
As for Zaila, who ranked third, she had also unlocked an aspect of her mind control powers during the battle, allowing her to enthrall the Dark Creatures.
While her powers awakened during the battle, she managed to amass a good number of points from both her personal kills and her thralls.
Still, that didn’t help.

Then there was Elsa, who had also managed to summon her Soul Sentinels. While her powers awakened near the climax of the battle, she amassed quite a few points. That had made most of her sisters wonder if she would rank even higher.
But Dia was at the top, and they just didn’t understand it.
Luckily, Tower saw this coming and had prepared.
She waved her hand, and a giant display showing certain moments of the Dark War appeared. On the screen, the moment Dia unleashed her Hair Domain appeared.
This time, however, the display showed what happened within the domain.
When they saw it, every last one of them became convinced. Dia indeed deserved the first spot, for what they were watching showed that she had indeed killed her fair share of opponents.
Inside her Hair Domain, thousands of Gods, Supremes, and even some Celestials were devoured, erased from existence as they became trapped.
It was as if whatever entered her Hair Domain was destined to die...

"This is hard to understand or believe, but Big Sister Dia’s Hair Domain grows with every kill. So while she started out killing Gods, it quickly picked up, and she was able to kill Supremes, which helped her kill Celestials.
Kill count-wise, she ranks in the top ten, but in terms of points accumulated from the quality of kills, none of you come close. She earned her spot all by herself, and that is commendable."
"Of course, we are all happy for her," Pandora said, a smile forming on her face.
The rest of her sisters joined in, congratulating Dia. "Congratulations, Dia. You deserve the best after all, so enjoy it."
The Mother of Heart Demons smiled and nodded. "Thank you all. Although I never expected this, I am happy to have gotten it."
They smiled and laughed with her.

The rewards for the top ranker were three months of uninterrupted time with Kent. Those ranked second through tenth would each get two months, while those ranked eleventh through thirtieth would each get one month. Anyone below that would only get a week.

Looking at the rankings now, they all knew where they ranked and how long they would get to spend with Kent, who had promised to return to the tower once he was done with his business with Lady Khronisia.
"Next time, I will take the first spot," Adina said, staring at her name, currently seated in second place on the rankings.

"You make it sound like I will be sleeping through the battle or something," Zaila sneered, looking at Adina, who thought that scoring second place meant she had the right to aim for first place next time.
Elsa also smirked, already prepared for when the next battle would arrive so she and her Soul Sentinels could prove to everyone that they were once the bane of every army.
A legion of warriors, each specializing in a unique Soul Art, surely made them a legion of terrifying warriors.
"At the end of the day, it is about getting the job done, so we shouldn’t compete against each other," Elaine said, allowing a small smile to form on her face.
Vexthra, who knew the kind of monsters Elaine was currently cultivating inside her Life and Death Primordial Space, smiled but said nothing.
She knew the next time they fought, the rankings would be different.
Why did she say that...
It was because, inside the top ten, there were two people whose rankings many of them were shocked by, one being Neomi and the other Alina.

Neomi, the Mother of Killers, ranked seventh, while Alina ranked eighth. It should be noted that Neomi fought with her twin short swords, while Alina spent most of her time protecting her sisters with arrays and formations.

For them to be within the top ten showed that they might just be the two with the fastest kill rates among their sisters. Neomi especially had surprised everyone. Unlike Alina, who could deploy dozens of formations, she fought only with her two swords and killed in close combat.
Such terrifying battle prowess was simply too good to be true.
But Neomi had proven herself to be someone who could not be underestimated.
Maybe next time, she would prove to everyone why she was the best and deserved to rank first.
But for now, the rankings were set, and when Kent returned, he would spend three months with Dia, and then the rest would follow.

Hopefully, by the time he was done with them, the time for the Galactic Pill Competition would arrive, allowing him to progress further on the path of pill making and finally become someone who could challenge even Pill Gods.

chapters.title: Chapter 1879: Leaving the Undead Realm
paragraphs: [Somewhere in the Supreme Undead Heaven]
Kaizo sat atop the skull of a very terrifying-looking Dragon Skull. From the aura around it alone, it was clear that when it was alive, even Celestials would have run from it.
Its size alone was too large to comprehend how much pressure it would have possessed back when it soared through the skies and scorched the earth.
However, it was dead, and Kaizo seemed to have found a liking for its skull, which he had used as his throne.

Standing across the vast skeleton of this dragon were the rest of his teammates and the Green Bone Oracle, who had led them to the Undead Grave, where the treasures left behind by the Bone Lich Undead Emperor were recovered.
It hadn’t been an easy adventure.

Kaizo and his friends faced all kinds of dangers, each far more dreadful than the last. Luckily for them, they had prepared thoroughly for everything, so despite the danger, they finally managed to complete their mission after months of battles.
"This has been eventful at least," Kaizo muttered, looking at the carnage they had left around them.

"We managed to retrieve the treasures. In my view, that was what mattered. But it is also good that we both managed to gain some treasures that will be used to upgrade when we return," Varyn said, and her friends nodded.

They had managed to gain some treasures that, if used well, would push all of them to at least the Supreme stage. That would surely boost their power, allowing them to have their own footing within the Legion.
"We better leave then, since the longer we stay here, the higher the chances that the Undead Monarch will return from wherever he had gone."
Varkhiel’s words were taken to heart, so after resting for an hour, they left, with Kaizo taking the bones of the dragon with him.
A week later, they returned to the Supreme Undead Heaven and booked a tavern, where they started to wait for the Third Undead Princess, who had promised to leave with them.

The last couple of months spent inside the Undead Grave had been spent preparing so that they would be ready when they came out, since there was a high possibility that the Undead Monarch would return before they did.
Luckily, they had the Third Undead Princess on their side, so she made sure they remained hidden from all who might recognize them.
Three days after they returned to the Supreme Undead Heaven, the Third Undead Princess arrived wearing a disguise.

Inasmuch as she would have loved to be seen outside with Kaizo and his friends, she knew her status as a Princess would bring them too much trouble, so she disguised herself to save them the trouble...
"So you have really decided to leave with them, huh?" the Green Bone Oracle asked, leaning against a beam.
The Third Undead Princess smiled and nodded.

"I need to see him and discuss some important issues with him. While there seems to be peace right now in the Undead Realm, there are far darker forces at work, and if we don’t handle these petty conflicts, one day we will all perish at the hands of these darker forces."
Green Bone Oracle didn’t seem too bothered, though. However, he nodded and turned to Kaizo.
"I cannot come with you this time since I have business. But inform Sanders that I will reach out when I’m done with the matters here."
"Master will hear your message."
"Good. Then here you go, the wine you requested. I have been saving some for millions of years, so be sure to inform Sanders I expect something of equal value when we meet."
Kaizo smiled and nodded. "I am sure Master will be ready and fully prepared when you meet."
Their conversation soon ended, and Kaizo and his team were ready to leave...
"I am pretty sure when the Undead Monarch returns and discovers you are not in the Undead Realm, he will be so pissed."
The Green Bone Oracle joked as he watched Kaizo work to open the portal that would take them back to the Infinity Universe.
"All the more reason for me to return before he does."
A few seconds later, a portal opened, and they were ready to leave.
"See you guys later."
Kaizo and his teammates bid their final farewells, and they were soon gone. The Third Undead Princess followed after they had all entered, and then the portal closed behind her.
"I can’t wait for him to return and throw his tantrums."
The Green Bone Oracle allowed a smile to form on his face for a few seconds before it vanished along with his body.
[Abyssal Realm]
Meanwhile, somewhere far away, a man with a head of white hair and an aura that would cause even Primordials to tremble in their shoes set down a cup filled with boiling hell wine.
"HMMMM."
He hummed, his expression turning a bit sour.
"So he had returned, huh?"
The expression on his face didn’t change much, but one could tell he wasn’t happy with what had come to mind. Clearly, the Third Undead Princess leaving the Undead Realm hadn’t escaped him.
In fact, he was someone who had always known that the Third Undead Princess and the Bone Lich Undead Emperor shared a past.
He had even tried to use their connection once to get close to Sanders and kill him. However, the Bone Lich Undead Emperor wasn’t someone he could kill easily, resulting in the failure of that plan.
Ever since then, he had kept a close eye on the Third Undead Princess. Now that she had left the Undead Realm, he knew the only place she would go was the Infinity Universe.
’Very well. Since you have returned, then be sure to prepare for what comes next. Once the issue with the Abyssal Chaos is resolved, I will be sure to focus on you.’

He lifted the cup, drank its contents, and set it back down. Kent wasn’t his priority right now, so he could have his few years of peace. Once he was done, he would turn his wrath back on him and make sure he understood what pain truly felt like.

chapters.title: Chapter 1880: Kaizo’s Regret
paragraphs: [Legion Tower]
A portal opened inside the Legion Tower, and Kaizo, alongside the rest of the Undead Legion, walked out, each radiating killing intent.
The moment they appeared, the rest of the Legion members currently present inside the Legion Tower surrounded them.
Kaizo had deliberately told his teammates to keep their killing intent active so that the moment they appeared, they would cause a scene.
Safe to say, as they were being surrounded, what he had envisioned came to pass.
In fact, it went beyond what he had envisioned, for the moment they were surrounded, Vexthra and her sisters also appeared inside the Legion Tower, each coming to welcome them.
Of course, sensing the intense killing intent emanating from them, they all felt like there was a lot to unpack.
Naturally, that worked in Kaizo’s favour, for he planned to exaggerate most of the things they had experienced in the Undead Realm just to make everyone jealous.
But as they say, he wasn’t prepared for what happened next...
"Kaizo, buddy, how I missed you... especially during the Dark War," Unity said with an evil grin, instantly wiping the smug expression off Kaizo’s face.
He even stumbled, his foot slipping slightly as the words Unity had practiced for weeks finally came out...
Back during the Dark War’s Kaizo and the rest sensed that something big was going on back home... something they are missing big time.
So Unity’s words were like a needle to his heart.
"You did WHAT?" the poor Undead General, who back in the Primordial Era had killed many Void Generals, asked, his gaze practically begging for more context.
Unity, of course, didn’t deny him those details...

"So after you guys were gone, Kent went missing for fifty days. When he returned, he came with a war unlike any we have participated in. In fact, it is the biggest one yet, even more chaotic than what we experience when we face Ant King Ketu.
Long story short, we finally faced the Dark Empress and her millions of Dark Fiends and defeated her. I faced many Supremes, killed three of them and severely injured a Celestial.
In fact, we were just about to view the rankings and see who in the Legion had the highest kill." Unity smiled and walked closer, wrapping her hand around Kaizo’s trembling hand.
"No need to be sad, Kaizo. I am sure another battle will soon show up soon...or not."
"Damn it."
Kaizo gritted his teeth, dark circles appearing around his eyes.
Everyone who knew just how much Kaizo loved battles and, most importantly, how much he loved to show off to Kent could tell the poor Undead brute had been broken by Unity.
They knew the two had this rivalry whenever they fought together, so Unity teasing him was clearly within her rights.

What many, except a few, knew was that behind the line, Zaila and Adina were using their abilities to influence Kaizo’s mental stability and emotions, causing him to be affected more than he should have been.
’I think we may have spoiled Unity too much,’ Vexthra said telepathically to the rest of her sisters, who nodded, knowing she was indeed overdoing it.
However, judging by how annoying Kaizo could be sometimes, teasing him was surely within reason.
"Okay, that is enough." Pandora stepped in just when Kaizo was nearly drawn to tears. Zaila and Adina deactivated their powers, allowing him a chance to breathe and gather his thoughts.
Unity smiled and teleported away, knowing Kaizo would challenge her to a duel once he realized she had used underhanded means to get under his skin.
Luckily for her, just before Kaizo could straighten his thoughts, a portal opened, and Kent, alongside Mjolnir and the Second Flame Matriarch, walked out.
Everyone turned to face them, for they sensed two dangerous individuals had arrived inside the tower.
Luckily, before any of them could go on high alert and enter battle mode, they noticed that the two individuals who had come were with the master of the tower.
Kent smiled, seeing that everyone he wanted to see had gathered in one place...
"Well, something seems to be lively here," he said, watching as everyone stared at him and the two behind him.
It turned out even the Second Flame Matriarch hated to rot in chains for all eternity, so after a much deeper soul search, she agreed to Kent’s request and swore the Oath of the Flame.
Right now, she was as obedient as a cat.

She had agreed to lead Kent and his Legion into the Flame Realm. While she categorically made him aware that she would not lift her weapon against any of her kin, she was willing to lead them there to try and conquer the flame realm.
She had her bottom line she would not cross.
Of course, there was a chance Kent would perish in that ordeal, resulting in her freedom. So she took a gamble, hoping it would pay off.
Kaizo stepped forward, a frown painting his otherwise handsome face.
"Master, what you did wasn’t fair. You waited for us to go on a mission before bringing a mega war to our doorstep."
He complained, still feeling pained at not being part of the Dark War.
Kent laughed and patted his most hardworking subordinate on the shoulder.
"Sorry, buddy. I had wanted to summon you over, but you were occupied at the time, so I didn’t. However, fear not, for a much bigger battle is on the way, and I am sure you are going to enjoy it."
Kent turned and pointed at the Second Flame Matriarch.

"Everyone, meet the Second Flame Matriarch, one of the most dangerous Flame Demons you will ever meet in your life. She and I go way back, and well, as old friends, she has agreed to lead us into the Flame Realm, where we will conquer it completely."
The Second Flame Matriarch flashed a murderous look at Kent, but she couldn’t do anything to harm him. In the end, she smirked and turned around.
Unfortunately for her, somebody else had no plans to allow her the peace of mind she needed.
Ruby grinned back at her, her broadsword drawn and battle intent burning in her eyes.
"So we meet again, Second Flame Matriarch," she said, the grin on her face widening.
For a moment, the air became cold. Then it erupted into chaos, flames and intense heat spreading everywhere.
"Blood Fox Demoness."
The Second Flame Matriarch muttered, her killing intent mixed with flame intent, pushing Kent and everyone else back...
"Oh, I am going to enjoy this."𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
Ruby moved, and the next moment, the entire Legion Tower shook.

sentences.text: [Legion Tower]
A portal opened inside the Legion Tower, and Kaizo, alongside the rest of the Undead Legion, walked out, each radiating killing intent.
The moment they appeared, the rest of the Legion members currently present inside the Legion Tower surrounded them.
Kaizo had deliberately told his teammates to keep their killing intent active so that the moment they appeared, they would cause a scene.
Safe to say, as they were being surrounded, what he had envisioned came to pass.
In fact, it went beyond what he had envisioned, for the moment they were surrounded, Vexthra and her sisters also appeared inside the Legion Tower, each coming to welcome them.
Of course, sensing the intense killing intent emanating from them, they all felt like there was a lot to unpack.
Naturally, that worked in Kaizo’s favour, for he planned to exaggerate most of the things they had experienced in the Undead Realm just to make everyone jealous.
But as they say, he wasn’t prepared for what happened next...
"Kaizo, buddy, how I missed you... especially during the Dark War," Unity said with an evil grin, instantly wiping the smug expression off Kaizo’s face.
He even stumbled, his foot slipping slightly as the words Unity had practiced for weeks finally came out...
Back during the Dark War’s Kaizo and the rest sensed that something big was going on back home... something they are missing big time.
So Unity’s words were like a needle to his heart.
"You did WHAT?" the poor Undead General, who back in the Primordial Era had killed many Void Generals, asked, his gaze practically begging for more context.
Unity, of course, didn’t deny him those details...
"So after you guys were gone, Kent went missing for fifty days.
When he returned, he came with a war unlike any we have participated in.
In fact, it is the biggest one yet, even more chaotic than what we experience when we face Ant King Ketu.
Long story short, we finally faced the Dark Empress and her millions of Dark Fiends and defeated her.
I faced many Supremes, killed three of them and severely injured a Celestial.
In fact, we were just about to view the rankings and see who in the Legion had the highest kill." Unity smiled and walked closer, wrapping her hand around Kaizo’s trembling hand.
"No need to be sad, Kaizo.
I am sure another battle will soon show up soon...or not."
"Damn it."
Kaizo gritted his teeth, dark circles appearing around his eyes.
Everyone who knew just how much Kaizo loved battles and, most importantly, how much he loved to show off to Kent could tell the poor Undead brute had been broken by Unity.
They knew the two had this rivalry whenever they fought together, so Unity teasing him was clearly within her rights.

What many, except a few, knew was that behind the line, Zaila and Adina were using their abilities to influence Kaizo’s mental stability and emotions, causing him to be affected more than he should have been.
’I think we may have spoiled Unity too much,’ Vexthra said telepathically to the rest of her sisters, who nodded, knowing she was indeed overdoing it.
However, judging by how annoying Kaizo could be sometimes, teasing him was surely within reason.
"Okay, that is enough." Pandora stepped in just when Kaizo was nearly drawn to tears.
Zaila and Adina deactivated their powers, allowing him a chance to breathe and gather his thoughts.
Unity smiled and teleported away, knowing Kaizo would challenge her to a duel once he realized she had used underhanded means to get under his skin.
Luckily for her, just before Kaizo could straighten his thoughts, a portal opened, and Kent, alongside Mjolnir and the Second Flame Matriarch, walked out.
Everyone turned to face them, for they sensed two dangerous individuals had arrived inside the tower.
Luckily, before any of them could go on high alert and enter battle mode, they noticed that the two individuals who had come were with the master of the tower.
Kent smiled, seeing that everyone he wanted to see had gathered in one place...
"Well, something seems to be lively here," he said, watching as everyone stared at him and the two behind him.
It turned out even the Second Flame Matriarch hated to rot in chains for all eternity, so after a much deeper soul search, she agreed to Kent’s request and swore the Oath of the Flame.
Right now, she was as obedient as a cat.
She had agreed to lead Kent and his Legion into the Flame Realm.
While she categorically made him aware that she would not lift her weapon against any of her kin, she was willing to lead them there to try and conquer the flame realm.
She had her bottom line she would not cross.
Of course, there was a chance Kent would perish in that ordeal, resulting in her freedom.
So she took a gamble, hoping it would pay off.
Kaizo stepped forward, a frown painting his otherwise handsome face.
"Master, what you did wasn’t fair.
You waited for us to go on a mission before bringing a mega war to our doorstep."
He complained, still feeling pained at not being part of the Dark War.
Kent laughed and patted his most hardworking subordinate on the shoulder.
"Sorry, buddy.
I had wanted to summon you over, but you were occupied at the time, so I didn’t.
However, fear not, for a much bigger battle is on the way, and I am sure you are going to enjoy it."
Kent turned and pointed at the Second Flame Matriarch.
"Everyone, meet the Second Flame Matriarch, one of the most dangerous Flame Demons you will ever meet in your life.
She and I go way back, and well, as old friends, she has agreed to lead us into the Flame Realm, where we will conquer it completely."
The Second Flame Matriarch flashed a murderous look at Kent, but she couldn’t do anything to harm him.
In the end, she smirked and turned around.
Unfortunately for her, somebody else had no plans to allow her the peace of mind she needed.
Ruby grinned back at her, her broadsword drawn and battle intent burning in her eyes.
"So we meet again, Second Flame Matriarch," she said, the grin on her face widening.
For a moment, the air became cold.
Then it erupted into chaos, flames and intense heat spreading everywhere.
"Blood Fox Demoness."
The Second Flame Matriarch muttered, her killing intent mixed with flame intent, pushing Kent and everyone else back...
"Oh, I am going to enjoy this."𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
Ruby moved, and the next moment, the entire Legion Tower shook.

chapters.title: Chapter 1881: When Mortal Enemies Fight
paragraphs: Kent had already anticipated this would happen.

He knew that aside from him, the person the Second Flame Matriarch hated the most was Ruby, the demoness who had led the Hell Devastators to slaughter her legion of flame demons after she was defeated by the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.
If there is one thing War Generals hate, it is watching their legion get decimated by their opponents while they themselves are in positions where the only thing they can do is watch it all happen.
That was what happened to her.
After she was defeated and chained, Ruby led the charge that completely reduced the flame demons to the last corpse.
Naturally, she hated her the most, and so Kent could only smile when he considered the day the two would meet.
He clearly had no idea Ruby had already found her way back to him. But it was already too late for him to do anything... well, he had one last card he could play as the Master of the Chaos Tower.

"Tower, put them in one of the arenas," to minimize the damage caused to the legion tower, Kent gave the order, and the next second, Ruby and the Second Flame Matriarch were transported into an arena.
Kaizo, of course, took a front-row seat to witness the battle between Pseudo-Primordials.
Ruby wielded her broadsword, and the Second Flame Matriarch conjured a spear from her flame element.

"I have waited for this moment for a very long time," Ruby said with mocking laughter as she brandished her sword. "You know, I actually wanted to kill you the most back then, but Master had plans for you. But now, even though he had plans for you, allow me to discipline you."
"You can try."
"Oh, I will." The smile on Ruby’s face didn’t falter.

Kent shook his head and spoke, directing his words to Ruby, "Ruby, sweetheart, I know you have become very powerful now, but don’t for a moment underestimate a flame demon. Trust me, she is very dangerous, so don’t get cocky."
"Rest assured, Master, I could kill her before she blinks."
"Oh, I am sure you can do that, but can you defeat her, though?"

The clash of blood intent and flame intent instantly filled the Arena. Luckily, they were in a self-healing arena, so whenever the void cracked open, it closed, healing at a speed that would astonish many.
Back when they met, Ruby was a Celestial, and the Second Flame Matriarch was a Pseudo-Primordial. Ruby could only wish she had the power to face her back then.
However, they are now a match, for it had been years, and Ruby had had time to catch up. Now, she can unleash powers that would even shake the hearts of Primordials.
So, as they clashed, one could see that they were both at the peak of their power.
Ruby specialises in close combat. She is very fast, so fast that most opponents she has faced in battle don’t even know when she moves until it’s too late.
Aside from that, she possesses an uncanny ability of illusion and misdirection. She can choose to move left when, in fact, she wants to move right.

The only way to counter it is for the opponent to also possess speed beyond comprehension. The Second Flame Matriarch does, and so, in the clash, one could tell that, in terms of speed, they were evenly matched.
This boils down to who possesses the most experience in high-speed battles like this.
"Master, who among them do you think would win?" Kaizo asked, turning to look at Kent, who was already surrounded on all sides by his wives...
He had no idea a certain undead Princess was looking at him, wondering just what had happened to the cold and distant Bone Lich Undead Emperor she knew.
"If they are fighting to the death, then Ruby would win. But if they are trying to subdue each other, I am pretty sure Ruby would lose in..." Kent paused and raised three fingers.
"...in three, two, one."
Just as the countdown struck zero, the Second Flame Matriarch raised her spear and drew a flame circle in the air. The moment the circle formed, a terrifying pressure descended upon the battlefield.
Ruby, who was aiming for an opening in the Second Flame Matriarch defense, immediately allowed her eyes to narrow when she sensed the scheme.
But it was already too late for her to do anything.
She had fallen into a well-crafted trap, one that the Second Flame Matriarch had cooked up before the battle even began.
The circle exploded, and in the air, a large head made of bones and metal appeared and fell in Ruby’s direction.
"Tch, I had underestimated my opponent," she smiled, watching as her body was locked in place, and even her fingers were locked in place.
"Mjolnir, save her," Kent commanded, despite knowing death is not permanent here. He just didn’t want Ruby to experience death when she hadn’t had the chance to prove herself to him yet.
Mjolnir didn’t even move. He just pointed his finger at the falling head, and a beam of lightning mixed with flames shot out and landed on the head.
CRACK
BOOM
It cracked, and then it exploded, causing the Second Flame Matriarch to suffer a backlash. She coughed up a mouthful of blood, then turned and glared hatefully at Kent.
"Hey, why are you looking at me when I had nothing to do with what happened?"
The Second Flame Matriarch didn’t reply; instead, she turned and looked at Ruby, who had regained control of her body...

"Just because you are a Pseudo-Primordial doesn’t mean we are equals. Let this be a lesson to you." Without another word, the Second Flame Matriarch teleported out of the arena and reappeared somewhere in the Legion Tower.
She sat down under a tree and started to meditate.
Ruby shook her head and smiled. "How disappointing."
She also teleported out of the arena, leaving Kent and everyone wondering about so many things.
In the end, however, Kent just smirked and left the Arena with his wives. His legion followed, and a few minutes later, they were staring at the legion rankings.
Seated at the top, of course, was Grand Shaman Vorgun.

chapters.title: Chapter 1882: Undead Reunion
paragraphs: Grand Shaman Vorgun surely deserved first place, considering the kind of assistance he had offered Kent and the legion during the Dark War.

Not only did he single-handedly create over a thousand Soul Fiends, but he was also able to upgrade each one to the peak of the Celestial stage, something that allowed them to handle more of the pressure, allowing the rest of his teammates to have it easy.
So, having the most points surely didn’t come as a shock to anyone.
The second with the most points in the legion, of course, was Dia again. Her points in the harem ranking were enough to win her a spot in the legion ranking, too.
Then came third, and this time it was Shade King Nykali who took that spot.
Just like Grand Shaman Vorgun, he also possesses the ability to weaponize souls. His ability allows him to turn ordinary souls into soul wraiths, or, as he prefers to call them, Shades.
So he used it well during the Dark War, and aside from merely ranking third, he also managed to upgrade his Shades to a much higher grade.
The fourth spot was taken by Veera, whose undead warriors had proven to be rather resilient. They gave her an edge, and that alone allowed her to rank that high.
Thankfully, Adina came fifth, and the remaining spots were filled by Zaila, Elsa, and the rest.
"You all did great. Personally, I am not sure my points will rank even in the top thirty, so you all should be proud," Kent said to his legion, causing them all to smile and nod.
"Tower will take you to the place to pick the rewards I have prepared. Afterwards, after I am done handling some business, we will plan how to handle the missions ahead of us."

Kent knew better, so he turned and looked at Kaizo. "Of course, if you have nothing to do, use the time to clear the rest of the dungeons. We can’t keep the other members of the Eternal Wrath Legion waiting."
They soon dispersed, and Kent decided to meet with the undead legion to have a much-needed catch-up, considering he had sent them on a mission.
However, before the meeting could start, Kent noticed something peculiar.
He paused before he could say what he was about to say and scanned the faces of the people around him. One face stood out, and this time he noticed it.
For a moment, no words were spoken.
Then Kent smiled and stepped forward. "I honestly don’t understand why you chose to wear a disguise before me, Dominique."
The Third Undead Princess, who perhaps wished to check whether Kent could see through her disguise, smiled and removed it, revealing her pale face, a look that showed she was indeed an undead.
"One would never know until they try." She walked closer to Kent and hugged him. "Nice to see you again, Sanders. Or do you prefer I call you Kent instead?"
"Whichever works for you," Kent hugged her back...
Kaizo and his pals knew the two needed some alone time, so they moved back.
After hugging for a few minutes, Kent pulled back and looked at Dominique. "The last time we saw each other, you tried to kill me."
Dominique blushed, but she nodded. "I did try, didn’t I?"
Kent just smirked, knowing she didn’t truly mean to kill him. If she had meant her attacks, perhaps things would have ended much more chaotically.
Kent took her hand and walked to a bench under a tree somewhere in the Legion Tower. His wives had noticed the presence of another powerhouse, so he could already sense their gazes on them.

However, since he held her hand, none of them tried to approach them, fearing that something might happen to Kent. But then again, who were they kidding to even think someone inside the tower could harm Kent?
"How have you been, Dominique?"

"What can I say? After you left, I went into seclusion to recover my strength and increase my cultivation. I spent millions of years doing that. Afterwards, I spent the rest of the time working around the clock to increase my summons."
She looked around for a few seconds before snapping her fingers, causing five portals to open—four purple portals and one red portal.
Kent furrowed his brow when the portals opened. He knew what was coming, but still, he was stunned when the portals opened.
From the four purple portals, four Pseudo-Primordials, each powerful enough to shake the heart of an army, walked out.
Kent recognized one of them.
"White Lady," he said, smiling at the lady clad in white armor.
She scanned Kent with a hateful gaze before turning to stare at Sylara, who held a smug expression on her face.
"I see she still hasn’t forgotten about what happened back then," Kent said, referring to the White Lady, who still seemed pissed.
"Just give her some time. I am sure she will come around."𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎

Kent just laughed and looked at the three other Pseudo-Primordials. All of them are what the undead call Ancients. They are a special kind of undead, possessing powers far more dreadful than those of regular undead.
They first appeared when Sanders went to the Undead Realm. In fact, Kaizo is the first-ever Ancient, for he was the first-ever undead Kent had created.
Later, he got to know that the Ancients came from a realm unknown even to him. Long story short, he managed to find a way to summon them.

She summoned the White Lady, and back when she sided with her father to attack him, the White Lady fought Sylara. Safe to say she was defeated, and that defeat had followed her ever since then.

From within stepped a figure who possessed no aura, yet as she walked out, everyone inside the Legion Tower stopped whatever they were doing and turned in her direction.
"Oh damn... she’s hot." Kent blurted out, absentmindedly

chapters.title: Chapter 1883: Athena
paragraphs: Maybe Kent never meant to say those words out loud.
However, considering the beauty of the lady who had walked out of the portal, the words just came out. But who could blame him? In fact, the lady was indeed stunning.
Kent would be lying if he said she wasn’t the most beautiful woman he had seen in his life, and that says a lot when, especially, there is someone like Adina in his harem.
Thus far, Adina is the most beautiful woman in his harem.
However, this Undead Ancient is far more beautiful than she is.

She possesses a pair of long, silver-blue hair, so long, in fact, that they seem to sweep the ground behind her. Dia beats her in the hair department for length, but her hair is still incredibly long.
Her skin is flawlessly pale white, with not even an atomic defect visible. Every aspect of her complexion is pristine, pretty, and enchanting.
As for her facial features, she has an oval-shaped face, deep blue eyes, and a smile that seemed to bring meaning to just about anything.
Every step she took sent waves of attraction to almost everyone. In fact, aside from Kent, even his wives were mesmerized by her beauty.
The only ones who managed to resist her allure were Pandora, Mjolnir, and Fiannarel. Even Kent was taken by surprise by just how good-looking she was.
Noticing the look on his face, Dominique smiled and introduced her fifth Undead Ancient. "She is the War Goddess Athena, my strongest Ancient."
Athena stopped beside Dominique and bowed, revealing her cleavage, which, judging by the size of her breasts, made Kent feel his heart tremble.
"Nice to meet the infamous Bone Lich Undead Emperor." Her tone was just as enchanting.

"Pleasure meeting you too, Athena," Kent replied, taking a deep breath before adding, "If you don’t mind me asking, how can an undead become a Primordial? The last I checked, undead beings cannot comprehend the Origin Dao, meaning they can’t become Primordials."

Athena smiled and answered, "That is true. Undead beings cannot become Primordials. However, that rule only applies when one is in this universe. The moment they step out of this universe, they can sense and comprehend the Origin Dao."
Kent nodded, slightly expecting such an answer.
He knew with certainty that the rules could be bent to suit one’s desires, so hearing it from Athena wasn’t too shocking, as one would have expected.
He was even sure the Undead Monarch had already reached the realm of a Primordial. After all, back when they fought, he was already at the Pseudo-Primordial stage.
The question now is, where would one go aside from the Primordial Chaos to comprehend the Origin Dao?
The answer isn’t one he is ready to hear. But even if there were such a mysterious place, Kent also knew, and he even possessed a place where his undead could comprehend the Origin Dao...
Chaos Chasm, the world of the Chaos Ascension King.
Since it is his birthright and he has already claimed the legacy that came with it, he can easily use it, and he most certainly has plans to do so...
Kent turned to Dominique. "I suppose getting her wasn’t easy."
"Indeed. I had to go into seclusion for millions of years just to gather enough Necrotic Qi. Luckily for me, after she was summoned, things have been moving in the right direction."
Kent turned and looked at Athena again before turning back to Dominique. "That is good to hear."

He allowed his mind to settle before asking the question that had come to mind. "Though it is good to see you again, I can’t help but think of what your old man will do if he finds out you left the Undead Realm to come see me. So why did you risk coming here?"
Dominique sighed before answering, "Because I need your help... well, we need your help in the upcoming war between my kind and the Abyssal Chaos."
"Oh, the Abyssal Chaos? What about them?"
Safe to say, Kent’s interest had been piqued at the mention of the Abyssal Chaos. He had a past with that place since his parents were still there, so he wanted to know more...
"I know it has been years since you left, but during that time, a new Abyssal Chaos King rose, and he has been pushing for an invasion.

The Abyssal Realm had, in the past, locked the gateway to their realm to avoid being attacked. Naturally, the next places they can attack are the Undead Realm, the Resentful Realm, or the Infinity Universe.

My father discovered a couple of years ago that the target realm they planned to attack is the Undead Realm. If that is indeed the case, there is a chance the Undead Realm will be brought to its last legs this time.
My father will never ask for your help, so when I noticed Kaizo and the others had returned to the Undead Realm, I had to find a way to meet you."𝙛𝓻𝒆𝓮𝒘𝙚𝙗𝒏𝙤𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝒐𝙢
Kent nodded, not too bothered. He owed nothing to the Undead Realm, and he most certainly owed nothing to the Undead Monarch, so saving them wasn’t something he would even consider.
However, they were talking about the Abyssal Chaos. If such a powerhouse had risen in recent years while he was away, he had to speed up his plans and return there for his parents.
Before, he wasn’t someone who could roam there. Now, however, he could cultivate both Chaos Qi and Abyssal Qi, so he would be like a fish in water there.
"Do you have an estimation of when they may attack?"
"No. However, my father met with some of the Undead Barons, and from what they discussed, it seems they have already started preparing, so I estimate this will happen within the next 1,000 years.
Of course, the reason I came also had to do with what Athena discovered. It appears some insidious forces have infiltrated the Undead Realm and are slowly corrupting it from within.

You once claimed that a race in this universe had been corrupted once. I want to know if you have found a way to root them out. If not, by the time the Abyssal Chaos attacks, we will be reduced to nothing by this unknown corruption."
