chapters.title: Chapter 1884: A Chance
paragraphs: Kent allowed his mind to wander a little, recalling some events that had transpired in the past, most especially during his incarnation as the Bone Lich Undead Emperor.
Back when he and the Undead Monarch were in conflict, Sanders had actually sensed, on multiple occasions, an insidious presence working behind the scenes to influence events.

Most of the time, he felt as though the Undead Monarch was being influenced by them. Of course, he had no idea who or what was at work, but he knew for a fact that somewhere deep within the Undead Realm, something very rotten was slowly corrupting them.
Today, he seemed to have received confirmation of that. Though there was a question he had to ask...
Kent turned and looked at Athena. "You discovered the corruption, right? How did you manage that?"
Athena smiled and answered, "I have a natural affinity for nature."
Kent furrowed his brow, clearly not expecting to hear such an absurd statement from an undead. Nature energy wasn’t something undead beings with an affinity for Necrotic Qi were expected to possess.
In fact, access to Divine Essence, which comes from natural essence, wasn’t something undead beings were supposed to have an affinity for.
But Athena seemed to possess an affinity for it, and that was just mind-blowing.
Dominique smiled, seeing how shocked Kent had become after learning that Athena had an affinity for natural essence.

"Athena is a unique kind of undead. In fact, she doesn’t even have an affinity for Necrotic Qi like most of us. It baffles me sometimes how she even lives as an undead when the natural energy that sustains us isn’t something she possesses."
"That is indeed strange, but in a way, also great. At least with someone like her by your side, I wouldn’t have to worry about the corruption getting to you."

"She said the exact same thing to me." Dominique looked at Athena and smiled. "To be frank, she has been a blessing ever since she was summoned by me. Sometimes, I think she was a gift sent to be with me."
Athena smiled sweetly, her beauty further amplified.

Kent just nodded and asked, "Can you explain to me what you sensed..." Kent paused and turned into the distance, meeting Dia’s gaze. No words were exchanged, but the next second, Dia teleported and appeared beside him.
"You can speak now. Dia here is an expert when it comes to corruption."
Athena nodded and narrowed her eyes at Dia, perhaps because she could sense some form of power that went directly against her nature.
She didn’t react negatively, though, since she knew Dia was with Kent, and Dominique had a good relationship with Kent.
Saying or doing anything against her would provoke Kent’s wrath, and from what she knew of Kent, she had no plans to provoke him.
"I first sensed it when I travelled to one of the Undead Graves. Hidden somewhere deep within, there is a presence far more dreadful than any of the horrors living there.

This presence, from what I sensed, possessed some kind of power that, even by merely sensing it, tried to corrupt my soul. Luckily for me, I am not easily corrupted, so I managed to resist. However, the millions of beings living there aren’t like me.
Hidden within their souls, from what I could sense, were seeds of corruption that would one day bloom, and when that day comes, I am sure the Undead Realm will feel the wrath of that corruption."
Kent didn’t say much and instead closed his eyes and snapped his fingers, summoning a golden-red eye. The moment the Eye of Chaos appeared, Athena felt her mind clear and her senses open.
"Now, I want you to imagine what happened when you tried to sense the corruption back then."

Athena nodded despite having so many questions she wanted to ask first. She took a deep breath. Then, reaching into her memories, she began to recall the moment she sensed the seed of corruption, or perhaps the true corruption.
The moment she began, the space around them shifted, and a freezing atmosphere enveloped everyone. The feeling soon deepened when, out of nowhere, a howl came from in front of Athena.

The howl caused everyone inside the tower to pause their actions and turn to look at a monkey-like silhouette made of smoke. The moment the construct appeared, Kent formed a hand seal, and at once, a cage appeared around the shadow monkey.
"Dia, manifest it as a heart demon and send it into my soul."

Dia nodded and, without any hesitation, walked closer and grabbed the monkey by the neck. The monkey tried to resist, but before it could, she gave it a hard squeeze, and it exploded into a cloud of smoke that drifted into the air behind Kent.
The Eye of Chaos closed, and the coldness in the air also vanished.𝘧𝓇𝑒𝑒𝑤ℯ𝑏𝓃𝘰𝑣ℯ𝘭.𝘤ℴ𝘮
"I will be right back."
Kent closed his eyes, and the next second, he was inside his Soul Sea.
Hades and Lady Kenzie stood before a pale, shadowy man with the features of a monkey.
"What’s this thing, Lord Chaos?" Hades asked, looking a bit disgusted by the presence of this being inside Kent’s soul.
"It is a manifestation of corruption I was hoping to study and, if possible, track its origin," Kent answered while getting a better look at the shadowy figure.
"It is horrible to look at," Lady Kenzie complained, and Kent just smiled. He knew she would hate it because corruption and life are enemies.
So, as someone who represents life, even if she wanted to, she would feel disgusted by the presence of this shadowy figure.
"Relax, guys. I just want to test something. Once I am done, I will put it down."
They nodded and stepped back for Kent to work. The earlier he got this thing out of his soul, the better for them.
Kent examined the shadowy figure for a few seconds. Then he stopped before it and asked, "You are in the presence of the Primordial Chaos Dragon. State your name and purpose."
The shadowy figure said nothing, not even flinching.
Kent didn’t mind the lack of reaction.
He even smiled.
Then he walked closer and pressed his finger against the shadowy figure’s forehead.
"Soul Search."
Kent invoked a soul technique, and at once, his face paled...

chapters.title: Chapter 1885: Deeper Corruption
paragraphs: Everything happened so fast that before everyone knew it, Kent was already on the ground, his expression pale and his body practically drained of all energy.
Yet again, Kent came close to death had it not been for Lady Kenzie and Hades stepping in when he needed help.
Since they are connected to his life and death, respectively, whenever his life is threatened, Lady Kenzie handles that, and when death tries to claim him, Hades handles that.
Just now, something dreadful tried to take him down, but they were already connected to him, so they managed to stop it from happening.
Lady Kenzie and Hades appeared on the outside just as Kent was drained to make sure his body was also protected. There was no better way to ensure Kent’s safety than these two.

"Master, you really should take your life and death more seriously," Lady Kenzie said, casting a healing spell on Kent while Hades worked on taking away the lingering aura of death on and within Kent’s soul.
Dia, however, removed the heart demon and caged it again.

Luckily, Kent didn’t pass out this time, so after a few minutes of healing, he was back on his feet, though he was still weak from what he had experienced when he tried to soul-search the shadowy fiend.
"Kent, what happened?" Dia asked, looking worried.
Kent just smiled and brushed his hand through her hair. "Nothing too crazy. I just performed a soul search on the shadowy fiend, and I may have overstepped my boundaries."
Dia narrowed her eyes at him and frowned. "You call that nothing too crazy? Just what is considered crazy in your books then?"
Kent just smiled but didn’t answer her question.
Rather, he turned and looked at the shadowy fiend and sighed.

"All I can say is, the undead realm is in grave danger, one that, if not handled well, will doom your kind. I hate to say this, but even I can’t handle it alone unless your old man is willing to provide me with the resources I’ll need.
But I think we both know that will be difficult, considering the kind of hatred he has for me is far deeper than the one he has for his mortal enemies."
Kent smirked and continued.

"Honestly, I don’t even know why he hates me. We used to be friends, you know. He and I explored some of the most dreadful zones in the undead realm back in the day. So I don’t even know what changed for him to become bitter toward me."
Dominique sighed, knowing that, indeed, things would be extremely complex if Kent and her father were to see eye to eye.
"But there is a silver lining, though, and I think if we work together, we will be able to get him on board."
Dominique’s interest was piqued, causing her to knit her brow and look at Kent with a curious gaze. "I am listening."
"So when I tried the soul search on the shadowy fiend, I managed to see some memories that belonged to the corruption it came from.
Apparently, the reason why the Abyssal Chaos will be attacking your home is because of something precious hidden in your realm.
I don’t know what they want from the undead realm, but their interest in it is so great that they planned to use the abyssal race to get it.

Of course, they haven’t accounted for my presence in any of this. However, they clearly underestimate me when I say that the attack on your realm would not happen, since I had plans to go to the Abyssal Chaos within the next 200 years."
"Oh, that is new." Dominique and Athena furrowed their brows, each wondering why someone like Kent would drop everything and go to such a dreadful place.
They knew he wasn’t going because the undead realm was threatened. In fact, Dominique didn’t even see him agreeing to help her kind deal with the corruption and the Abyssal Chaos.
The last she checked, Kent was driven away by her kind, and so he owed them nothing.
How then was he going there...

"Relax, I am not going there to wage war. There are some people close to me imprisoned there, and I intend to bring them back. That said, while there, anything can happen, so we can work some things out and, if possible, involve your old man or not involve him.
Regardless, in the next 200 years, there is a chance your people would have to step in, or I will handle everything without them knowing.

But as Athena had said, this corruption has already corrupted a lot of horrors in the undead realm, so that part, whether your old man likes it or not, he either compromises with me or I will happily stand on the side and watch your realm burn to the ground."
Dominique nodded, wearing a serious expression.

At least their trip wasn’t for nothing. They managed to identify the issue with the Abyssal Chaos, but they knew that before Kent returned to the Undead Realm, he and the Undead Monarch would have to sit down and reach a compromise.

"You must know that the moment the events in the Abyssal Chaos are disrupted by me, the corruption will activate its second plan. So if there are going to be any discussions, they should happen within the next 200 years.

We would have to set up safeguards to handle the chances of anything happening. Of course, if the undead realm is destined to fall, you have a place here with me, so you shouldn’t worry too much."𝒇𝒓𝙚𝒆𝔀𝓮𝓫𝒏𝓸𝙫𝓮𝓵.𝓬𝙤𝙢
Dominique nodded, but she knew that, as the Third Undead Princess of the Undead Realm, it was her duty to ensure her people were protected.
So, unless it was a last resort, she would not abandon them.
She nodded, wearing a serious expression.
Seeing this, Kent just smiled.

"Relax a little, Dominique. While your father is difficult and borderline insane, he is still the monarch who loves his people, so he will see reason. But even if he doesn’t, when the time comes, I will just unleash the full extent of my Bone Lich Undead Necromancy Class and handle everything on my own."
Kent laughed, though he was being extremely serious.

paragraphs: [Planet Nila]
Planet Nila is one of the largest celestial-grade planets in the universe. It is home to the Blue Horn Tigerkin, one of the most dangerous beastkins in the universe.
Legend has it that during the Primordial Era, the Ancestor of the Blue Horn Tigerkin fought side by side with the Primordial Chaos Dragon during the Great War.
But before that, he was crowned as one of the most dreadful beasts during the Primordial Era, second only to a few.
Due to this influence and his survival of the Great War, many saw him as a legend whose name alone struck fear into the hearts of many.
He had earned his name in the history books, and that alone placed him on the same ranking as the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
Due to his influence, his descendants seem to think they are invincible.
They drag themselves around with a chip on their shoulders, thinking that just because they came from the family tree of the Blue Horn Tiger Ancestor, they can do as they please and get away with it.
Ten weeks ago, one of the descendants, a Supreme, travelled to a planet not far from Planet Nila with ten Celestials as his guards.
This particular Blue Horn Tigerkin is famous for taking advantage of ladies and later disposing of them to shut them up.
He had done so many times before, but because of his influence and backing, nobody dared hold him accountable for it.
That was until he met her, a lady whose sister was kidnapped and sold to a brothel where this Blue Horn Tigerkin happened to have booked that very day.
Unfortunately for him, the sister of this very dangerous lady caught his eye, so he chose to buy her for the night.
Safe to say, things didn’t end well for him.
That night, the lady tracked her sister to that brothel, and that very night, the brothel was wiped from the face of the universe.

That night, over 300 people died, including all 10 Celestial guards the Blue Horn Tigerkin brought. She rescued her sister and made sure the Blue Horn Tigerkin would never again have the means to touch any lady.
She used a special method to cut his dick off. This method, of course, prevents any form of healing or regeneration. Meaning the Blue Horn Tigerkin can never walk around with a dick ever again.

That was unforgivable, so he called home, and after five days of chasing, they managed to capture the lady and set out to execute her today to wash away the shame she had brought upon the Blue Horn Tigerkin family.

Today, gathered in a large arena are descendants of the Blue Horn Tigerkin race and others who have come to witness the death of someone whose legend has spread throughout the Celestial Realm for thousands of years.
"I never expected a day would come when the infamous Blood Harvester would be bound in shackles, ready to be slaughtered like a dog," someone in the audience said, playing with his beard.
"I know, right? When she began to gain fame, many thought she was the reincarnation of that dreadful fiend from the Blood Era. Who would have thought she was even far more dreadful than that?"
"She sure is more dangerous than that person. However, to think she had killed over 300 Celestials before she was caught, I don’t know any Supreme alive who can pull something like that off."
"I know a demigod who can," someone else said, joining the conversation...

The man with the beard turned and looked at the person who spoke. "If you are talking about Kent Madson, then I have to say, while he is someone none of us can make sense of, he has yet to prove he is capable of surpassing the Blood Harvester."

He played with his beard and added, "I don’t know if any of you have read the history books, but for us to say this lady is more dreadful than the original Blood Harvester, you must understand she is indeed a fiend.

The original Blood Harvester was someone who walked side by side with the Blood Spear King. She fought in all the major battles that plagued the Blood Era, and she stood tall as the last of the Blood Fiends were dealt with.

Legends even had it that she singlehandedly killed two Primordials and over a dozen Pseudo-Primordials. If the history books didn’t exaggerate, then I hope you now understand the kind of person we are comparing this lady to."
Everyone who heard what the bearded man said turned to look at the bound redhead, her head lowered, blood trickling down from the many injuries she had sustained.
"Damn, I never knew a day would come when I would sympathise with a criminal. But I feel like she should be freed. She doesn’t deserve to die for defending herself and protecting her sister."
In the end, the words of the outsiders held no substance when it came to the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family.
After the time reached the middle of the day, a Pseudo-Primordial clad in a green tiger-patterned robe walked into the arena holding a large sword. The blade of the sword had dried blood on it.
This showed it was a sword they had used several times to execute people who had wronged their family.
The moment he walked into the arena, all talking died down.
"Good day, everyone, and thank you all for coming on such short notice," the Pseudo-Primordial Blue Horn Tigerkin said as he scanned the arena.

"I know most of you have this idea that this criminal deserves to live. However, I say she deserves to die because her crimes are ones that cannot be forgiven. She laid hands on an heir of my race, and she went ahead to kill over 200 of our warriors.
The last time someone dared to try that, they were cut down, so hold your sympathy, for she will die today, and there is nothing anyone under or above the heavens can say to stop or prevent that."
Chills ran down everyone’s spines as his words reached their ears.
He turned and looked at the Blood Harvester, whose expression remained calm despite death staring at her.
"Any last words before you are escorted to the underworld..."
The arena went quiet for a few seconds before a male voice spread through the space...
"She doesn’t, but I do."

"I don’t want to make things hard for you and your family since I have a history with your ancestor. Consider that as me making your life easy. I wouldn’t just commit a slaughter without giving you a chance to take a step back.
Of course, my patience can only be tested for a moment. As to what happens next, trust me, I will not hesitate to cut every last one of you down."
Kent took a deep breath and took one step forward, causing the very ground before him to crack. He took one more step forward, and the ice on the ground melted and evaporated.

"The person you are about to execute is someone you do not want to cross. Trust me, if you dare point your weapon at her one more time, not only will your family be wiped off the face of the universe, but there will be no chance of reincarnation."

Though Kent’s words sounded funny, given that he was merely a demigod, many sensed he was very serious. He meant what he said, and that was now showing as everyone gathered started to wonder just who they had come to watch being executed.
"Such big words from a no-name. If you dare, reveal your name to us and see if you or your family will live to tell the tale of your miserable life."
Suddenly, ten new individuals, each having the aura of a Pseudo-Primordial, appeared in the air.
They were all Tigerkins and far stronger than the Pseudo-Primordial who had come to execute the Blood Harvester. The moment they appeared, the pressure in the air increased, forcing Kent to frown.
He looked up and met the gazes of the ten new arrivals.
"So I assume you have made up your minds, huh?"
"Is that even a question? Even if you are the reincarnation of the Grim Reaper, you wouldn’t be able to stop us today, so leave while we are still being generous."
Kent sighed, and then he turned toward the Blood Harvester. "Raise your head and look at me."
His words were calm, but unlike before, when the Blood Harvester didn’t even bother to look at the Pseudo-Primordial, she slowly and painfully lifted her head and looked at Kent.

"The universe hasn’t been kind to you, too, huh?" A smile appeared on his face. "Back then, when you made the decision to sacrifice yourself, I prayed to the heavens to give you a good reincarnation. I suppose my prayer fell on deaf ears.
However, I am here now, stepsister, and I will make sure you have the best life ever."
Kent pointed his finger forward, and before the Pseudo-Primordial Tigerkins could stop him, a red rune shot forward and merged with the Blood Harvester’s forehead.
Everything happened so fast that before anyone knew it, a beam of light came from the heavens and bathed the Blood Harvester.
BOOOM
A deadly explosion came from her body, followed by a painful scream that sent shivers down the spines of everyone gathered.
"Hahahahahahahaha..." Kent raised his head and let out hearty laughter.

"You idiots clearly don’t know who you have offended. I gave you a chance to step back and put everything behind you, but I suppose you all wish for death more than anything, so you had to act stubbornly.
Now, your fate is sealed, and there is nothing even I can do to change that. Not even your ancestor can do anything to change that."
Kent’s laughter continued to spread throughout the arena, prompting the audience to wonder why.
Suddenly, someone in the audience asked, "Mister, if you don’t mind me asking, who is this lady?"
Kent turned to the person who asked the question. "She goes by many names and titles, but a very long time ago, she was known as the Blood Harvester."

chapters.title: Chapter 1892: The One Who Harvests Blood
paragraphs: "Are you saying this lady is the original Blood Harvester?" Everyone turned pale, waiting for confirmation from Kent despite knowing deep in their hearts that, indeed, the person they had all come to witness get executed was that dreadful fiend from the Blood Era.
The signs were already there and had been there from the start.
She didn’t name herself, but her deeds gave her that name.
From the moment people started to notice her, whenever she killed an opponent, no matter how dangerous the situation was, she wouldn’t fail to harvest their blood essence.
Every last soul she had killed, she harvested their blood essence, something only the Blood Harvester was known to do.
Initially, many were hesitant to give her such a name, but as time went by and more of her deeds spread across the celestial realm, the name naturally became hers.

But people who knew the legend of the original Blood Harvester still became hesitant when they referred to this lady by that name. Safe to say, they all feared Kent’s answer, for if it was true, then they were all at risk.

The legacy the original Blood Harvester had left wasn’t straightforward. She had had her fair share of ups and downs, and most of them were her own decisions that, in today’s universe, many considered evil.

One time, she slaughtered and harvested the blood of an entire battalion simply because one of them assaulted a mother and her daughter. She should have just killed that one warrior, but no, she killed all 12,000 of them.
What if she awakened right now and decided to slaughter everyone simply because they had come to watch her get executed?
Kent smiled, perhaps sensing their worry.
But he didn’t answer the question with a yes or no. Rather, to buy time, he decided to tell a story...

He flew a bit higher and started to speak... "A very long time ago, a young, beautiful lady, born to a loving father and mother, both pacifists, decided to embark on a path that went contrary to what she was raised to believe in.𝑓𝓇𝘦ℯ𝘸𝘦𝑏𝓃𝑜𝘷ℯ𝑙.𝑐𝑜𝓂
"This young lady, keen and determined, entered the infamous Blood Trial, the same trial that, years later, the legendary Blood Spear King would dominate.

Of course, what many didn’t know was that before the Blood Spear King dominated that trial, the young lady who would later be known as the Blood Harvester had come face to face with the Blood Monarch, who later on invaded this universe and nearly reduced every living soul to a pool of blood.
When they met, they fought, and he was injured by the Blood Harvester. That battle bought the universe enough time for its heroes to rise and defend it.
I know she had her ups and downs, but we all know that in the grand scheme of things, her role during the Blood Era significantly impacted this universe and everyone living in it.

She was selfless, determined and willing to do everything necessary to ensure life was preserved. Lastly, when the Blood War neared its climax, she was the one who laid down her life to ensure the universe was ushered into another era where life as we know it continued to thrive."
Kent paused and smiled, looking at the grim expressions that had appeared on the faces of everyone, especially the 11 elders of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family.

"So allow me to spell out something to you all. You see, after she had willingly laid down her life, using her blood and soul to seal away the devastation of the Blood Race, one would expect her to have a good reincarnation.
"But no, you losers decided to chase her down, arrest and beat her up, then tie her down and order a public execution." Kent’s voice dropped low, a wave of killing intent coming out through his eyes.
"Do you losers even have an idea of the kind of people you have offended? I mean, the Blood Harvester was someone known to have led a legion called the Blood Hounds during the Blood Era.
"As far as one is concerned, the history books recorded only 340 dead after the Blood War, meaning 259 are still alive and somewhere out there waiting for their general to awaken.

"Judging by the kind of legend they had left in their wake, do you seriously think they would take kindly to what you had done to their general? I mean, even I am this close to annihilating every last one of you, down to the last seed bearing your bloodline.
"Eliza is a war hero, someone who has been given a true name by the universe for her service to mankind. Do you seriously think such a person is someone you can mess with?"

Kent’s eyes turned red, showing he was pissed now... "You know what, none of you qualify to answer me, so allow me to call someone who can explain to me why I shouldn’t annihilate your entire Blue Horn Tigerkin Family."
"Tsh, do you think you have what it takes to threaten my family?" one of the elders sneered, a dark expression of disdain on his face.
"But I do." Kent grinned and turned to Ruby. "Kill him."
"With pleasure."
Ruby smiled and turned to face the elder who spoke. He still had the look of disdain on his face, but before he could say anything, Ruby moved, and a head flew into the air.
For a moment, everyone was left wondering when Ruby would make her move.
It took some people a minute to finally register what had happened. When they did, every last one of them turned pale white like a sheet.
"Now that I have proven I can threaten your Blue Horn Tigerkin Family, allow me to summon the one who can explain to me what the hell you losers have done to my stepsister."
Kent’s eyes narrowed, then, out of nowhere, a voice from far away spoke, "Get your ass over here, Cassius. Don’t let me repeat myself."
For a moment, nothing happened. But then space cracked, and a figure radiating a presence that the universe seemed threatened by stepped out.

chapters.title: Chapter 1893: Blue Horn Tigerkin Ancestor
paragraphs: "An-Ancestor," one of the 10 remaining elders of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family muttered, his voice breaking as he stared at the middle-aged man who had walked out of the portal.

To many generations of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family, their infamous ancestor, who walked shoulder to shoulder with the Primordial Chaos Dragon during the Primordial Era, was merely a myth told by their elders.
In fact, after several eras had passed, the people who could boldly say they had met the ancestor could be counted on one hand.
So, expecting him to show up here today wasn’t on any of their to-do lists when they woke up today.
Yet here he was, his striking blonde hair flowing down his back, a small smile tugging at the corner of his lips as his deep blue eyes gazed back at Kent.
If one didn’t know better, one would say he had just turned 20.
His appearance and age didn’t align.
But then again, in the world of cultivation, beings billions of years old can sometimes look like a 16-year-old. Preserving one’s youth is something one can easily do if they want to.

Ahead of him, the heavens started preparing to strike in case he dared use his power on anyone. It was clear that he was several times stronger than one would think, perhaps even stronger than the limit the universe had set.
After he was fully out of the void gate, it closed behind him.
All ten elders went down on their knees, and just before they could greet their ancestor, 5 more appeared, followed by a sixth who had the aura of a Primordial.
She went down on her knees and bowed.
"We greet the ancestor."
The others followed in her steps, "We greet the ancestor."

Every last one of them, including the thousands of Blue Horn Tigerkin around the arena, went down on their knees and greeted their ancestor as a show of respect, especially considering the current matriarch of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family had taken the lead.
Just as they were done greeting, one of the ten elders pointed his finger at Kent, "Ancestor, deal with this bas—"
He wasn’t done with his statement when his body disintegrated into nothingness, leaving nothing but shock behind.
Those who saw what happened stared at the blonde-haired man in shock. All it took was a single glance from him, and a Pseudo-Primordial was reduced to nothing.
Kent smirked and flew much higher into the air, "Looks like your descendants only grew weaker and more useless as the eras passed, Cassius."
The blonde-haired man who went by Cassius smiled and nodded, "It appears so..." He paused and smirked before acknowledging Kent. "Old Friend."
Kent just laughed while the thousands of people gathered, especially the Blue Horn Tigerkins, were stunned, some widening their eyes at the sound of their ancestor calling Kent "Old Friend."
Just what does that mean?
"Old Friend, you say?" Kent laughed. "I suppose you are right to call me that. After all, we fought side by side back in the day. Which is also why I held back and didn’t slaughter your descendants.
However, it goes without saying, they had offended someone they shouldn’t have. In fact, right now, there is a chance every last one of them will be reduced to blood mist when she wakes up.
I don’t want that to happen, and you sure don’t want it to happen, so what can you do or say to help me convince her when she wakes up?

I don’t know where you are now, but the fact that you were able to send a clone over on such short notice shows you are not far from the universe, and so you probably know what the Blood Harvester is capable of?"
Cassius nodded, a sigh escaping his lips.
He indeed had some idea of what would happen when Eliza, or as she was known far and wide, the Blood Harvester, woke up; things would be super difficult for his descendants.
But did he even care what happened to them?
Maybe not.
However, he wasn’t the only one to survive the Primordial Era and form a family. If they were wiped out right now, it would stain his reputation.
So, inasmuch as he was disappointed in his descendants, he knew he had to step in and save them.𝐟𝗿𝐞𝚎𝚠𝐞𝚋𝕟𝐨𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝕔𝕠𝚖
"I know pleading for their lives isn’t something I should be doing. They bear my name, but they aren’t me, so their life and death shouldn’t be determined by me.
However, for the sake of our shared camaraderie, I would ask that you offer mercy this once. I am willing to bargain for their lives with this."
He waved his hand, and a pill bottle holding a golden substance flew toward Kent. He caught it and then, using the Eye of Chaos, he scanned it.
[You have discovered a Primordial Grade Blood Essence]
Kent’s brow furrowed. "Oh, you came prepared."
Cassius smiled. "Knowing your opponent is half the battle won."
"That is indeed true. However, as to whether she accepts this will depend on her, though I can say with this, she will be a bit merciful."
"As long as she doesn’t lay waste to my descendants, I don’t really care what she does with them. But for the sake of what we shared in the past, I do hope you will say something for me, Old Friend."

Kent laughed, but he nodded. "Fear not, I always treat people who stand for what is right as friends. At the end of the day, there is a chance we will fight side by side once again, so the last thing I want is to get on your bad side."
Cassius smiled and nodded...
Then he turned and looked at the matriarch of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family...

"Let this be the first and last warning. If you somehow survive this ordeal, you will ensure that anyone, irrespective of how insignificant they are, as long as they have my blood flowing through them, behaves themselves.
All who step out of line will have their cultivation crippled and bloodline stripped, forever destined to rot in hell."

chapters.title: Chapter 1894: Blood Harvester
paragraphs: The warning was very simple, but every last descendant of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Race, regardless of where they were—be it the mortal realm, Immortal, God, Supreme or Celestial realms—they all felt it in their blood.
Clearly, Cassius didn’t just say those words for show.
He made sure they became a rule, which showed just how deep his understanding of the Dao was. He was able to turn mere words into rules, and nobody even seemed to realise it had happened.
’It appears he is far stronger than a Primordial,’ Kent smiled, clearly pleased with Cassius’s strength.
If he were this strong, perhaps, when the time came, he would be able to help defend his universe as he fought the horrors that threatened existence.

The matriarch of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family bowed toward Cassius and said, "We have all taken the ancestor’s words to heart, and I personally will ensure nobody with your bloodline will step out of line.
"If such a person ever appears, I will personally ensure they don’t see the light of day. That is my promise to you, Ancestor."

Cassius smirked. "Whatever. Just know that this dragon isn’t someone you can mess with. Trust me, even I have no plans of messing with him, and look at me, my clone is practically a threat to the universe."

Everyone present in the arena turned and looked at Kent, their minds wondering just what kind of existence he was for a whole powerhouse like the ancestor of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Race to show him this much respect.

Right now, Kent had morphed his appearance to look like Chaos, the Primordial Chaos Dragon. Since Chaos was a true Dragon and Kent himself was a dragon, he now stood 7 feet tall, his presence as imposing as ever.
And now that he had been shown this much respect by Cassius, one could already see some form of otherworldly aura coming off him.
In fact, Kent himself had started to sense some form of aura that wasn’t of this universe coming out of him after he read the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy manual.
This had made him appear more mysterious to everyone, and since he had changed his appearance, nobody recognised him as Kent Madson.
He knew what he wanted, so he chose this look to fool everyone yet send a very loud message.
Of course, the critical thinkers among them began to put two and two together after hearing so much already.
"Dragon, Primordial Era," the bearded man who seemed to know more about the Blood Harvester muttered, his mind spinning. Judging by the badge on his chest, he was from the Cult of Wisdom.
"Don’t tell me he is the Primordial Chaos Dragon." His words, however, triggered a wave of silence that enveloped everyone.
Every last soul who heard him took a moment to settle their thoughts before they turned to face him.
"Hey, Old Matin, what nonsense are you spouting? How can this kid be the legendary Primordial Chaos Dragon?"
"Yes, are you perhaps tired of your life and wish to call down the wrath of the heavens by speaking nonsense and blasphemy?"

Old Matin smiled and answered, "I didn’t say those words with no evidence, everyone. I said it because I think the signs point to the truth. Or are you all telling me an existence like Lord Cassius would show this much respect to someone if they weren’t worthy of it?

"From the history books, we know that the universe selected 13 powerhouses and blessed them, making them the Universe Guardians. However, out of the 13 of them, one stood out, and he was the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
"Legend speaks of him as an existence whose presence alone can shut down battlefields. He was respected by many and hated by billions.
"So tell me, if someone from the Primordial Era suddenly chooses to show respect to someone much weaker than them, what does that tell you?"
"This..."
Everyone turned and looked at Kent, who stood there, a smile on his face as he stared at the red cocoon holding the Blood Harvester, now showing cracks.
"It can’t actually be him... right?"
Old Matin smiled and brushed his beard. "He is a dragon, and he knows Lord Cassius. That alone is enough evidence to show he is the Primordial Chaos Dragon... at least his incarnation."

This time, many took Old Matin’s words seriously, and so they turned to face Kent. However, before they could ask a question, a powerful shockwave that caused everyone to turn pale came from the cocoon.
"BOOM"
Kent grinned and turned to look at Cassius, who, despite the weight of the universe crushing down on him, stood with a calm expression, his arms crossed over his chest as he stared back at Kent...
BOOM
Another shockwave came, this time forcing everyone to their knees. Kent placed his hand on Ruby’s shoulder to shield her from the pressure.
Thankfully, he wasn’t targeted, so aside from him, Ruby, the matriarch of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family and Cassius, everyone was being suppressed.
"Looks like she is coming out much stronger than before," Cassius said, and Kent nodded...
"It is only natural. Her sacrifice warrants more than even this." Kent smirked and then turned to the cocoon and spoke...
"No need to hide in there, Eliza. Come out so we can get things over with..." The grin on his face widened. "Of course, I don’t mind dragging you out if I have to."

"Tch." A chuckle came from the cocoon, followed by a crack and a sarcastic tone. "You are much weaker now, stepbrother. How can you then drag me out when I can literally kill you with a mere flick of my pinky?"
"We will never know until we try."

Kent’s words hadn’t even ended when, suddenly, the cocoon exploded, and a lady clad in crimson leather armor, her thighs practically exposed and her boobs barely contained in the armor, walked out, two long crimson braids hanging behind her.
In her hand, a glaive dripping with blood was held, practically begging to be used.
She stretched her slender body, causing both men and women to drool at the sight of her lustful body.
A grin formed on her face, making Kent pale.
"Well then, which blood should I harvest first..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1895: Blood Messengers
paragraphs: Kent turned pale simply because he clearly knew what followed when Eliza put on the smile she currently had on her face.
The last time he saw that smile was when she snatched the Blood Seal scroll and dove into the Blood Gate.
From the little memory he has of that life, he never forgets that smile.

Before coming to this planet, Kent received a quest that required him to save Eliza, who happened to be his stepsister and also one of the most dangerous female warriors to ever walk the face of the universe.
She was also the general of the Blood Hounds, a legion formed by the Blood Spear King.

Kent had yet to recall all his memories, but the quest gave him enough to know just when to be cautious. Right now, from the little he remembered, the smile on Eliza’s face said she was ready to kill.
Perhaps the elders of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family also sensed her killing intent, so their hands reached for their weapons, their battle modes activating automatically.
Kent knew he had to step in, so before she could charge at the nearest Blue Horn Tigerkin, he teleported and appeared before Eliza... "Hold back now, would you, stepsister?"

"Why should I stop?" Eliza complained. "Not only did a bastard from their family try to force himself on my sister, but they even had the audacity to chase me down, nearly killing my sister in the process. If anything, you should be helping me rid this universe of such filth."
She was angry, and Kent knew it. But he and Cassius were old friends, and since he had promised to speak on his behalf, he knew he had to keep his word.

"I know they have wronged you, Eliza, which, from where I stand, is unforgivable. In fact, I had recently given the order for an entire family like this to be slaughtered, and while I wasn’t the one who did it, it goes without saying the job was well done.
So, inasmuch as I would love to see blood flow, for my sake, spare them this once. I mean, their ancestor had literally descended to step in for them. He even brought this."
Kent presented the primordial-grade blood essence that Cassius had offered in exchange for the lives of his people.
Looking at the blood essence, Eliza furrowed her brow. "Oh, good stuff."
She reached forward and took the blood essence. Kent didn’t mind since it was offered to her. He merely held on to it for her.
That said, he would love to get his hands on something like that, as it would greatly help him. But he allowed his greed to settle for now.
"So what do you say, Eliza? Are they safe, or do I still have to convince you?"

Eliza stored the blood essence away and turned to look at Cassius... "I don’t know what kind of relationship you have with my stepbrother, but since he seems to like you, I will let today’s events slide."

She turned and looked at the matriarch of the Blue Horn Tigerkin Family. "However, by a year from now, I expect 100,000 Supreme-grade beast blood essences to be delivered to me right here. Failure to meet these demands will cause me to reach for my weapon."
She smirked. "Let’s just say nobody wishes to see me touch my weapon."
Cassius smiled and nodded. "Thanks for showing mercy, Blood Harvester." He looked at the matriarch and spoke, his tone dropping low... "Be sure to meet her demands before the one year is over."
"I will make sure it is handled, Ancestor," the matriarch spoke, her head lowered.
Eliza smirked and turned to look at Kent, who held a smile on his face. She deactivated her weapon and was about to walk toward him when a sudden explosion came from the sky...
"BOOOOOOM"

The explosion was so loud that even Kent flinched. However, before he could turn and look at where the explosion came from, a terrible pressure came from the clouds, causing everyone, Kent included, to drop to their knees.
He managed to land on his feet, but the pressure crashed down hard, causing his legs to buckle and almost all the blood to drain from his face.
"Wh-What is happening?" Ruby asked, struggling to lift her head.
Seeing this, Kent, against all odds, tapped into every last core he had, and using the power, he enveloped her and then, using the willpower he could muster, sent her straight into the tower.
The moment Ruby was gone, he crashed to his knees, blood coming from his nose. Then, as if he were the main target, a beam exploded from the sky, and in the blink of an eye, it arrived before Kent.
It was only when it was mere inches away that he saw it was a spear.
Kent had practically no energy to do anything.
The little energy he could harness was what he had used to send Ruby back into the tower. But even if he had any ounce of power, the spear contained so much power that he couldn’t have done anything.
Luckily for him, just before the spear could pierce his chest, a hand reached forward and grabbed it.
"Hmmmm."
Cassius hummed, his gaze narrowing toward the direction the spear came from.
He thought about throwing the spear back where it came from, but before he could, the spear turned to blood mist and vanished.
From the clouds, a large crack opened, making it feel like the heavens were coming down. Just as it opened, two large hands came from it, grabbed both sides, and pulled.
CRAAACKKKKK

The crack widened some more, increasing the pressure. By this point, Kent was at his limit. However, before he could lose consciousness, Cassius placed his hand on his shoulder, and almost as if the pressure wasn’t there, he felt okay.
He did the same for Eliza, who was faring much better than Kent.𝙧𝙚𝙚𝔀𝒆𝓫𝓷𝙤𝓿𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝙤𝓶
"Hahahahahaha..." From the large crack, laughter came. "After billions of years, we have finally returned."
Kent narrowed his eyes and was about to ask who dared invade the universe when a red flag bearing the insignia of two cracked skulls and a jaw came from the crack...
"Blood Messengers..." Kent and Eliza muttered, turning to look at each other.

chapters.title: Chapter 1896: Blood Challenge
paragraphs: A very long time ago, a crack like this appeared in the clouds, and from within came five people who called themselves Blood Messengers.
They came from the Blood Realm, or as they referred to it, the Nine Savage Heavens.

They came with a message: an invasion that later nearly swallowed the entire universe. Kent was there, from the little he could remember, and so was Blood Harvester, who could actually remember everything.
Right now, as she gazed at the nine people, each bearing the aura of a Primordial, appearing from the crack, her expression turned pale, for she knew what followed.
The nine people walked out, each holding a flag bearing the same insignia: two shattered skulls and a jaw in the middle.
After the last of them appeared, they turned their gazes toward Cassius, for he was the strongest so far, and they could sense that. However, instead of addressing him, they turned and faced Eliza...
"Looks like the reports were wrong. You are still alive, Blood Harvester," one of them, a baldy with a rather large belly, said, his dark eyes narrowing at Eliza.
"Looks like your reports were indeed wrong. After all, I still live and would probably be there when we slaughter your kind the next time we meet on the battlefield."
The big-bellied Blood Messenger laughed, not even angry at the provocative words said by Eliza...

"Indeed, you have the right to say those words. After all, when you faced the first five Savage Heavens, you managed to kill quite a number of them. But that was then, because now, there is no telling if you can withstand even a single blow from me or any of my comrades."
Eliza scanned the nine people, and indeed, she knew deep in her heart she could not fight any of them, even if she put everything she had into the battle.
Perhaps, if she were a Primordial, she would have had a chance to turn things around.
"But you have nothing to worry about since we didn’t come here to fight."
One of the nine Blood Messengers, a fella with crimson angel-like wings, stepped forward and produced a scroll. He bit the tip of his finger and let the blood drop onto the scroll.
It unfurled, and with it, a mysterious power unleashed a chilling aura that everyone felt deep in their bones...
[They are broadcasting to the entire universe,]

Tower said to Kent, who merely nodded but said nothing. He looked at the scroll that had now unfurled and sighed, knowing the universe was in danger and that the danger was now being broadcast to everyone, from the Celestial Realm to the Middle Worlds.
"People of the Infinity Universe, this is a combined message from the Nine Savage Heaven Monarchs. Several eras ago, we fought and lost to the warriors of this universe.

It was a disgrace to our kind, and that defeat has since plagued us. However, after eras of trying and failing, we have finally returned, and this time, we came with a challenge, one that will determine the fate of this universe and the Nine Savage Heavens.

100 years from today, the Blood & Death Arena will descend. When it does, it will appear in the realm boundary where, under the guidance of the Primordial Order, we will officially challenge the Infinity Universe to Ten Death Duels.
7 Pseudo-Primordials and 3 Primordials from both realms will fight to the death. After ten battles, the one with the highest number of wins will gain the authority to rule the loser.

This means that if the Nine Savage Heavens win, the Infinity Universe is ours to rule, and this will be enforced by the Primordial Order. This also means that if you win, we will forever become your servants.
That is all, and good luck, for you are going to need it."𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
The scroll closed and shot toward Eliza, who caught it...
"This scroll must be delivered to the one they call the Blood Spear King. He is to sign it with his blood and accept the call when the 100 years are up.
Until then, good luck, and may fortune smile on you."
With mocking smiles on their faces, they turned and walked back into the crack, vanishing from sight. Kent watched them leave, his fists clenched.
Everything that had just happened was clearly not normal.

He was happy to have his stepsister and one of the most capable warriors he had ever commanded back from the dead... literally, only for him to be disturbed by a challenge that he was sure had already sparked chaos on every cultivation planet in the universe.
’This is bad... really bad.’
The challenge will happen as planned, and aside from himself, he knew he had to find nine more who would represent the universe.
He knew that when the time came, the major powers in the universe would have no say. It would fall on the shoulders of the Blood Spear King.
He is that person, and inasmuch as he would love to push the responsibility onto someone else, the fate of the universe is at hand, so he cannot fail.
’Aside from me and Kaizo, I need 8 more who are willing to die for the universe.’
He has people, but at the same time, he didn’t want to pick any of them, except Kaizo, who he knew would not even allow him to back down from this fight.
There are the likes of Ruby, Eliza, Pandora, and many others, but can he really send them into battle when he has no idea what the Nine Savage Heavens have planned this time around?
For all he knew, this was merely a trap that, if he didn’t plan well, would swallow him and the universe in one gulp.
’Looks like the Blood Spear King has to return once again, and this time, he must finish what he started during the Blood Era.’
Kent turned to Cassius. "Thanks for the assist earlier on; however, it appears we have to part ways here, seeing as the universe is now on a ticking time bomb."
"It appears so. Until next time, then." Cassius dissolved into mist and vanished.
"Eliza, time to leave."

It was a disgrace to our kind, and that defeat has since plagued us.
However, after eras of trying and failing, we have finally returned, and this time, we came with a challenge, one that will determine the fate of this universe and the Nine Savage Heavens.
100 years from today, the Blood & Death Arena will descend.
When it does, it will appear in the realm boundary where, under the guidance of the Primordial Order, we will officially challenge the Infinity Universe to Ten Death Duels.
7 Pseudo-Primordials and 3 Primordials from both realms will fight to the death.
After ten battles, the one with the highest number of wins will gain the authority to rule the loser.
This means that if the Nine Savage Heavens win, the Infinity Universe is ours to rule, and this will be enforced by the Primordial Order.
This also means that if you win, we will forever become your servants.
That is all, and good luck, for you are going to need it."𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
The scroll closed and shot toward Eliza, who caught it...
"This scroll must be delivered to the one they call the Blood Spear King.
He is to sign it with his blood and accept the call when the 100 years are up.
Until then, good luck, and may fortune smile on you."
With mocking smiles on their faces, they turned and walked back into the crack, vanishing from sight.
Kent watched them leave, his fists clenched.
Everything that had just happened was clearly not normal.

He was happy to have his stepsister and one of the most capable warriors he had ever commanded back from the dead... literally, only for him to be disturbed by a challenge that he was sure had already sparked chaos on every cultivation planet in the universe.
’This is bad... really bad.’
The challenge will happen as planned, and aside from himself, he knew he had to find nine more who would represent the universe.
He knew that when the time came, the major powers in the universe would have no say.
It would fall on the shoulders of the Blood Spear King.
He is that person, and inasmuch as he would love to push the responsibility onto someone else, the fate of the universe is at hand, so he cannot fail.
’Aside from me and Kaizo, I need 8 more who are willing to die for the universe.’
He has people, but at the same time, he didn’t want to pick any of them, except Kaizo, who he knew would not even allow him to back down from this fight.
There are the likes of Ruby, Eliza, Pandora, and many others, but can he really send them into battle when he has no idea what the Nine Savage Heavens have planned this time around?
For all he knew, this was merely a trap that, if he didn’t plan well, would swallow him and the universe in one gulp.
’Looks like the Blood Spear King has to return once again, and this time, he must finish what he started during the Blood Era.’
Kent turned to Cassius.
"Thanks for the assist earlier on; however, it appears we have to part ways here, seeing as the universe is now on a ticking time bomb."
"It appears so.
Until next time, then." Cassius dissolved into mist and vanished.
"Eliza, time to leave."

chapters.title: Chapter 1897 Chaotic Moments (1)
paragraphs: Just as Kent had predicted, on almost every cultivation planet in the universe, there was chaos and mayhem everywhere.
The sudden broadcast by the blood messengers, while some took it as a prank, inadvertently opened the door for most people to do what they thought was right.
After all, there was a chance the universe would be coming to an end, so why not just let it burn to the ground now and be done with it?
Safe to say, in less than 5 minutes, billions had died.
In the grand scheme of things, that number was a small number compared to the total number of living beings in the universe.
Of course, some planets had fewer than half a billion living souls, so, in comparison to the lives lost, it could be treated as alarming.
As many were concerned, the Blood War never happened, for they had never heard of it until today.

chapters.title: Chapter 1898 Chaotic Moments (2)
paragraphs: A portal opened at the center of the room, and three people walked out—Kent, Ruby and Eliza, the Blood Harvester.
The moment they appeared, everyone went on high alert, some even pulling out their weapons.
"Who are you three, and how dare you invade this sacred hall?" Mythos shouted, the aura of a Primordial flaring. All 13, including the Celestial Supreme, did the same.
They are all Primordials.
However, despite their superior cultivation, none of the three people showed any sign of being suppressed. That was easily noticed by the 13 elders and the Celestial Supreme.
They sensed something wasn't right, especially with Kent, whose hair was now crimson, his eyes blood-red, and a wave of blood Qi emanating from his body.
He had taken on the appearance of the Blood Spear King, fully embodying everything there was about him.
Ruby and Eliza were Pseudo-Primordials, each possessing an aura that would make Primordials second-guess themselves.

However, as they looked at the three, Kent, whose cultivation base was a mystery, turned out to be the most dangerous one. They could all sense it; the aura coming from his body wasn't one they could underestimate.

chapters.title: Chapter 1899 First Three Selection
paragraphs: Kent had already made up his mind not to associate himself with the Universe Council, and he most certainly had no plans to interact with the Celestial Supreme in this life.
While the Celestial Supreme who betrayed him and a few others wasn't this one, he had learned a very long time ago that the Universe Council was one he could not trust.

In fact, all other major organizations, such as the Ice Council, the Elemental Council and even the Pill Council, could not be trusted. So, since that was the case, he knew he had to make sure they were all aware that he had no plans to rely on them.
They could choose not to rely on him, and he was fine with that.
After all, if they messed up, he could clean up their mess. But if he trusted them and they betrayed him, like how the twelve Sword Elders did during the Divine Era, then he might just lose his life.
In the end, it was up to whether or not Kent trusted them, and the answer was no, he didn't. So he made his stance clear, and as to whether they liked it or not, he didn't really care.
Right now, he knew he had to form a team of ten members, including himself, to face the challenge the Blood Savage Heavens had thrown at the Infinity Universe.

chapters.title: Chapter 1900 Ancient Primal Inheritance
paragraphs: It is safe to say that when it comes to life-or-death battles, there is no one better suited for them than the Mother of Killers.

Long before she became the legendary Spear Maid, Rakshasa, she was known as Shara, the Mother of Killers. She was among the thousands who entered the Trial of Death with nothing but a pair of short swords in hand.
After 700-plus kills, she emerged as the lone survivor, her killing intent forcing even Celestials to take a step back.

Many have won the Trial of Death, but none before or after her came out with that much aura. It was said that even Death feared her, for in her presence, unless she willed it, Death could not claim the souls she had killed.

Kent knew it had to be her, for he knew that unless she willed it, she could not die. Death would not even accept her because Death feared her, and Kent knew this because inside his soul, he had a literal embodiment of Death who was wary of Neomi.
This gave him the confidence to select Neomi, since she would be well-suited to handle what he had planned.
Kent patted her back and said, "No need to cry, Neomi. You are qualified to represent the universe in this challenge, so lift your head and accept your mission like the warrior you are."

Neomi lived during the Flame Era, when the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith reigned supreme. While they'd never met, Fjorge (Kent's Incarnation as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith) had heard a lot about the legendary Rakshasa back then.
